commits.pr_title: [MM] Support mm_device_do_normalize for Gemma 4 Unified
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Follow-up to #65577 (requested in its review): `mm_device_do_normalize` for Gemma 4 Unified (`Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration`, `google/gemma-4-12B-it`). #65577 has merged and this is rebased onto main, so it is one commit. No other PR covers this.

Like Gemma 4, Unified's processor only rescales by 1/255. With the flag on it sends raw `uint8` patches (4× fewer bytes) and the model rescales them on the device.

## Changes

- `Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration._normalize_pixel_values`: shared per-pixel (channel-last) normalization, used by `_embed_patches` and by Unified's `_embed_vision_patches`, which covers images and video.
- Unified builds the input norm and drops the opt-out from #65577. DiffusionGemma and EmbeddingGemma 2, which borrow Gemma 4's vision methods, also borrow the helper.
- `tests/models/registry.py`: `google/gemma-4-12B-it` is public, so it's no longer marked unavailable. Unified's processing tests now run in CI.
- New Unified `test_mm_device_do_normalize`.

## Validation

- RTX A6000, bf16, 6 llava-bench images: Unified with the flag on vs off gives identical greedy tokens, logprobs and prompt logprobs.
- `test_gemma4.py` + `test_gemma4_unified.py`: 82 passed, 1 skipped. pre-commit passed.
- **No PPL test entry:** `gemma-4-12B-it` lists `suppress_tokens` (`<image|>`, 258882, and 258883), and Gemma 4's `compute_logits` sets them to −inf at every position, so the harness reports an infinite PPL with the flag off too. That's a separate issue.
- Unified's encoder CUDA graph path predates this PR and isn't changed (it reads `vision_tower`, which is `None` for Unified).

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Quantization] Use fast SiLU intrinsics in Humming MoE activations
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Use fast SiLU math (`__fdividef` plus a flush-to-zero `ex2.approx.ftz.f32` exp) in the SiLU-family activation expressions that vLLM passes to Humming's `process_input`, the kernel that fuses the MoE w2 activation with input quantization. Humming compiles this kernel without fast math (`ProcessInputKernel.disable_fast_math = True`, added in vllm-project/humming#80), so SiLU currently compiles to a precise `expf` plus IEEE division. This change only affects the activation expression; Humming's quantization, Hadamard and scale math keep the precise flags.

## Claims

- Humming w2 activation+quant kernel is 16–30% faster at prefill sizes on B300, and up to ~40% for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's clamped SwiGLU (see tables).
- gpt-oss-20b end-to-end prefill throughput: +1.9% (MXFP8 activations) / +1.7% (FP8 per-token), n=3, spread ≤0.3%.
- Covers SILU / SILU_NO_MUL, clamped SiLU (SWIGLUOAI, SWIGLUOAI_UNINTERLEAVE), SITU and SWIGLUSTEP. GELU (`erff`) and `tanhf` are unchanged.
- No accuracy regression: GSM8K unchanged within noise; quantized outputs are bit-identical for MXFP4/MXFP8 and differ in ~1e-6 of bytes for FP8.

## Validation

**Kernel, first commit only (ncu, `--clock-control none`, B300, SiLU-and-mul input `rows x 2N` bf16, one launch per case):**

| case | precise (main) | fast (this PR) | vLLM reference kernel |
|---|---|---|---|
| bf16 out, N=2048, 65536 rows | 137.6 µs | 115.4 µs | `silu_and_mul` 132.0 µs |
| fp8 block-128, N=2048, 65536 rows | 156.5 µs | 118.4 µs | `silu_and_mul_per_block_quant` 682 µs |
| mxfp4, N=2048, 65536 rows | 153.2 µs | 115.5 µs | `silu_and_mul_mxfp4_experts_quant` 171.3 µs |
| mxfp4, N=768, 65536 rows | 63.7 µs | 48.6 µs | |
| any mode, N=2048, 512 rows (decode) | ~5.5–6.3 µs | ~5.5 µs | launch-latency bound, no change |

On main, at prefill sizes the kernel is instruction-issue bound (IPC ~3.5/4, issue slots 80–87% busy, DRAM 45–55% for quantized outputs); the SiLU math dominates the instruction count.

**FTZ exp2 (second commit):** without fast math, `__expf` keeps a denormal guard (an `FSETP` and two predicated `FMUL`s per element). `ex2.approx.ftz.f32` exists on every target; it is bit-identical here because `e^x` only underflows where SiLU(a) == a. CUPTI + CUDA graphs, cold L2, B300, `__expf` → FTZ: +4–10% at prefill sizes for quantized outputs (MXFP4, N=2048, 131072 rows: 232.6 → 215.0 µs), no change at decode sizes.

**DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash w2 shapes** (clamped SwiGLU, limit 10; block-FP8 activations as on Hopper; grouped-EP layout; CUPTI + CUDA graphs, cold L2, B300; main → this PR):

| N (parallelism) | 128 tok | 1024 tok | 8192 tok | 16384 tok |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2304 (EP) | 6.21 → 4.70 µs | 26.08 → 19.04 | 180.2 → 126.7 | 355.7 → 248.6 |
| 640 (TP4, padded) | 3.74 → 3.26 µs | 9.66 → 7.65 | 54.95 → 41.54 | 105.5 → 78.95 |

MXFP8 activations give the same picture.

**Hopper (H200, SM90)**, same harness (CUPTI + CUDA graphs, cold L2), Humming upstream main, default launch configs, main → this PR:

| shape | 128 tok | 1024 tok | 8192 tok | 16384 tok |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DSv4.1 N=2304 (EP), block FP8 | 5.95 → 4.86 µs | 27.23 → 21.95 | 195.8 → 147.6 | 386.2 → 289.6 |
| DSv4.1 N=1152 (TP2), block FP8 | 4.83 → 3.78 µs | 18.30 → 13.54 | 126.2 → 89.4 | 247.1 → 175.4 |
| DSv4.1 N=640 (TP4), block FP8 | 3.23 → 2.82 µs | 10.05 → 7.94 | 61.8 → 45.5 | 122.5 → 87.8 |
| DSv4.1 N=2304, FP8 per-token | 6.91 → 5.12 µs | 28.35 → 21.40 | 185.3 → 134.0 | 364.5 → 261.8 |
| gpt-oss N=2880 (SWIGLUOAI), FP8 per-token | 5.79 → 4.61 µs | 26.14 → 19.36 | 152.9 → 118.8 | 292.7 → 230.5 |

That is +15–41% across these shapes (up to +53% for N=1152 with FP8 per-token); activation-free input quant (w13) is unchanged, as expected.

**Accuracy (through the real Humming kernel):**

- Exhaustive sweep of all 65,280 finite bf16 gate values (up=1) vs an fp64 reference: fp32 output max relative error 3.3e-6 (precise: 1.8e-7) for a ≥ -80, worst in the a ∈ [-12, -6] tail where |SiLU| < 0.015. bf16 output differs from precise on 3 of 65,280 values.
- 8192x2048 inputs (normal, heavy-tailed with outlier channels, 1e-3 scale), fast vs precise: MXFP4 and MXFP8 values and E8M0 scales bit-identical; FP8 per-token / block-128: ~10 of 16.7M bytes differ, fp32 scales within 3.2e-7 relative, dequantized error vs exact SiLU·up identical to 7 significant digits.

**Tests:**

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/core/test_activation.py tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py -k humming
# 175 passed
```

`test_humming_activation_matches_framework` (already in CI via `tests/kernels/core`) compares each Humming activation against vLLM's reference in fp16/bf16/fp32 with edge and clamp values, at default tolerances.

**GSM8K** (existing Humming configs, 1319 questions, 5-shot, indexed Humming MoE GEMM, B300, main vs this PR side by side):

```bash
cd tests/evals/gsm8k && pytest -s test_gsm8k_correctness.py --config-list-file=configs/humming/<list>
```

| config | path | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8-block-humming` | SILU + fp8 g128 act | 0.850 | 0.876 |
| `gpt-oss-20b-humming-act-fp8` | clamped SiLU (SWIGLUOAI) | 0.307 | 0.315 |

Differences are within run-to-run noise.

**gpt-oss-20b** (TP1, Humming MoE, B300), main vs this PR:

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| GPQA (`tests/evals/gpt_oss`, low reasoning, MXFP8 act) | 0.569 | 0.579 |
| GSM8K (1319 q, 5-shot, MXFP8 act) | 0.299 | 0.292 |
| prefill throughput, MXFP8 act (tok/s, n=3) | 192,964 | 196,656 (+1.9%) |
| prefill throughput, FP8 per-token act (tok/s, n=3) | 201,974 | 205,406 (+1.7%) |

```bash
vllm bench throughput --model openai/gpt-oss-20b --moe-backend humming \
  --quantization-config.moe.activation mxfp8 --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 4096 --random-output-len 1 --num-prompts 512 --max-model-len 8192
```

The end-to-end gain is smaller than the kernel gain because this kernel is one part of each MoE layer.

## Details

- Why not enable fast math in Humming: `--use_fast_math` also implies FTZ, approximate division and approximate sqrt for the quantization/scale code, which vllm-project/humming#80 turned off on purpose. Requesting the intrinsics only in the activation string keeps that change local.
- `__fdividef` is a standard CUDA intrinsic; `ex2.approx.ftz.f32` is a single PTX instruction available on every target, not an arch-specific one.
- Edge cases: for very negative inputs `1 + exp(-a)` overflows and `__fdividef` returns 0, the correct SiLU limit; large positive inputs return `a`. The FTZ change was checked bit-exact against the `__expf` version for every changed activation over all finite bf16 gate values, in bf16 and fp32.
- Follow-up (not in this PR): Humming's `process_input` launch-config heuristic under-picks vector width (and uses multi-token blocks) on large grids on both SM90 and SM100. Fixing it upstream adds another ~1.4–1.9% end to end on gpt-oss-20b (B300) and 10–55% at the kernel level on H200 and B300; that change belongs in vllm-project/humming.
- No duplicate: the closest open PR is #59514, which changes vLLM's own `silu_and_mul_quant` CUDA kernel, not the Humming path.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Model] MiMo-V2 omni: label video grids with the sampled frames' media time
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fixes #65523. MiMo-V2 omni writes a timestamp before each 2-frame video grid in the prompt, but stamped the sampled frames 1 s apart. vLLM's video loader samples 32 frames across the whole clip by default, so every clip was labelled `00:00`–`00:30` whatever its length. This PR takes the frame times from the loader metadata (`frames_indices / fps`). Source change: +36/−5 in `mimo_v2_omni.py`.

Example: a 120 s video at 24 fps. The default loader picks 32 frames evenly across it, one every ~3.9 s. MiMo groups them in pairs into 16 grids and writes a `mm:ss` label before each grid in the prompt (`<label><|vision_start|><grid tokens><|vision_end|>`). The label should be the time of the grid's first frame in the video:

| Grid | Its first frame is at | Label on Baseline | Label After PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.0 s | `00:00` | `00:00` |
| 2 | 7.8 s | `00:02` | `00:07` |
| 3 | 15.5 s | `00:04` | `00:15` |
| … | … | … | … |
| 16 | 116.1 s | `00:30` | `01:56` |

On Baseline the model is told the whole 2-minute video lasts 30 s.

## Claims

- Prompt timestamps match the sampled frames' media time: at most 1 s off (labels are whole seconds) for every loader setting and input layout tested, versus up to 434 s off before.
- MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL answers timing questions correctly: "when does the screen turn red" 5/20 → 19/20, "how long is the video" 4/20 → 20/20 (Baseline answers `00:31` for every clip, 30 s to 8 min).
- Unchanged where there is no frame timing: text and image outputs are identical, inputs without metadata keep 1 s spacing, and prompt length and KV cache size are the same.
- No performance change: the processor's host time per video request is unchanged (16 ms), and serving throughput is within 2.5% at concurrency 1 and within the launch-to-launch variation at higher concurrency.

## Validation

Baseline is main `f8b116409c`; After PR is this PR on it.

**Affected models.** Every MiMo-V2 checkpoint with a `vision_config`, since those load as `MiMoV2OmniForCausalLM`: MiMo-V2.5, -V2.5-Base, -V2.6-Flash-RL, -V2.6-Flash-MOPD, -V2.6-Pro-RL, -V2.6-Pro-MOPD. Text-only MiMo-V2 checkpoints (V2-Flash, V2.5-Pro) and MiMo-V2.6-Distill-Qwen-9B (Qwen3.5 architecture) are not affected. The fix is in the processor and does not depend on weights. All six share the same video settings (1 fps, temporal patch 2; V2.5-Base has `max_frames` 1024 instead of 3600). With each checkpoint's own config and tokenizer, a 120 s clip ends at `00:30` on Baseline and at `01:56` After PR (true 116.1 s).

**Label accuracy across input layouts.** A video reaches the processor in several forms: as a URL decoded by vLLM's loader (with different frame-sampling settings and decoders), or offline as frames the user passes in (with or without the loader's metadata). For each form, we feed a real MP4 through the same loader (`MediaConnector`) and processor used in serving, read the 16 or so labels out of the resulting prompt, and compare each label with the actual time of the frame it labels. The table gives the largest difference over all labels of a video (0 is perfect; labels are whole seconds, so up to 1 s is rounding):

| How the video arrives | Largest label error, Baseline | Largest label error, After PR |
|---|---|---|
| default loader (32 frames), 0.5 s–480 s clips at 24 / 29.97 / 60 fps | 9.6–434.5 s | ≤ 0.92 s |
| `num_frames` 8 / 31 (odd, padded) / 64 / all | 32.6–405.4 s | ≤ 0.92 s |
| `fps: 2` | 58.6–118.1 s | ≤ 0.95 s |
| `fps: 1` | 0.92 s | 0.92 s (unchanged) |
| TorchCodec decode (CPU and CUDA), offline `(array or tensor, metadata)` | 86.1 s | 0.71 s |
| offline raw array or PIL frames (no timing) | 1 s spacing | 1 s spacing (unchanged) |
| prebuilt `(frames_TCHW, timestamps)` | given timestamps ignored | given timestamps used |

<details>
<summary>All 22 cases</summary>

| Input | Clip | Frames | Baseline max error | After PR max error |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| default | 120 s, 24 fps | 32 | 86.1 s | 0.71 s |
| default | 480 s, 24 fps | 32 | 434.5 s | 0.54 s |
| default | 120 s, 29.97 fps | 32 | 86.1 s | 0.71 s |
| default | 60 s, 60 fps | 32 | 28.0 s | 0.87 s |
| default | 1.5 s, 24 fps | 32 | 28.6 s | 0.92 s |
| default | 0.5 s, 24 fps | 12 | 9.6 s | 0.42 s |
| default | 75 min, 4 fps | 32 | 4,324.5 s | 4.5 s (see Details) |
| `num_frames: 64` | 120 s | 64 | 56.0 s | 0.88 s |
| `num_frames: 8` | 480 s | 8 | 405.4 s | 0.38 s |
| `num_frames: 31` | 120 s | 31 | 90.0 s | 0.04 s |
| `num_frames: -1` | 1.5 s | 36 | 32.6 s | 0.92 s |
| `fps: 2` | 60 s, 24 fps | 120 | 58.6 s | 0.42 s |
| `fps: 2` | 120 s, 29.97 fps | 239 | 118.1 s | 0.95 s |
| `fps: 1` | 120 s | 120 | 0.92 s | 0.92 s |
| TorchCodec, CPU | 120 s | 32 | 86.1 s | 0.71 s |
| TorchCodec, CUDA | 120 s | 32 | 86.1 s | 0.71 s |
| offline `(ndarray, metadata)` | 120 s | 32 | 86.1 s | 0.71 s |
| offline `(tensor, metadata)` | 120 s | 32 | 86.1 s | 0.71 s |
| offline raw ndarray | 120 s | 32 | 1 s spacing | 1 s spacing |
| offline list of PIL frames | 120 s | 32 | 1 s spacing | 1 s spacing |
| prebuilt `(frames_TCHW, timestamps)` | 120 s | 32 | 1 s spacing | given timestamps |
| same request twice | 120 s | 32 | 86.1 s | 0.71 s |

</details>

**Does the model answer timing questions correctly?** We generated 20 test videos with a known answer. Each is gray with a moving white square, and for a stretch the whole screen turns one solid color, e.g. a 2-minute video that turns red from 78 s to 93 s. Lengths are 30 s, 1, 2, 4 and 8 min; the color starts 15%, 40%, 65% or 85% of the way in. For each video we ask MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL two questions and check the answer against the truth:

- "At what time in the video does the whole screen turn red? Reply with only the timestamp in mm:ss format." (with the video's own color: red, blue, green or yellow) Counted correct if within one grid of the truth (video length / 16, e.g. 7.5 s for a 2-minute video).
- "How long is this video? Reply with only the duration in mm:ss format." Counted correct if within 1/8 of the length.

Example answers, Baseline → After PR: the 2-minute video turning red at 78 s, `00:21` → `01:17`; the 8-minute video's length, `00:31` → `07:59`.

Setup: FP8 checkpoint, TP4 on one GB200 node, requests via `video_url`, greedy, thinking off (`chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": false}`), `--mm-processor-cache-gb 0`. Number of correct answers out of 20 videos:

| Frame sampling (`media_io_kwargs` video settings) | Question | Baseline | After PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| default (32 frames) | when does the color change | 5/20, median error 35 s | 19/20, median error 2 s |
| default (32 frames) | how long is the video | 4/20 | 20/20 |
| `num_frames: 64` | when does the color change | 2/20, median error 37 s | 12/20, median error 7 s |
| `num_frames: 64` | how long is the video | 4/20 | 20/20 |
| `num_frames: 8` | when does the color change | 2/20, median error 45 s | 3/20, median error 36 s |
| `num_frames: 8` | how long is the video | 0/20 | 11/20 |
| `fps: 2` | when does the color change | 0/20, median error 72 s | 6/20, median error 12 s |
| `fps: 2` | how long is the video | 0/20 | 20/20 |

The default-loader scores are the same in all three launches of each build. Loader settings are set per request (`media_io_kwargs`, server started with `--trust-request-mm-kwargs`). After PR is better for every setting; the remaining misses on "when" are the model's limit, not the labels: With 8 frames one grid spans a quarter of the clip, so the event cannot be placed closely. With `fps: 2`, the long clips become 120–960 frames.

Baseline sees the color change at the right fraction of the video but reports the label it was given, so only the ~30 s videos come out right. With the default sampling, the one After PR miss is the 8-minute video turning red at 72 s, answered `01:33` (one grid is 30 s there).

Text-only (6 prompts) and image (3 prompts) outputs are identical between Baseline and After PR in two of the three launch pairs that ran them. In the third, the After PR launch differs from all other launches, including another launch of the same build (4/9 identical), so the difference is launch-to-launch, not the change. The KV cache is the same size (3,614,670 tokens), so memory profiling with dummy videos is unchanged.

**Performance.** The fix adds a few host-side operations per video and leaves the prompt length unchanged (labels stay `mm:ss`), so no change is expected. Two measurements:

- Processor host time per video request (parse, HF processing, prompt update; 120 s clip, 4 pinned cores, 300 calls, builds alternated three times): 15.95–16.25 ms After PR, 16.02–17.13 ms Baseline. The new `_video_timestamps` takes 1.9 µs per video; Baseline's `arange(T) / 1 fps` took 4.6 µs.
- Serving, MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL as above, streamed video requests (~1.4k prompt tokens, 64 output tokens, `ignore_eos`), each pair on one node:

| Pair | Concurrency 1, req/s (Baseline → After PR) | Concurrency 8, req/s (Baseline → After PR) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2.42 → 2.40 | 14.41 → 14.63 |
| 2 (After PR launched first) | 2.50 → 2.53 | 15.04 → 13.47 |
| 3 | 2.36 → 2.39 (two nodes) | 14.79 → 14.32 (two nodes) |
| 4 | 2.11 → 2.16 | 14.28 → 14.94 |

At concurrency 1 the builds are within 2.5%. At concurrency 8 and 32 this workload varies a lot between launches of the same build: two Baseline launches on one node gave 14.28 and 11.18 req/s at concurrency 8 (−22%) and 12.12 and 10.40 at 32 (−14%), so the After PR differences there (−10% to +23%) are within launch-to-launch variation.

**Tests.** `pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_mimo_v2_omni.py` (CPU, public `XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.5` config and tokenizer, no weights): 11 passed After PR. On Baseline, `test_labels_use_frame_media_time` fails for both the plain and the `MediaWithBytes` (serving) input (`second_per_grid_ts` 2.0, expected 16.0).

## Details

- **Root cause.** The data parser dropped the loader metadata (`video_needs_metadata` was off), so `_get_hf_mm_inputs` saw only frames and stamped them `arange(T) / 1 fps`. The HF processor derives the grid spacing (`second_per_grid_ts`) from those stamps, and `get_video_replacement` writes labels as `start + j * second_per_grid_ts`. Labels were right only when the loader happened to sample at exactly 1 fps.
- **Fix.** Enable `video_needs_metadata` in the MiMo data parser and stamp frames from `frames_indices / fps`, evenly spaced from the first to the last sampled frame. The loaders sample (nearly) uniformly, and the labels are arithmetic steps from the first two stamps, so even spacing keeps them consistent. Inputs without timing (raw arrays, PIL frames, metadata without `frames_indices` or `fps`) keep 1 s spacing instead of being rejected, and so does a clip whose first and last sampled frame are the same (for example a one-frame clip that a loader pads to two frames), which would otherwise give equal timestamps and a division by zero in the processor. Dummy profiling videos are raw arrays, so profiling is unchanged.
- **Not changed.** The `video_audio` conversion loop: the data parser has no `video_audio` modality, so serving never reaches it.
- **Remaining error on very long clips.** `second_per_grid_ts` is cast to bf16, so a 75 min clip's 290.3 s grid step becomes 290 s and the last label is 4.5 s early. #64477 fixes the same cast for Qwen2.5-VL.
- **Related work.** #65581 also targets #65523 but reads `frames_indices` / `fps` as attributes of the frame array, which never has them (the parser has dropped the metadata by then), so it always falls back to 1 fps. ziywang50 claimed the issue first and handed it over in the thread; the approach follows the diagnosis ngutten posted there.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Quantization] Index INT8 MoE per-channel weight scales independently of act quant - #58570
commits.pr_body:
**PR authors: @gokay-ai @ahsan-ca @fxmarty-amd - resubmitting https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58570 here with some minor fixes.** I lost ability to push to `https://github.com/gokay-ai/vllm.git` so landing here.

## Overview

Fixes #58532

`QuarkW8A8Int8MoEMethod` can load static per-tensor activation scales with per-output-channel weight scales. The legacy Triton `fused_experts` path still used `per_act_token_quant` to pick both layouts, so static activations (`per_act_token_quant=False`) also took the tensor weight-scale branch. Routed experts' channel scales were ignored.

This keeps the legacy static-INT8 path (no oracle migration) and splits the two flags:

- The non-block W8A8 Triton kernels (`fused_moe_kernel` and the batched `moe_mmk` kernels) index A scales with `per_act_token_quant` / `per_channel_quant` and W scales with a new `per_out_ch_quant` constexpr. `TritonExperts` and the batched Triton experts forward `quant_config.per_out_ch_quant`.
- `int8_w8a8_moe_quant_config` / `make_int8_moe_quant_config` now take `per_out_ch_quant`. Quark, compressed-tensors and online INT8 set it from the actual weight scheme.
- Quark INT8 (static and dynamic branches) derives `per_act_token_quant` from the activation `QuantKey` and `per_out_ch_quant` from the weight `QuantKey`, instead of deriving activation granularity from `weight_qscheme`.

No open PR already covers this combo. #57092 is the opposite mixed case (per-token acts + per-tensor weights) and is still open.

### Note on `per_out_ch_quant` defaults

`FusedMoEQuantConfig.make` and the `fp8` / `int8` / `int4` quant-config factories keep `per_out_ch_quant=False` as the default (unchanged from `main`). All in-tree production callers now pass it explicitly. `Fp8MoEMethod` passes `per_out_ch_quant=False`, which matters for per-token activations + per-tensor weights under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`.

**Behavior change for callers of the factories:** previously, setting `per_act_token_quant=True` alone made the Triton kernels index weight scales per channel. Now the weight-scale layout follows `per_out_ch_quant`, so callers with per-channel weight scales must pass `per_out_ch_quant=True`. The in-tree tests that relied on the implicit coupling were updated (`test_triton_moe_ptpc_fp8.py`, `test_int8_kernel.py`, `test_cpu_fused_moe.py`, `test_deepep_moe.py`, `test_deepep_v2_moe.py`). The direct Triton launchers (`invoke_fused_moe_triton_kernel`, `dispatch_fused_moe_kernel`, `fused_experts_impl`, `invoke_moe_batched_triton_kernel`) still default `per_out_ch_quant=None` to `per_channel_quant`.

This is a stopgap: as per #61024, `FusedMoEQuantConfig` should move to `QuantKey` and drop the `per_act_token_quant` / `per_out_ch_quant` flags.

The W8A16 path does not need the flag: the W8A16 kernels always index weight scales per output channel.

## Validation

Run on MI350X (gfx950), ROCm `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm` nightly image, at commit
9cd72c182ad74b20f19ebd90cd835c5beaec4d6f (branch head, `main` merged in,
working tree clean). The checkout was installed editable
(`pip install -e . --no-deps --no-build-isolation`); the compiled extensions were
built from this same source tree, and the only later change in the tree was the
`per_out_ch_quant` docstring.

New / modified tests:

```bash
pytest tests/quantization/test_quark.py -k int8
# 23 passed, 118 deselected, 14 warnings in 79.59s (0:01:19)

pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py -k launcher
# 3 passed, 1086 deselected, 17 warnings in 1.05s

pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_batched_moe.py tests/kernels/moe/test_zen_cpu_int8_moe.py
# 474 passed, 509 skipped, 14 warnings in 154.18s (0:02:34)

pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_triton_moe_ptpc_fp8.py tests/kernels/quantization/test_int8_kernel.py
# 76 passed, 16 warnings in 20.35s

pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_cpu_fused_moe.py -k int8
# 1 skipped, 14 warnings in 0.25s  (x86 CPU int8 kernel not available on this node)

pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_deepep_moe.py tests/kernels/moe/test_deepep_v2_moe.py
# 74 skipped, 18 warnings in 1.19s  (DeepEP not available on this node)
```

`test_quark_int8_static_per_channel_weight_scales` (GPU) perturbs per-channel scales of a routed vs an unrouted expert, for both `w13` and `w2`. It fails on `main` and passes here.

Possibly impacted tests (shared Triton MoE kernels / quant configs):

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py tests/kernels/moe/test_block_int8.py tests/kernels/moe/test_modular_kernel_combinations.py
# 858 passed, 382 skipped, 18 warnings in 272.95s (0:04:32)
```

No model eval: this is scale indexing, not a serving/accuracy algorithm change. `test_quark_int8_w8a8_moe` runs the `amd/tiny-qwen3-moe-w8a8-int8` end-to-end.

AI assistance was used to implement and write tests; a human should review the diff before merge.

commits.pr_title: [RL] Add configurable staging and parallel stage pulls to sharded RDT
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Add opt-in host receive staging and parallel owner-stream pulls to the existing
sharded-RDT weight-transfer backend. Defaults remain GPU staging and one stream
in flight.

This extends [#43375](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43375); it does
not replace the backend or alter the weight-reload API. Searches for open PRs
covering sharded-RDT host staging or parallel stage pulls found no duplicate.

## Claims

- `staging_device="host"` receives RDT objects into registered pinned memory
  and asynchronously scatters them to GPU layers. GPU staging remains the
  default.
- `stages_in_flight=N` pulls from up to N independent owner-connected streams,
  each with `num_rdt_buffers` receive slots. The default remains one stream.
- Sync-tagged free signals, bounded slot polling, quant-stream tensor lifetime,
  and transactional re-init preserve correctness under the added concurrency.
- The quant-stream commit also added `update_param_tp_status` to the
  sharded-RDT quant path, so the engine re-reconciles parameter TP state after
  `process_weights_after_loading` like upstream's reload path already did; this
  fixes replicated (`disable_tp`) weights on a subsequent reload through
  sharded RDT. Both paths now share one helper, `_process_loaded_layer` in
  `model_loader/reload/layerwise.py`, so they cannot drift again.
- Host-staging slots are page-locked with `cudaHostRegister` at their exact
  size (no pinned-allocator rounding or caching) and released on every drop
  path; a slot whose release cannot be proven safe is parked, never freed.

## Validation

Current-vLLM validation:

- Post-trim targeted suite on CPU: **28 passed, 3 CUDA-only skipped**:
  `test_sharded_rdt_engine.py`, `test_sharded_rdt_settings.py`, the host-scatter
  and quant-stream CUDA tests, the changed plan invariants, and the
  sync-tagged producer tests.
- Focused sharded-RDT suite on one H100, Ray 2.58, torch 2.13:
  **301 passed, 3 deselected, 0 failed**. The three pre-existing real-model
  bake cases need the repository-wide fixture and were not part of the focused
  harness.
- Four-H100 `examples/rl/rlhf_sharded_rdt_small_ep.py` run over real
  NIXL-UCX, once with GPU staging and once with pinned-host staging. In both
  modes sync 0 changed the generation and sync 1 reproduced it.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, and `git diff --check` pass.

Large-model end-to-end measurements from the pre-upstream implementation of
the same staging and scheduling behavior:

| workload | serialized | parallel | change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3-235B, PP8, two trainer nodes | 7.54 s | 3.86 s, host S=8 | -49% |
| Kimi-K2, published 48-node/four-replica shape | 7.53 s | 4.30 s, host S=8 | -43% |

The current-vLLM smoke validates the port and real GPU/host transport paths.
Its uniform ownership produces one stream, so current-vLLM S>1 coverage is a
targeted scheduler deadlock regression plus plan/pool invariant tests; the
large-model runs above provide the multi-stream performance evidence.

## Details

The existing consumer has one ordered K-deep pull window. Increasing K overlaps
chunks from that order but does not keep independent trainer PP stages active.
This change:

1. partitions the call plan by connected producer ownership;
2. gives each active stream a disjoint K-slot receive block;
3. schedules up to `stages_in_flight` streams while preserving per-owner order;
4. optionally allocates those slots in pinned host memory.

Receive memory is:
`effective_lanes * num_rdt_buffers * rounded_slot_size`. GPU slots remain
outside `gpu_memory_utilization`; host mode moves the receive pool to pinned
memory, but layer materialization still uses GPU memory. Host staging requires
Ray >=2.58; GPU staging retains the Ray >=2.56 floor.

Sync 0 remains one stream at depth one so registration completes before
concurrent transfer. Changes 3-4 from the broader POC (first-arrival packing
and dynamic share-group splitting) are deliberately out of scope.

---

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf] Skip DSA indexer scoring for short dense-MHA prefills
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

On ROCm, the `deepseek_v32` path (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.x) now skips the sparse indexer's Q projection and scoring for pure short prefills that run on dense MHA. CUDA already skips the scoring (#48407, #51298), and both now use the same check. Builds on the ROCm dense-MHA prefill from #49263.

## Claims

- GLM-5.1-FP8, MI355X, TP4: 1K-token prefill median TTFT -10.7% at c1, -5.0% at c32. On every call it changes, the attention output and KV caches are bit-identical to main. gsm8k unchanged; GPQA-Diamond 0.691 on both main and this PR (8 runs each).
- GLM-5.2-MXFP4 (indexer on 21 of 78 layers): no significant change (measured on the first revision).
- Mixed batches, prefills longer than `index_topk`, MTP layers, FULL cudagraph and capture still score. Other platforms are unchanged.

## Validation

- `test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py`: 36 passed, 8 skipped (7 need SM100, 1 needs the DeepSelect extension) on MI355X. `test_rocm_short_prefill_skips_indexer_q_and_scoring` drives `_fused_attention`: a short dense-MHA prefill runs neither `wq_b` nor the indexer, and `fused_norm_rope` still gets the indexer K cache. pre-commit clean.
- `test_rocm_fused_v32_dense_prefill_matches_mqa` (existing, AMD V1 Attention CI): passed, auto and fp8 KV. Its dense run skips one step whose keys a later 2049+-token decode scores.
- Serving, GLM-5.1-FP8, TP4, output 1 token, 2 runs per arm in order main, v1, PR, PR, v1, main (v1 = first revision, scoring skip only), no failed requests:

| workload | median TTFT (ms), main → v1 → PR | PR vs main |
|---|---|---|
| 1K in, c1 | 165.8 → 150.5 → 148.0 | -10.7% |
| 1K in, c32 | 1949.7 → 1919.0 → 1851.9 | -5.0% |

- gsm8k 5-shot strict / flexible, GLM-5.1-FP8: main 0.9462 / 0.9439, PR 0.9454 / 0.9439 (stderr 0.006).
- GPQA-Diamond (CoT zero-shot, chat template, temperature 0, 12288-token cap), GLM-5.1-FP8, 8 runs per arm, interleaved: main mean 0.691 (0.652-0.737), PR 0.691 (0.646-0.722), stderr 0.033 per run. 59-72 of 198 answers hit the cap in every run. lm_eval sends all 198 questions at once; a step logger showed that only the first prefill step (1-3 prompts) takes the skip, and the other prompts prefill in mixed batches, which run the same code as main. Batching matched across arms: in every logged run, one sparse-MHA prefill step took 60-62 prompts, 57 of them the same in all eight.
- Bitwise check: on every call this PR changes, a probe ran the main path twice and then the PR path on the same inputs, and compared the attention output and both KV caches (MLA and indexer). 13,416 calls on each of the 4 TP ranks (80 greedy requests at c1, the 1K c1 and c32 workloads, and a GPQA burst): all bit-identical, for main vs main and for main vs PR.
- v1 only: 1900 in c1 and 8K in c1 (sparse path) within noise. GLM-5.2-MXFP4, MTP3, 3 runs per arm: TTFT -0.6% to -1.9%, within noise; gsm8k strict 0.9356 → 0.9356, acceptance length 3.31 → 3.31.

<details>
<summary>Per-run numbers, probes, profile and reproduction</summary>

Image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly` (AITER 0.1.25) running main at 7f730b4 and this branch from source, MI355X.

GLM-5.1-FP8 (78 indexer layers, no spec decode), median TTFT in ms:

| run | arm | 1K c1 | 1K c32 | 1K c32 total tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | main | 164.8 | 1949.2 | 16755 |
| E2 | v1 | 152.0 | 1920.0 | 17032 |
| E3 | PR | 148.0 | 1851.2 | 17643 |
| E4 | PR | 148.1 | 1852.6 | 17636 |
| E5 | v1 | 148.9 | 1918.1 | 17037 |
| E6 | main | 166.8 | 1950.3 | 16748 |

GPQA-Diamond runs in order: PR 0.697, main 0.737, main 0.712, PR 0.646, main 0.712, PR 0.687, PR 0.692, main 0.697, then with the step logger main 0.677, PR 0.722, PR 0.692, main 0.682, main 0.652, PR 0.687, PR 0.702, main 0.662. The first eight favor main by 3.4 points and the next eight favor the PR by 3.3. Main is not run-to-run deterministic on this model even at c1: the same 40 greedy requests sent twice to one main server give bit-identical prompt logprobs for 0.3% of values (mean |d| 0.21 nats); main vs PR shows the same 0.21.

A probe on TP rank 0 counted eager indexer-layer calls over the same workloads. On pure dense-MHA prefills, v1 ran `wq_b` and the indexer part of `fused_q` in 7098 of 7098 calls and scored in none; this PR ran none of the three in 7176 calls, and `fused_norm_rope` wrote the indexer K cache in all 7176. Mixed batches (156 calls) and decode (4368) ran all three in both arms.

First revision (v1) against main, earlier sessions:

| run | arm | 1K c1 | 1900 c1 | 1K c32 | 8K c1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | main | 166.5 | 175.8 | 1950.1 | 622.9 |
| F2 | v1 | 149.2 | 174.6 | 1916.9 | 623.1 |
| F3 | v1 | 153.1 | 172.7 | 1919.1 | 623.6 |
| F4 | main | 162.5 | 175.4 | 1947.0 | 617.4 |

v1 gsm8k strict / flexible: main 0.9469 / 0.9462 and 0.9424 / 0.9409, v1 0.9447 / 0.9439 and 0.9462 / 0.9484.

GLM-5.2-MXFP4 (21 indexer layers plus the MTP layer; TTFT runs use MTP3 with synthetic acceptance 3.0), median TTFT in ms, runs in order A B B A A B:

| arm | 1K c1 | 1900 c1 | 1K c32 | 8K c1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 152.4 / 154.3 / 152.8 | 148.9 / 150.3 / 152.2 | 1501.8 / 1503.7 / 1513.2 | 471.6 / 475.7 / 473.0 |
| v1 | 152.0 / 150.6 / 154.1 | 145.7 / 147.4 / 149.5 | 1489.8 / 1492.2 / 1492.2 | 471.8 / 470.5 / 457.9 |

GLM-5.2 gsm8k with real MTP3: strict 0.9356 → 0.9356, flexible 0.9356 → 0.9363, acceptance length 3.310 → 3.311. At concurrency 1 (250 questions, every prefill a pure short prefill): 0.952 → 0.944 (stderr 0.014). A probe on TP rank 0 counted indexer-layer calls on pure dense-MHA prefills: main scored 8382 of 8382, v1 382 of 8404, all on the MTP layer.

Why 1K gains more than 1900 in v1 (GLM-5.1-FP8, TP rank 0). Prefill runs eagerly, and on main the host needs about 148 ms to issue a step at either length. A probe timed the forward without a profiler (median of 20, ms). Host times move by up to 10 ms between sessions with node load; a first main session under heavy load (1K host issue 187 ms) was repeated:

| arm | 1K: host issue / GPU tail after it | 1900: host issue / GPU tail after it |
|---|---|---|
| main | 147.6 / 4.4 | 149.8 / 12.3 |
| v1, run 1 | 131.3 / 6.9 | 131.1 / 27.6 |
| v1, run 2 | 142.0 / 0.4 | 143.4 / 15.3 |

At 1K the GPU finishes within a few ms of the last launch, so the step is host-bound and the indexer's host work shows up in TTFT. At 1900 the GPU runs 12-28 ms past the host; host + tail stays at 159-162 ms in every run, and only the indexer's GPU time is saved. A torch profiler trace per step: v1 removes 312 kernels (4 per layer), 1.43 ms of GPU time at 1K and 2.17 ms at 1900; on main the indexer op costs 190-198 us of host time but 24-34 us of GPU time per call (host time inflated by the profiler).

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MLA=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_RMSNORM=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP8BMM=0 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4BMM=0 \
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8 --tensor-parallel-size 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --max-model-len 16384 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9
# GLM-5.2: amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4, same flags plus
#   --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'

# 1K c1 shown. 1900 c1: --random-input-len 1900 --seed 45.
# 1K c32: --num-prompts 512 --max-concurrency 32 --seed 46.
# 8K c1: --random-input-len 8192 --num-prompts 16 --seed 47.
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8 --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1 --temperature 0 \
  --num-prompts 40 --max-concurrency 1 --seed 44

lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size 1 \
  --model_args model=zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=64,tokenized_requests=False
lm_eval --model local-chat-completions --tasks gpqa_diamond_cot_zeroshot --apply_chat_template \
  --model_args "model=zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=198,tokenized_requests=False,think_end_token=</think>" \
  --gen_kwargs max_gen_toks=12288

VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 pytest -v tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py \
  "tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py::test_rocm_fused_v32_dense_prefill_matches_mqa"
```

</details>

## Details

- Placement: `DeepseekV32MLAAttention._fused_attention`, which already holds the MLA metadata. CUDA passes the layer name into its op only because the op cannot see that metadata.
- Conditions: `should_skip_indexer_scoring()` in `sparse_attn_indexer.py`, which the CUDA op now also calls, plus the layer taking the dense-MHA branch. The flag in `DeepseekV32Attention` moves from `is_cuda()` to `is_cuda_alike()`.
- K cache: still written by `fused_norm_rope`. The indexer Q projection (`wq_b`), the indexer part of `fused_q` and scoring are dropped.
- The gain at c1 is host time: an eager 1K prefill is host-bound and each indexer call costs about 0.2 ms on the host. Dropping `wq_b` (a 2048 → 32x128 GEMM per layer) also saves GPU time, which shows at c32.
- CI: `vllm/models/deepseek_v32` is added to the source dependencies of the MI300 Model Executor step in `test-amd.yaml`, so that changes there run this test file. `test_areas/model_executor.yaml` has it since #59223.
- Not measured: DeepSeek-V3.2 (same code path), GLM-5.1 with MTP, TP8.

<details>
<summary>Design notes</summary>

- Moving the check into `rocm_aiter_sparse_attn_indexer` would mirror CUDA but add an argument to an op that DeepSeek-V4 shares; the model already has the MLA metadata and the dense-MHA decision.
- The ROCm indexer op is built with `skip_k_cache_insert=True`. `fused_norm_rope` writes the indexer keys and clears the top-k buffer before the decision.
- PCP leaves the flag off, as on CUDA; ROCm sparse MLA rejects DCP. MTP layers keep scoring, as on CUDA.
- This model is not torch.compiled. Prefills run eagerly under the default FULL_DECODE_ONLY; under breakable cudagraphs the eager segment re-evaluates the decision on replay. Profile and dummy runs (no metadata) still call the op, so its workspace is reserved.

</details>

Not a duplicate: no open or closed PR skips indexer scoring on ROCm.

<details>
<summary>Duplicate search</summary>

`gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state all --search` with "short prefill indexer ROCm", "skip indexer ROCm", "indexer scoring ROCm", "dense mha indexer ROCm", "short prefill topk ROCm", "rocm_aiter_sparse_attn_indexer", "dense_mha_metadata_layer_name", "short prefill skip indexer", "GLM ROCm indexer prefill", "ROCm DSv3.2 indexer". Nearest: #56944 and #60601 (shard indexer prefill rows across TP), #61504 (sparse MLA decode indptr), #60294 (aiter `mqa_logits` for indexer prefill); none skips scoring.

</details>

AI assistance (Claude) was used for the implementation, the measurements and this description.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Accept media_io_kwargs video fps over gRPC
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`media_io_kwargs` is the per-request field that tells vLLM how to load media: `{"video": {"fps": 1}}` samples one video frame per second. The Rust frontend's gRPC `GenerateRequest` has no such field, so a gRPC client cannot change the frame rate. This PR adds it as field 19 and applies `video.fps`, which the Rust media loader already supports per video. Any other option returns `INVALID_ARGUMENT` instead of being ignored. Part of #65841 (sub-item 2).

```python
kwargs = struct_pb2.Struct()
kwargs.update({"video": {"fps": 1}})
stub.Generate(pb.GenerateRequest(..., media=[video_item], media_io_kwargs=kwargs))
```

## Claims

- Each video `url` or `data_uri` part is sampled at `video.fps` frames per second.
- A client `uuid` is scoped by the rate (`<uuid>@fps=<fps>`), as in Python, so two rates never share an encoder-cache entry.
- `INVALID_ARGUMENT` for other keys, an fps that is not a number in [0.2, 5] (a null fps reads as omitted), raw-bytes video, preprocessed features, and models that sample a fixed frame count (Gemma 4, Nemotron Omni).
- `vllm-proto` 0.6.0 to 0.7.0. A 0.6 server ignores field 19, so clients check `ServerInfo.proto_version`.

## Validation

Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct, `vllm-rs` v0.33.0 with this diff, one 60 s clip:

| Request | Prompt tokens |
|---|---|
| no `media_io_kwargs` | 5347 |
| `{"video": {"fps": 1}}` | 2682 (Python OpenAI server, `--trust-request-mm-kwargs`: 2682) |
| `{"video": {"num_frames": 8}}` | `INVALID_ARGUMENT` |
| same `uuid`, fps 1, 2, 1 | 2682, 5347, 2682 (without the uuid scoping: OK, `INTERNAL`, OK) |

- `cargo test -p vllm-server --lib grpc`: 77 passed
- `cargo test -p vllm-chat --lib multimodal`: 113 passed
- `cargo clippy -p vllm-server -p vllm-chat -p vllm-proto --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo publish --manifest-path rust/proto/Cargo.toml --locked --dry-run`

## Details

- **No trust flag on gRPC.** `docs/usage/security.md` limits the gRPC port to trusted callers, and fps stays in [0.2, 5] under the frame cap. The doc now says so.
- **Only `video.fps`.** The Rust loader has no per-request frame count, so `num_frames` and `max_frames` are rejected, not ignored.
- **Fixed frame count models reject fps.** Their Rust sampler ignores the rate (Python's loader applies it), so fps would do nothing.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Preserve confirmed junction after lookup retry
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Preserve a confirmed full-attention junction when offload lookup convergence excludes an in-flight chunk. Related to #63565 and its fix #63566.

## Claims

- A deferred full-attention lookup can become confirmed after a sparse group shortens the lookup range, even when the pending chunk itself remains pending. Record the confirmed boundary if a later sparse group shortens the hit again.
- Never record a junction from a full-attention group that has not been confirmed, even if another group has reset the convergence loop's deferred flag.
- This changes junction retention, not the converged hit length or the manager's lookup semantics.

## Validation

- Real `CPUOffloadingManager`, real requests and scheduler: both new regression tests fail on the base revision and pass with the fix. The first returns a 16-token hit and changes the junction from 0 to 32; the second prevents an unconfirmed 16-token junction.
- Full `test_scheduler.py`: **507 passed**, 15 warnings. The worktree lacked compiled extensions, so the run used the configured venv and a temporary Python bootstrap that loaded the existing extensions from another checkout. The actual command was `$VENV/bin/python /tmp/vllm-junction-investigation/pytest_boot.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py -q --disable-warnings --maxfail=2`.
- `pre-commit run --files tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py`: passed.
- End-to-end, Qwen3.5-0.8B-text-only BF16 on one H100 MIG 10 GiB with native CPU offload: real producer requests populated CPU caches; lookup responses were selectively demoted to reproduce the interleaving while using real cached data. The original and fixed scheduler each loaded 576 tokens and generated the same next token (264); the original recorded junction 0 and the fix recorded 1152. This is a controlled single-prompt correctness check, not an accuracy benchmark or a performance measurement.
- Four rounds of natural shared-prefix and eviction traffic on that model produced 195 hits and 41 misses, but did not encounter a pending full-attention lookup. Natural occurrence and workload frequency remain unverified; no speedup is claimed.

## Details

The old code writes 0 when full-attention lookup is deferred, then only captures the boundary while the field is `None`. A sparse group can narrow the candidate and trigger a full recheck that no longer includes the pending key; a second sparse constraint can then narrow the final hit. The original 0 masks the confirmed boundary. Also, the shared defer flag can be reset by another full-attention group before the first sparse lookup; track the per-iteration full-attention confirmation separately to avoid registering an unconfirmed boundary.

Duplicate check: #63566 covers stable lookup, while open #62278 and #62400 address junction representation / MooncakeStore and do not update this deferred-convergence logic. Searches for offload junction / pending / lookup found no open PR addressing this path. The boundary representation will need a rebase if #62278 lands first.

AI assistance (OpenAI Codex) was used to investigate, implement and test this change and draft this description. The human submitter confirmed reviewing the changes and running the relevant tests.

commits.pr_title: [CI/Build] Move the default CUDA build from 13.0 to 13.2
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`requirements/cuda.txt` already pins `torch==2.13.0`, and PyTorch publishes cu132 wheels for that release. This moves the default vLLM build from CUDA 13.0 to CUDA 13.2 so the shipped wheels match the CUDA version the pinned torch is built against.

## Changes

- `CUDA_VERSION` `13.0.3` → `13.2.1` in `docker/Dockerfile` (plus the regenerated `docker/versions.json`), `.buildkite/release-pipeline.yaml`, the arm64 / GH200 image builds, and the torch-nightly image build.
- Build base images → `pytorch/manylinux2_28-builder:cuda13.2-9f3983c9d6...` and `pytorch/manylinuxaarch64-builder:cuda13.2-9f3983c9d6...` (same pinned commit for both arches).
- `VLLM_MAIN_CUDA_VERSION` `13.0` → `13.2` and the `setup.py` variant map `cu130` → `cu132`, so precompiled-wheel autodetection and the nightly-index default agree with what is actually built.
- `--torch-backend cu130` → cu132 for `check-ray-compatibility.sh`; `DEFAULT_VARIANT_ALIAS` → `cu132`.
- Regenerated `requirements/test/cuda.txt` against the cu132 index.
- Docs updated.

### Verified available before pinning

| Artifact | Status |
| --- | --- |
| `torch==2.13.0+cu132` | ✅ |
| `torchvision==0.28.0+cu132` | ✅ |
| `torchcodec+cu132` | ✅ |
| `pytorch/manylinux2_28-builder:cuda13.2-9f3983c9d6...` | ✅ |
| `pytorch/manylinuxaarch64-builder:cuda13.2-9f3983c9d6...` | ✅ |
| `nvidia/cuda:13.2.1-base-ubuntu24.04` / `-ubuntu22.04` | ✅ |

## Two upstream gaps worked around here

**1. FlashInfer has no cu132 index.** `https://flashinfer.ai/whl/` publishes `cu128`, `cu129`, `cu130` and `cu134` — `cu132` 404s, which would break the `flashinfer-jit-cache` step outright. CUDA minor version compatibility makes the cu130 build usable on a 13.2 runtime, so the Dockerfile now maps `cu131|cu132|cu133` → `cu130`. Happy to drop this in favour of asking FlashInfer to publish a cu132 index if maintainers prefer.

**2. `--torch-backend cu132` is unusable for the test lock.** It restricts every torch-ecosystem package to the cu132 index, and `torchaudio==2.11.0` has no cu132 build — torchaudio is no longer released and its last build predates cu132, so the cu132 index tops out at torchaudio 2.2.0:

```
× No solution found when resolving dependencies:
╰─▶ Because there is no version of torchaudio==2.11.0 and you require
    torchaudio==2.11.0, we can conclude that your requirements are unsatisfiable.
```

torchaudio is imported at module scope by several model processors (`midashenglm`, `cohere_asr`, `funasr`, `minicpmo`), so it cannot simply be dropped. The `pip-compile` hook therefore uses `--extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu132` instead of `--torch-backend`; `unsafe-best-match` still prefers the `+cu132` local versions for torch/torchvision/torchcodec, and torchaudio resolves to its PyPI wheel (`torchaudio==2.11.0`, no local version).

Side effect: uv does not echo `--extra-index-url` into the lock header, so the header no longer records which CUDA index was used. `.pre-commit-config.yaml` is the source of truth.

## Notes for reviewers

- **Lock churn.** `requirements/test/cuda.txt` shows ~677 changed lines, but only ~32 of those come from cu130 → cu132. The rest is ordinary staleness — recompiling with the *same* `--torch-backend cu130` today produces ~649 changed lines on its own.
- **`torchao` in `.buildkite/test_areas/quantization.yaml` is deliberately left on the cu130 index.** `torchao==0.17.0` has no cu132 build (the cu132 index only carries 0.18.0). Bumping torchao is out of scope; the cu130 build runs fine on a 13.2 runtime. Worth a follow-up.
- `--torch-backend=cu132` requires uv ≥ 0.12.0. This PR does not need it (the pre-commit `uv` rev stays at 0.11.1), but the install docs now suggest `cu132` to users, and the surrounding text already tells them to `uv self update` if it fails.

## Test Plan

Full CI. The docker build is the real test here — it exercises the CUDA 13.2 base image, the FlashInfer cu130 fallback, and the regenerated lock.

Locally verified: `docker/versions.json` regenerates clean from the Dockerfile ARGs, all touched YAML parses, and the cu132 lock resolves end to end.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Don't reopen reasoning after the prompt closed it
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

On the Rust frontend, structured outputs are not enforced when the chat template closes reasoning in the prompt, for example Qwen3 with `enable_thinking: false`. The output grammar still offers a new reasoning block, the model opens one, and `content` comes back as `<think>...` text instead of the requested JSON. This PR makes the grammar start at the visible output in that case, as the Python frontend does.

## Claims

- For reasoning parsers built on `DelimitedReasoningParser`, a prompt whose last reasoning boundary is the end marker now gets only its unconsumed separator followed by the visible-output grammar, without the optional reasoning block.
- With thinking disabled, Rust frontend responses now satisfy `response_format` / `structured_outputs` and are identical to the Python frontend's on Qwen3-0.6B and Qwen3-8B.
- Prompts that open reasoning or have no reasoning boundary (thinking enabled) are unchanged: output is byte-identical to before.

## Validation

H100 MIG 1g.24gb, driver 580.105.08, torch 2.14.0+cu132. "Before" and "after" are local release builds of `vllm-rs` without and with this change; their `rust/` is identical to this PR's base `7a90549f7e`. Rust unit tests ran on macOS.

**Repro** (served with `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --reasoning-parser qwen3`, plus `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.8` for the MIG slice):

```bash
curl -s localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Describe a cat."}],
  "max_tokens": 200, "temperature": 0,
  "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": false},
  "response_format": {"type": "json_schema", "json_schema": {"name": "animal", "schema": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {"name": {"type": "string"}, "legs": {"type": "integer"}},
    "required": ["name", "legs"]}}}
}'
```

| | finish_reason | content |
|---|---|---|
| Python frontend | `stop` | `{ "name": "A Cat", "legs": 4 }` |
| Rust, before | `length` | `<think>\nOkay, I need to describe a cat. Let me start by thinking about what makes a cat unique...` |
| Rust, after | `stop` | `{ "name": "A Cat", "legs": 4 }` |

**Constraint validity with thinking disabled** (greedy, streaming and non-streaming; 5 prompts on 0.6B, 10 on 8B; servers also had `--enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser hermes --seed 0`; valid = content parses and matches the constraint):

| Model | Constraint | Python | Rust before | Rust after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-0.6B | `json_schema` | 10/10 | 4/10 | 10/10 |
| Qwen3-0.6B | `json_object` | 10/10 | 4/10 | 10/10 |
| Qwen3-0.6B | `choice` | 10/10 | 6/10 | 10/10 |
| Qwen3-8B | `json_schema` | 20/20 | 10/20 | 20/20 |
| Qwen3-8B | `json_object` | 14/20 | 8/20 | 14/20 |
| Qwen3-8B | `choice` | 20/20 | 6/20 | 20/20 |

The Python `json_object` misses on 8B are long answers cut off at `max_tokens=200`. A `regex` constraint gave the same counts on all three (6/10 and 4/20; the model repeats digits until `max_tokens`).

- Thinking disabled: Rust-after content equals Python's in 40/40 requests on 0.6B and 80/80 on 8B (four constraint types).
- Thinking enabled: Rust-after output (content and reasoning) equals Rust-before in 40/40 requests on 0.6B and 10/10 on 8B.
- A 121-request differential suite (completions, chat, tools, logprobs, errors) differs between before and after only in the `json_schema` case, plus random request ids in two error messages.

**Tests**

```
# new e2e test, test_completion_with_function_calling.py (runs in the Rust Frontend Tool Use step)
pytest ... -k test_response_format_with_thinking_disabled
  Python frontend      -> 2 passed
  Rust, before         -> 2 failed (JSONDecodeError; content '<think>\nOkay, I need to describe a cat...')
  Rust, after          -> 2 passed
pytest test_completion_with_function_calling.py -k "not test_no_args_tool_call"   (Rust, after) -> 30 passed

# rust/
cargo test -p vllm-parser                -> 627 passed (both prompt_closed_reasoning_* tests fail on main)
cargo fmt --all -- --check               -> clean
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings -> clean
```

<details>
<summary>Local environment notes</summary>

`cargo test -p vllm-chat -p vllm-server` passes except for tests that fail here regardless of this change: `roundtrip_{qwen3,mimo_v26,kimi_k25,step5}` fail identically on main (local HF files: the Step-5 config has no `vocab_size`, and the Qwen3 fixture differs only in `all_stop_token_ids`); `audio_pipeline_attributes_stage_timings_to_request` and `chat_completions_n_returns_one_choice_per_seeded_sample` failed once in the full parallel run and pass when run alone.

</details>

No model eval: logits and sampling are untouched. Only the grammar sent for structured-output requests whose prompt closed reasoning changes, which the results above cover.

## Details

**Root cause.** `DelimitedReasoningParser::wrap_visible_format` (added in #57340) treats two different prompt states the same way: no reasoning boundary in the prompt, and a prompt that already closed reasoning. Both get `optional(<think> ... </think>)` in front of the visible grammar. With thinking disabled, Qwen3's template renders `<think>\n\n</think>\n\n`, and the model takes the optional block. It spells `<think>` with ordinary tokens (27, 26865, 397), so the output parser, which matches markers by token identity, keeps the block in `content`. The Python frontend checks the prompt in `resolve_reasoning_ended` and applies the plain grammar from the first token.

**Change.**
- `delimited.rs`: record whether the prompt's last boundary is the end marker, and in that case return the unconsumed separator plus the visible grammar. The removed `pending_after` branch was only reachable in that case.
- `prompt_closed_reasoning_keeps_only_unconsumed_separator` and HY3's `grammar_root_follows_prompt_reasoning_state` pinned the optional block for a closed prompt and now expect the visible grammar. A new test covers Qwen3, DeepSeek V3, GLM-4.5 and Nemotron V3 with their thinking-disabled prompt endings.

This affects `qwen3`, `deepseek_r1`, `deepseek_v3`, `glm45`, `hy`, `step3p5` and the parsers aliased to them (MiniMax M2, Step3, DeepSeek V4/V4.1, GLM-4.7/5, Kimi K2, MiMo, Nemotron V3).

**Relation to other PRs.** I found no issue or PR for this. #65397 and #60815 (both drafts) edit the same files but do not change the closed-prompt case.

**Limitations.** Real-checkpoint runs used Qwen3 only; the other families are covered by the unit tests. Not run on ROCm.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Prebuild mamba-ssm and causal-conv1d from pinned commits in a torch-keyed test-image stage
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Trunk change: needs line-by-line review. It changes the CUDA test image every CI job uses and the commands of three test steps.

Three NVIDIA jobs, `Language Models (Hybrid)`, `Granite Language Model Compatibility` and `Language Models (Extended Generation)`, compile `mamba-ssm` and `causal-conv1d` from source before pytest on every run. This PR builds them once in the test image instead, so the jobs only verify them. It takes over @khluu's #52333; his three commits are kept with authorship.

The earlier revision of this PR built them at the end of `test-deps`. That layer reruns whenever any test or runtime requirement changes: 31 commits on `main` in the last 30 days. Each of those reruns would also have redone the ~14-minute extension build, delaying every job in that CI build. This revision keys the build on the torch versions only; they changed once in the same 30 days.

## Claims

- The three jobs run the verifier and pytest, with no source builds.
- The extensions rebuild only when the torch, torchvision or torchaudio version (the stage copies all three from `base`; they change together), the pinned commits, the build-tool list, the build script, the toolchain stage or a build argument such as `max_jobs` changes. A requirements-only change leaves them cached.
- Both are fetched by commit SHA (`mamba` v2.3.0 = `f1493ff6`, `causal-conv1d` v1.6.0 = `da6dbaa9`), not by tag.
- The four CUDA image steps that bind-mounted all of `requirements/` now mount only the files they read (`rubin-prerelease.txt`, `kv_connectors.txt`, `kv_connectors_cu12.txt`). A change to any other requirements file no longer reruns `base`'s torch install or the vLLM CUDA compile after it. This commit is @khluu's mount change from #64719, split out at his suggestion; the ancestor-cache lookup stays in #64719.
- Nothing they declare as a dependency is installed. Their runtime dependencies come only from the hash-pinned `requirements/test/cuda.txt`, and their build tools from a new hash-pinned list.

## Validation

- `tests/tools/test_dependency_pins.py`: 9 new tests pass. They check that the verifier and the build script pin the same commits, that every build tool has a hash, and the verifier's pass and fail paths. A mutation run on the verifier leaves no surviving mutants.
- `pre-commit run` on the changed files passes, including mypy, the Dockerfile graph and `docker/versions.json`. `docker build --check` reports no new findings beyond one known false positive for a repeated `ARG`.
- CI:
  - [x] [#99812](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/99812) (`/ci run`, cold): `hybrid-test-wheels` built in about 6 minutes, compiling only sm_80 and sm_90, alongside the vLLM CUDA compile, which took longer, so it did not delay any test. Hybrid (both shards) and Granite passed; each verifier line shows both commits, and no test logged transformers' "falling back to its reference PyTorch implementation" warning for these packages. The one failure, an Entrypoints Unit shard (`test_shutdown.py` timeout), is unrelated.
  - [x] [#99858](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/99858) (a throwaway commit touching only `requirements/test/cuda.in`, since removed): every `hybrid-test-wheels` step was `CACHED`; `test-deps` reran and installed the wheels in about a second. Granite and Extended Generation passed with the same verifier lines and no fallback warnings.
  - [x] [#99976](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/99976) (`TORCH_NIGHTLY=1`): the wheels built against torch `2.16.0.dev20261102` with no warning, the nightly test image installed them, and Granite passed on that image with the same verifier line and no fallback warnings. The H200 jobs in that build never started: a host hook pre-pulls the plain commit tag, which only exists when a normal image build has run for the same commit, as it always has on `main`. H200 is covered by the two builds above.
  - [x] [#100183](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/100183) (`/ci run` on the current head, rebased on `main`): Hybrid (both shards) and Granite passed with the same counts as `main` builds #100175 and #100181 (15 passed + 2 skipped, 23 passed, 1 passed), each verifier line shows both commits, and no fallback warnings. Without the source builds, each of the three jobs ran 14 to 19 minutes shorter than on those `main` builds. The one failure, Intel HPU Test, fails the same way on `main`.
  - [x] [#100195](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/100195) (image build only, on a throwaway child commit that touched only `requirements/test/cuda.in` and imported only this branch's build caches, since closed): `base`'s torch install and the vLLM CUDA compile stayed `CACHED`, `hybrid-test-wheels` was reused, and only `test-deps` and the per-commit steps ran. The image built in 6 minutes.
- Builds #99812 and #99858 predate the mount change, so both reran the vLLM CUDA compile (about 13 minutes) because `base` mounted all of `requirements/`.
- **Why this PR's own builds can still rerun `base`.** [#100054](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/100054) made the same `cuda.in`-only change but also imported `main`'s cache, as every PR build does, and reran the torch install and the CUDA compile although both cache keys were unchanged. That is a BuildKit bug, moby/buildkit#6418: with several cache sources, a step whose cache key exists only in this branch's cache is not found when its parent's key also exists in `main`'s cache and the step bind-mounts a file from the build context. It hits only a PR that changes such a step relative to `main`, as this PR does to `base`'s torch install. After merge, `main`'s cache has the new step, so a requirements-only PR keeps `base` and the CUDA compile cached. The fix (moby/buildkit#7312) is merged for BuildKit v0.35.0; the CI build hosts pick up the latest stable BuildKit when their image is rebuilt.

## Details

**Decisions to check**
- **A separate stage, not a step in `test-deps`.** `base` is split at its slow-changing section into `base-toolchain` (OS packages, compilers, uv, Python) and `base`, which is otherwise unchanged. `hybrid-test-wheels` starts from `base-toolchain` and copies only `torch_lib_versions.txt` from `base`. A copied file is cached by its contents, so requirement changes in `base` do not invalidate the stage. Starting it from `base` instead would rebuild it about as often as the earlier revision did.
- **Fail the image build if the extensions fail to build.** The earlier revision only warned, but a step that warns is cached as a success, and the image would then lack the extensions until torch next changed. Rebuilds happen about once a month, so a failure is rare and visible. The exception is the torch-nightly image build: its torch changes every run and it has no layer cache, so a failure there warns, leaves the wheels out, and fails only the three jobs (at their verifier) rather than the whole nightly run. A compile failure repeats exactly, so the build does not retry it; only the GitHub fetch is tried twice.
- **Compile for sm_80 and sm_90 only.** Upstream hard-codes 9 targets on CUDA 13. Only these jobs load the extensions, through the transformers reference path, and they run on L4 (sm_89 runs sm_80 code) and H200. The one Blackwell hybrid test, `v1/e2e/test_hybrid_chunked_prefill.py`, has no transformers reference.
- **Hash-pinned build tools in their own small list** (`requirements/build/hybrid-test-deps.txt`) instead of `requirements/build/cuda.txt`, which has no hashes and leaves `ninja` and `wheel` unpinned. The list has no pre-commit hook; regenerate it with the command in its header.
- **torch is the same exact version `base` installed, without a hash check,** the same as in `base` today.
- **arm64 and Rubin images skip the build.** No job on those images runs these tests.
- **The stage honours `max_jobs`**, like the vLLM build stage, since on a rebuild the two compile at the same time.

**Also changed:** the CPU test image copies in `requirements/build/hybrid-test-deps.txt`, since the CPU tools step runs the new tests. Changes to the build script, the build-tool list or the verifier now trigger the three jobs and the CPU tools step. The Hybrid job drops its Git HTTP/1.1 setting, which only its source installs needed.

**Unchanged:** AMD mirrors and `test-amd.yaml`; the ROCm image already builds its own mamba fork. Release images (`vllm-openai`) do not include `test-deps`, so they never build this stage.

**Not done:** the torch-nightly image build has no layer cache at all, so it rebuilds this stage on every run, along with everything else.

**AI assistance:** written with Claude Code. The human submitter chose the design decisions above and reviews every changed line before requesting review.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Tests] Fix iteration-details recomputation test setup
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix the undefined `_start_decoding` call in `test_iteration_details_count_recomputation_as_prefill`, which currently fails both Ruff and mypy on main.

Fixes #66750.

## Claims

- Set up the existing regression through a real scheduler prefill and sampled output, preserving its recomputation and iteration-metrics assertions.
- Immediately verify that the request remains `RUNNING`, has one output token, and is still the scheduler's running request before testing preemption.
- Fix the CI-blocking undefined name without changing production code.

## Validation

- Reproduced Ruff F821 on the unmodified test. Upstream CI also reports the same undefined name in both Ruff and mypy: [failing pre-commit job on #66502](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/actions/runs/42772438264/job/129683156106).
- Changed-file pre-commit hooks, including Ruff, formatting and mypy, pass.
- Linux CPU pytest, base `ade4feed90d9` versus commit `f98bb8bd95cd`:


commits.pr_title: [Perf][EPLB] Copy rebalanced experts back from the buffer in one launch per weight
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Async EPLB calls `move_from_buffer` on the step loop once per MoE layer during a rearrangement. It issued one `copy_` per moved expert row per weight tensor (plus one per duplicated row), so a layer with many moved experts cost several ms of host time, and the copies ran at copy-engine bandwidth on the compute stream. This PR copies all moved rows of a weight tensor in one Triton launch.

## Claims

- Per-layer copy-back host time drops from 0.44–6.1 ms to 0.20–0.30 ms once 8 or more rows move, and GPU time drops 1.8–4.7x (GB200, table below).
- Expert weights after copy-back are byte-identical to main.
- No serving-time JIT: `EplbState.add_model` compiles the kernel for the model's weight layouts.
- CPU and XPU tensors keep the per-row `copy_` path.

## Validation

Tests on 4x GB200:

```
pytest tests/distributed/test_eplb_migration_scheduler.py  # 32 passed
pytest tests/distributed/test_eplb_execute.py              # 37 passed, 14 skipped (NIXL not installed, XPU-only)
```

- The new test compares the CUDA copy-back with the per-row CPU path byte for byte, on random placements with duplicate and unused (-1) rows. It fails if the kernel reads the wrong source row or drops the last element of a row.
- `test_eplb_execute.py` runs torch_nccl, torch_gloo, pynccl and symm_mem end to end through the new path.

Microbenchmark: one `move_from_buffer` call (one layer) on one GB200, main vs this PR, median of 9 alternating runs. The GPU is kept busy so launches never block. Host is Python plus launch time; GPU is measured with CUDA events. A/A noise on host time is about ±0.01 ms. Experts are DeepSeek-V3 shaped (H=7168, I=2048) with ep_size 8. "+d" adds one duplicated remote expert. Output bytes match main in every case.

| layout | local experts | moved rows | host ms, main → PR | GPU ms, main → PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FP8 block-scale (4 tensors) | 36 | 2 | 0.190 → 0.228 | 0.061 → 0.046 |
| FP8 block-scale (4 tensors) | 36 | 2+d | 0.210 → 0.240 | 0.055 → 0.050 |
| FP8 block-scale (4 tensors) | 36 | 8 | 0.442 → 0.198 | 0.234 → 0.132 |
| FP8 block-scale (4 tensors) | 36 | 18 | 0.883 → 0.209 | 0.520 → 0.262 |
| FP8 block-scale (4 tensors) | 36 | 36+d | 1.679 → 0.226 | 1.035 → 0.484 |
| FP8 block-scale (4 tensors) | 72 | 72+d | 3.311 → 0.254 | 2.065 → 0.954 |
| NVFP4-style (8 tensors, 4 of them one scalar per expert) | 36 | 2 | 0.269 → 0.284 | 0.062 → 0.057 |
| NVFP4-style (8 tensors, 4 of them one scalar per expert) | 36 | 8 | 0.818 → 0.275 | 0.254 → 0.104 |
| NVFP4-style (8 tensors, 4 of them one scalar per expert) | 36 | 36+d | 3.174 → 0.281 | 1.122 → 0.298 |
| NVFP4-style (8 tensors, 4 of them one scalar per expert) | 72 | 72+d | 6.057 → 0.299 | 2.664 → 0.563 |

Not included: an end-to-end serving benchmark. The change only affects rearrangement steps (one MoE layer per step, every `step_interval` steps).

## Details

- `_copy_rows_kernel` uses a (rows, cdiv(row_len, BLOCK)) grid with 16 KiB per program, in the tensor's own dtype. `row_len` is specialized, so Triton emits 16-byte accesses. EPLB expert weights are already contiguous `(E, -1)` views, with 1-byte dtypes viewed as uint8 (`get_expert_weights`, `MixtureOfExperts.set_eplb_state`). The buffers share that layout.
- Duplicate rows now read the primary's received copy in the buffer instead of the primary weight row. One launch per tensor then covers every row, with no ordering between rows. The bytes are the same.
- Tradeoff: with only 2 moved rows on a 4-tensor FP8 layer, host time is ~0.04 ms higher (4 launches plus one index upload vs 8 `copy_`), while GPU time is lower. I kept a single path instead of adding a small-count fallback.
- Alternatives measured:
  - `swap_blocks_batch` (`cuMemcpyBatchAsync`) cuts host time similarly, but it runs at copy-engine bandwidth, so GPU time stays at main's level (1.03 ms vs 0.48 ms for 36 FP8 rows).
  - `index_select` + `index_copy_` needs a temporary holding every moved row.
- The kernel is compiled by a no-op row-0 self-copy in `add_model`, not through `JitWarmupRegistry`, because the main model's `maybe_register_model` runs outside `jit_warmup_registry.activate()`.
- ROCm also takes the Triton path; it was not tested.
- Not a duplicate: the open EPLB PRs (#66399, #64485) change other parts of `eplb_state.py`, and none of them touches the copy-back.

[CI] Run the offline examples as pytest and shard the Examples step
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

The Examples step (H200 MIG 35GB, plus its MI355 DPX mirror) runs 16 example invocations as `python3` commands. The runtime shard planner only splits pytest, so the step always runs as one job, close to its 40-minute timeout. This PR runs the same invocations as one parametrized pytest file and enrolls the step and its mirror in automatic sharding.

Same approach as #66196 (NIXL PD accuracy core sweep as pytest). No open PR touches this step or `examples/`.

## Claims

- `tests/examples/test_offline_examples.py` runs exactly the commands the step ran before: same scripts, same arguments, same order, each in its own process from `examples/`. Serialize and deserialize for tensorizer stay together in one test.
- The step and the MI355 DPX mirror are enrolled with `automatic_shard: true`, so the planner can spread the 16 examples over several jobs that each stay under the 20-minute target.
- Nothing else changes for the examples: same image, same `pip install --no-deps tensorizer` setup, same timeouts.

## Validation

- Equivalence: a script loads the old step from `origin/main` and the new `EXAMPLES` list, and asserts the argv of every invocation is identical, in order (16 of 16).
- The planner's own `split_commands` accepts the new commands: setup `pip install --no-deps tensorizer`, tests `pytest -v -s examples/test_offline_examples.py`.
- `pytest --collect-only`: 16 tests. `pre-commit` passes on the changed files.
- CI build 101316 (main merged in): both Examples jobs report `16 passed`, each as one job, as expected before main has timings for the step.
- Baselines: main builds 101304 (NVIDIA) and 101276 (AMD) ran the old step with no change to `examples/`, `vllm/entrypoints` or `vllm/multimodal` since, and passed, so every example passes on both sides. Each job's wall time is within the range of recent main runs of the old step.

## Details

- **Why one pytest with subprocesses, not `LLM` calls in-process:** the examples are what users copy, so the test runs the scripts themselves. One process per example also keeps GPU memory isolated on the 35 GB MIG slice, as the old commands did. `skip_global_cleanup` is set because the pytest process starts no engine.
- **New `tests/examples/` and `working_dir: /vllm-workspace/tests`:** the planner reads test files relative to the step's working dir, and `tests/` gives the file vLLM's conftest. It finds `examples/` from its own path.
- **First timings:** main has never recorded test timings for this step, so on this PR's build it runs as one job. Main's first run after merge records per-test timings, and the step shards from the next build on. Until then nothing changes in cost or runtime.
- **Timeouts unchanged** (40 min NVIDIA, 75 min AMD). If no plan is available the step falls back to one job, as today.
- **Not done:** the examples still only check that each script exits 0 (spec decode keeps its `--test` acceptance check). Adding assertions is out of scope.

## Purpose
Bump AITER to v0.1.29.

## Test fix included

commits.pr_title: [Fast Start] Seed compiled caches through the D2D transport
commits.pr_body:
## Overview This PR extends daemon-to-daemon warmup cache seeding to FlashInfer compiled artifacts. ## Claims - Reuses the existing D2D `SeedTransport` control plane. - Transfers FlashInfer cubins and JIT compilation artifacts through Mooncake. - Allows a target daemon to install compatible artifacts before model construction, avoiding repeated JIT compilation. ## Validation - End-to-end validation on NVIDIA B300 with a K3-like MoE model. - Cold daemon startup: approximately 337 seconds. - Daemon startup with transferred compiled artifacts: approximately 34 seconds. - Target logs confirmed successful compiled-cache adoption and no repeated JIT module builds. - Both configurations successfully mapped 465 tensors through the zero-copy IPC path. ## Details The source daemon creates a versioned and checksummed cache bundle. The target validates and installs the bundle atomically before loading the model. The existing D2D control plane exchanges the manifest, while Mooncake carries the compiled-cache payload using the selected TCP or RDMA protocol. The target falls back to local compilation when the remote cache is unavailable or incompatible. Autotune artifact reuse is handled by the preceding PR; this PR focuses on compiled runtime artifacts. ---
