commits.pr_title: [Perf][GLM-5.3-Flash] Specialized decode for GB300 TP4
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Adds an opt-in specialized decode path for GLM-5.3-Flash on GB300 at TP4, built the same way as the Kimi K3 (#61867) and DSV4.1 (#61868) specialized decode: CuTe DSL kernels for every sublayer, fused all-reduce + mHC boundaries, and one policy table that picks an implementation per token count. Decode and uniform MTP verify steps of up to 64 tokens run it; everything else runs stock.

Enable with `--additional-config '{"decode_backend": "latency_specialized"}'`, the same switch as Kimi K3.

## Claims

- Median served ITL on 4x GB300 drops by 1.76x at concurrency 1 (5.15 -> 2.93 ms) and by 1.16x at concurrency 64 (13.92 -> 12.00 ms); with MTP 3 by 1.33x at concurrency 1 and 1.23x at 16.
- Accuracy stays within stock's range: GSM8K 0.918 (stock 0.914), 0.915 with MTP 3 (stock 0.912). Every kernel's error against an FP64 reference is no larger than the stock kernel's.
- Other deployments are not affected. The path refuses at startup with the list of unmet requirements (GB300 family, TP4 without PP/DP/EP/DCP, MRV2 with FULL decode graphs, FP8 KV cache), and steps it does not plan run the stock forward.

## Validation

GB300 x4, TP4, FP8 KV cache, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`, MRV2, no prefix caching, `--numa-bind` for both builds. `vllm bench serve`, random 8k-token prompts, 512 output tokens with `ignore_eos`, one wave of C requests. Median ITL is the decode step as a client sees it.

| concurrency | stock ITL | this PR ITL | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 5.15 ms | 2.93 ms | 1.76x |
| 8 | 7.23 ms | 5.53 ms | 1.31x |
| 32 | 11.11 ms | 9.04 ms | 1.23x |
| 64 | 13.92 ms | 12.00 ms | 1.16x |
| MTP 3, 1 | 6.64 ms | 4.98 ms | 1.33x |
| MTP 3, 8 | 11.61 ms | 9.28 ms | 1.25x |
| MTP 3, 16 | 14.72 ms | 12.00 ms | 1.23x |

With MTP each ITL is one verify step of 4 tokens per request. TPOT is not compared there, because on random prompts it follows the acceptance rate, which moves between runs.

The CUDA graph replay span of one decode step was measured with nsys and is the minimum over the TP ranks. Repeated runs vary by about ±0.25 ms at 32 requests.

| requests | 1 | 4 | 8 | 32 | 64 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| stock | 4.99 | 5.89 | 6.49 | 9.59 | 11.86 ms |
| this PR | 2.70 | 4.24 | 4.77 | 7.57 | 9.82 ms |

| GSM8K (1319, `vllm serve`) | stock | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| no MTP | 0.914 (c16) | 0.918 (c32), 0.921 (c2, c8) |
| MTP 3 | 0.912 | 0.915 (c16) |

Serial greedy outputs differ from stock only at near-ties: every divergence is at a top-1/top-2 logprob margin of 0.125–0.25. Stock shows drift of the same size when only the batch composition changes.

Tests: `pytest tests/models/glm5next/`. Each kernel is compared against FP64 or naive PyTorch references and against the stock kernel's error:

- the fused boundary against all-gather + PyTorch mHC, eager and under CUDA graph replay, 1–64 tokens;
- the indexer and kpool kernels, which are bit-exact with the stock Triton kernels and the Hadamard quant;
- per-route and grouped MoE, including the shared expert, on TRTLLM-prepared weights;
- the GLM copy of `KdaSplit` at the new head count, with and without the folded gate;
- the split-K projections of the DSA layers and the MTP draft, on strided inputs;
- the DSA attention kernels, the dense MLP, the draft all-reduce + norm, and the logits gather.

The tests cover each kernel at the ends of its token range rather than every token count. They skip off SM100, and the 4-GPU ones also skip with fewer than 4 GPUs. The GLM5Next CI step runs on H200, where they all skip, and no CI agent has GB300, so the tests and the evals above were run locally on GB300. The numbers above were measured on this change's previous base; on the rebased branch, pre-commit and the unit tests have been rerun. Moving the two generic pieces out keeps serial greedy outputs identical to the previous revision. With MTP, the draft prefill again computes every row, so draft tokens can flip at near-ties and later verify steps drift at near-ties; applying #64072 on top gives identical outputs again. The replay span is unchanged within noise except at 32 requests, where it is about 0.16 ms longer until #60070 lands.

## Details

**Structure.** `Glm5NextModelState` builds a `SpecializedDecode` after weight loading. At FULL graph capture, `plan()` accepts pure decode or uniform MTP verify steps of at most 64 tokens. A planned step walks the 45 layers itself and swaps in these stages, all in CuTe DSL:

- **`kda`:** a copy of Kimi K3's `KdaSplit` (`kda_split.py`) replaces four kernels per KDA layer. The copy adds schedule rows for GLM's 16 heads per rank and, at 32–64 tokens, folds the output gate GEMV into the kernel. K3's own kernel is not changed.
- **`gemm`, `dsa_gemm`, `kda_gate`:** a skinny GEMM at 1–4 tokens, then K3's split-K GEMM, which issues its weight TMA before the PDL wait. Each weight shape has its own tactics.
- **`dsa_attn`:** the q/kv a-norm becomes one kernel. Another kernel does the W_UK absorb, the FP8 query quant and the FP8 KV cache write.
- **`dsa_indexer`, `dsa_kpool`:** the indexer goes from 11 kernels to 1–2. The kpool path is bit-identical to stock.
- **`ar_mhc`:** every sublayer leaves its output TP-partial. One publish kernel and one cluster kernel then replace the all-reduce and the two mHC kernels at each of the 90 boundaries:
  - The publish kernel multicasts the partial into a Lamport mailbox.
  - The cluster kernel post-mixes the residual streams, runs the prenorm GEMV and RMS-normalizes.
  - The Sinkhorn mix only feeds the next boundary, so it runs on a side stream.
  - MoE layers stop before the finalize, and the boundary does the top-k reduction and the shared-expert add.

  At 64 tokens the boundary takes 15 µs against about 25 µs for stock.
- **`mega_moe`:** at 1–4 tokens, one 16-CTA cluster runs per routed expert, reading the TRTLLM-Gen FP8 weights in place. At 8–64 tokens, a persistent kernel walks packed units of (expert, up to 16 tokens), and routing, token quant and split-K GEMM1 all run inside it. The MoE layer at 64 tokens takes about 160 µs against 183 µs for TRTLLM-Gen.
- **`dense_mlp`:** two FP8 `mma.sync` kernels on the DeepGEMM-prepared weights.
- **LM head and MTP draft:**
  - a split-K head GEMM, and an NVLink all-gather of vocab shards in eager steps;
  - CuTe all-reduce + norm at the draft's boundaries;
  - a vocab-parallel greedy draft argmax that picks the same token as the stock argmax, ties included.

Which implementation runs at a given token count is set by one table in `policy.py`, using Kimi K3's `batch_table` specs. `additional_config["policy"]` can override entries for sweeps; an empty entry (for example `{"policy": {"boundary": ""}}`) runs that stage stock.

`specialized_decode/AGENTS.md` records the package's invariants (rank-uniform dispatch, TP-partial sublayer outputs, weight loads before the PDL wait, cluster limits) and how to validate a change to it.

**Outside `vllm/models/glm5next/`** the only change is the model config hook that turns on the vocab-parallel draft argmax for greedy MTP. Two generic pieces that earlier revisions of this PR carried are left to separate PRs, since they also help the stock path:

- FlashInfer sparse MLA: reuse a persistent multi-CTA KV counter buffer instead of allocating and zeroing one per call. #60070 already does this; this path picks it up once it lands.
- MRV2 MTP: skip draft decode metadata for indexer caches that draft steps do not read when the top-k is shared, and pass the last-token rows to the draft model so its prefill computes only those rows (#64072). Until it lands, `set_prefill_rows` in this PR is never called and the draft prefill computes every row, as stock does.

**Tradeoffs and limitations:**

- Kernels shared with Kimi K3 and DSV4.1 (CuTe DSL primitives, split-K GEMM, Lamport all-reduce primitives) are imported unchanged from those model directories for now; `KdaSplit` is copied because GLM needs a variant of it. Where they should live is left to the interface discussion in #60904 / #61311, and this PR will move to the common `--specialized-decode` interface if #61311 lands first.
- The change is large (about 11K lines, most of it kernels and their tests). It is opened as one draft so the whole path can be reviewed together. It can be split by stage if reviewers prefer.
- Not yet covered: AIME, GPQA, long-context evals, DFlash, and an in-situ comparison of the logits gather against `custom_all_gather`.

**Not a duplicate:** no other PR implements a GLM-5.3-Flash NVIDIA specialized decode. #61662 is the MI355X mono decode layer.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Remove step-path GPU syncs in EPLB skip-rearrange, AITER GDN prefill metadata, Moondream3 BOS and INT4 RHT signs
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Removes the GPU<->CPU syncs that `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` flags on ROCm at four step-path sites: the EPLB ROCm skip-rearrange heuristic, the AITER FlyDSL GDN prefill metadata build, the Moondream3 BOS embedding, and the lazy INT4 KV-cache RHT sign upload. No fix uses `gpu_sync_allowed()`. This is part of the series that replaces the allow-wrap approach of #64176 (as `njhill` suggested in review) so the ROCm test image can turn the check back on (#61939 dropped it).

## Claims

- **EPLB (sync mode, ROCm):** the skip-rearrange heuristic from #47206 now runs on the CPU copies of the load window and current map that the host policy already fetched. On `main` it runs on device tensors: `bool((map >= 0).all())` once, then `rank_load_imbalance()` twice, each doing `mean_load == 0` and `.item()`, and the second call also copies the CPU policy map to the GPU (`mapping.to(device=...)`, pageable). That is up to five D2H syncs and one pageable H2D copy per rearrange step. Skip decisions are unchanged.
- **AITER FlyDSL GDN prefill (Qwen3.5 on ROCm):** the per-step metadata is built on the host and uploaded with one pinned non-blocking copy, instead of AITER's blocking pageable `torch.tensor(..., device=cuda)`. The metadata is bit-identical and gsm8k does not change.
- **Moondream3:** the BOS id is a non-persistent buffer registered at init, instead of a blocking `torch.tensor(..., device=...)` on every multimodal step.
- **INT4 per-token-head KV cache:** the RHT signs are built in `TritonAttentionImpl.__init__` instead of on a cache miss in the first forward that writes the INT4 cache. On current `main` this is latent (see Details); it applies to CUDA as well.

## Validation

MI355X (gfx950), ROCm torch 2.13, amd-aiter 0.1.28.post1. Each before/after pair is an end-to-end `LLM` repro with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, run against the base file and the fixed file. The per-site repros ran on this PR's merge base, `main` at 5629b26146.

| Site | Before (base) | After (this PR) | Output equivalence |
|---|---|---|---|
| EPLB: DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat, TP2+EP, sync EPLB (window 5, interval 20), eager | rc=1, `GPU<->CPU sync detected` at `bool((physical_to_logical_map >= 0).all())` (same stack as CI `qwen3-30b-a3b-fp8-block-sync-eplb-accuracy-tp2`) | rc=0, 0 sync errors. Both heuristic outcomes ran under the checker: after the profile pass, 7 rearrange steps, 6 skipped and 1 that moved weights. The split depends on scheduling (the series integration run gave 5 skipped, 2 moved) | Old (GPU) vs new (CPU) heuristic on 150 random load/map cases (EP2/4/8, with and without redundant experts): `max_rel_diff=1.192e-07 skip_decision_mismatches=0` |
| GDN: Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B, MRV2, CUDA graphs, FlyDSL prefill | rc=1, sync at `aiter/ops/prefill_batch_metadata.py` `packed = torch.tensor(` (same stack as CI `lm-eval-qwen3-5-models-shard-1-2`) | rc=0, 0 sync errors; also with chunked prefill (`max_num_batched_tokens=256`) and prefix caching | Pickled metadata before vs after: equal. 10 greedy generations identical |
| Moondream3: moondream/moondream3-preview, bf16, eager, single and batched image requests | rc=1, sync at `moondream3.py` `embed_multimodal` | rc=0, 0 sync errors | Greedy outputs identical to base |
| INT4: Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct, `int4_per_token_head`, TRITON_ATTN, eager, sign cache reset to its post-`load_model` contents when the check is enabled | rc=1, sync at `_get_rht_signs` -> `signs.to(device)` (same stack as the CI `test_per_token_head_kv_cache_accuracy` failure) | rc=0, `RHT cache at check enable: [(64, 0, 'cuda:0')]` | Token ids identical to an unmodified base run |

The per-site repros ran before the final INT4 fixup that draws the signs explicitly as float32; the INT4 rows below were re-run on this branch.

<details>
<summary>Tests run on this branch</summary>

From `tests/` with `PYTHONPATH=<worktree>`, one MI355X unless noted.

```
# EPLB
pytest -q distributed/test_eplb_algo.py distributed/test_eplb_utils.py \
  distributed/test_eplb_events.py distributed/test_eplb_migration_scheduler.py
  => 53 passed, 2 skipped
# GDN
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 pytest -q v1/attention/test_gdn_aiter_flydsl.py v1/attention/test_gdn_metadata_builder.py
  => 79 passed
pytest -q v1/attention/test_gdn_aiter_flydsl.py v1/attention/test_gdn_metadata_builder.py \
  kernels/mamba/test_gdn_rocm_layout_dispatch.py kernels/mamba/test_gdn_forward_core_split.py
  => 106 passed, 6 skipped
# Moondream3
VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error pytest models/multimodal/generation/test_moondream3.py \
  models/multimodal/generation/test_moondream3_moe.py
  => 11 passed, 1 skipped (test_tensor_parallel needs 2 GPUs)
VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error pytest models/multimodal/generation/test_common.py -k moondream3
  => 1 passed (vLLM vs HF)
# INT4
pytest -q quantization/test_per_token_kv_cache.py => 85 passed
VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error pytest -q models/quantization/test_per_token_kv_cache.py -k "int4 and TRITON_ATTN"
  => 1 passed (int4_per_token_head), 0 `sync detected` lines (GPU 7, HEAD 1c7acbc722)
VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error pytest -q kernels/attention/test_attention_selector.py -k int4 => 6 passed
```

Series integration pass (all fixes of the series applied together, `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, before the INT4 float32 fixup), 0 `sync detected` lines each: the EPLB e2e repro (5 skipped, 2 moved), the Qwen3.5 GDN e2e repro, `models/multimodal/generation/test_moondream3.py` (6 passed, 1 skipped), and `models/quantization/test_per_token_kv_cache.py -k int4` (1 passed; a first attempt failed on the shared-GPU "Memory of devices not free" wait, not on a sync).
</details>

<details>
<summary>Model eval: gsm8k on Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B (GDN metadata path)</summary>

`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, 1x MI355X; both logs show "Dispatching AITER FlyDSL GDN prefill (prepare=flydsl, chunk=flydsl)". The baseline is this branch with only `vllm/_aiter_ops.py` taken from `main` (the only file of this PR on that model's path).

```

  --model_args pretrained=Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B,max_model_len=4096,gpu_memory_utilization=0.6,seed=0 \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --limit 250 --batch_size auto
```

| | flexible-extract | strict-match |
|---|---|---|
| baseline (`_aiter_ops.py` from `main`) | 0.360 ± 0.0304 | 0.356 ± 0.0303 |
| this PR | 0.360 ± 0.0304 | 0.356 ± 0.0303 |

</details>

## Details

**Not duplicating existing work.** I searched open PRs for `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK`, `gpu_sync_allowed`, "sync rocm" and each site's keywords:
- #62946 (`aarushjain29`) reported the INT4 RHT-sign sync first and wraps it in `gpu_sync_allowed()`; credit to it for the report. Here the signs are built at attention-impl init, so no allowance is needed and no forward takes the miss.
- #66003 removes a different allowed sync (ROCM_AITER_FA builder); no overlap.
- #64176 is my earlier allow-wrap PR; this series replaces it.

CI with the check re-enabled on ROCm: [vllm/ci #97758](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/97758), [vllm/amd-ci #15532](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15532).

### EPLB ROCm skip-rearrange
In sync EPLB mode, `EplbState.rearrange()` runs inside the checked `sample_tokens` step. The generic path already copies the global load window and the current `physical_to_logical_map` to CPU under `gpu_sync_allowed()` because the default policy runs in numpy; the ROCm heuristic then ignored those copies and re-read the device tensors. The copies are now kept as locals and the heuristic uses them, and `policy.rebalance_experts` moves out of the allowance since it only touches CPU tensors. `DefaultEplbPolicy`, the only registered policy, does not mutate its inputs, so reusing the CPU map is safe. The float32 reduction order on CPU can differ by about 1e-7 relative; every rank computes on the same all-reduced data, so all ranks still agree. CUDA is unaffected (the heuristic is `is_rocm()`-guarded).

### AITER GDN prefill metadata
`GDNAttentionMetadataBuilder.build()` calls `rocm_aiter_ops.build_gdn_flydsl_prefill_metadata()` on every prefill step. AITER computes the schedule as Python lists and materializes it on `cu_seqlens.device` with a blocking pageable H2D copy, the only sync on this path. The wrapper keeps its signature: it passes AITER a host `cu_seqlens` built from `seq_lens_cpu`, uploads the five int32 tensors with one `async_tensor_h2d`, and uses `dataclasses.replace` on AITER's frozen dataclasses to point at the device tensors and the caller's device `cu_seqlens` (so AITER's `layout.cu_seqlens is cu_seqlens` check holds). This mirrors the FLA path's `_build_chunk_metadata`.

Tradeoffs and limitations:
- The wrapper depends on AITER's dataclass field names. A rename fails loudly in `replace`; a new tensor field would silently stay on the CPU.
- AITER's async device assert that `cu_seqlens` matches `seq_lens` now compares the host cumsum with itself. Both callers derive the two from the same `query_start_loc`, so it could not fail in practice.
- AITER's "building during stream capture" error no longer triggers because the build runs on a CPU tensor. The metadata builders run outside capture today.
- The long-term fix is a pinned, non-blocking build path in AITER, after which this wrapper can go back to a plain call.

### Moondream3 BOS
`embed_multimodal` called `torch.tensor([bos_token_id], device=device)` on every multimodal step. The value is a model constant, so it is registered once as a non-persistent buffer, the same pattern the file uses for `_expert_map`. It is not in the state dict, so weight loading is unaffected. With the base code, `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=warn` reported only this line on the path.

### INT4 RHT signs
`_get_rht_signs()` draws the signs on CPU and calls `.to(device)` on a cache miss, and nothing filled the cache before the first forward that writes the INT4 KV cache. In the failing CI run no warmup forward reached that write before the check was enabled, so `test_per_token_head_kv_cache_accuracy` failed. On current `main` that test passes, only because the MRV2 post-capture `_dummy_run` from #62560 happens to fill the cache first; nothing guarantees this, on ROCm or CUDA. The INT4 e2e "before" above therefore resets the cache to its post-`load_model` contents to reproduce the CI ordering, and the existing CI test is not a regression signal for this site.

`TritonAttentionImpl.__init__` (the only backend supporting `int4_per_token_head`) now builds the signs for the head size's power-of-two block on the current device. The signs are drawn explicitly as float32: init runs under the model loader's default dtype, so otherwise they would be cached as bf16 rather than the float32 the lazy path produced (values are ±1 either way; callers pass float32 activations). Eager init is used instead of a pinned lazy upload so a first miss during CUDA-graph capture cannot leave a capture-only tensor in the cache.

### Coverage gaps
- **Not run locally:** gfx942/MI300; CUDA (all four paths are shared with CUDA except the ROCm-only EPLB heuristic); the CI models Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 (EPLB, DP2) and Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (DEP2/TP2/MXFP4), whose code paths were exercised with DeepSeek-V2-Lite and Qwen3.5-0.8B; Moondream3 TP=2; EPLB `test_eplb_execute.py` and `test_eplb_fused_moe_layer.py` (hit a 1500 s local timeout; neither exercises `EplbState.rearrange`).
- **No new tests.** Once the ROCm test image sets `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` again (#64176), the EPLB accuracy jobs, Qwen3.5 lm-eval and the Moondream3 generation tests fail without these fixes. INT4 has no CI regression signal on current `main` (see above). CUDA CI already runs with the check on.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Make fused MoE expert weights contiguous before GPU copy in Llama-4
commits.pr_body:
Fixes #31624.

## Summary

In `load_moe_expert_weights`, a sliced/transposed fused MoE expert weight view is passed to `weight_loader()` and copied to GPU while still non-contiguous. A non-contiguous CPU tensor's DMA transfer to GPU is dramatically slower than a contiguous one. Adds `.contiguous()` right before the `weight_loader()` call, on the already-sliced piece — not upfront on the whole weight, since a prior attempt at this fix (#32081, auto-closed by staleness, not rejected) found that naive blanket `.contiguous()` can regress smaller tensors.

## Scope note

A synthetic benchmark on H100 NVL (the real Llama-4 checkpoints, 109B-400B, don't fit on one GPU) tested three locations that could have the same issue. Only the fused MoE expert weight path (this PR) showed an unambiguous, large improvement — FP8 block-scale and Q/K rotary permute tensors were *slower* with `.contiguous()` added at their (smaller) sizes in isolation. Since MoE expert weights dominate total checkpoint bytes, this is the change with validated, measured benefit; the other two locations are deliberately excluded pending more precise real-world sizing data.

## Validation

```
torch 2.6.0a0+df5bbc09d1.nv24.11 | GPU: NVIDIA H100 NVL
=== fused MoE expert weight, basic-indexed view after transpose(-1,-2), shape [64,4096,1024] ===
non-contiguous transfer: mean=574.401ms min=536.849ms max=585.899ms
contiguous() transfer:   mean=28.911ms min=24.788ms max=103.387ms
speedup: 19.87x
```
(A first run on the same shape measured 22.35x; 19.87x on a clean isolated re-run — consistent within normal GPU/CPU scheduling noise.)

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Stream DeepSeek DSML tool-call arguments
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Rust tool parsers for converted formats emit each tool call whole when it closes, so between a call's start and end the stream is silent. Coding agents write long string arguments (file contents, edit strings, patches), and the silence can trip client idle timeouts and starves clients and middleware that render or review argument content as it streams. Native-JSON formats already stream their raw arguments.

This PR streams DeepSeek DSML (V3.2/V4/V4.1) arguments as they are generated, and adds the shared writer that the next PRs in the stack reuse for Kimi K3 and MiniMax M3.

## Claims

- The invoke name goes out when the invoke opens, and each parameter is written as it arrives or as soon as it closes:
  - `string="true"`: streams as escaped JSON string fragments.
  - `string="false"`: JSON text, written once complete, since only then is its validity known: as spelled when it is valid JSON, as DeepSeek's reference decoders pass it through, and otherwise as a JSON string of the text, as the Python parser falls back, so a malformed value cannot make `arguments` invalid JSON.
  - No `string` attribute: streams as a string when the schema type is exactly `string`, otherwise is converted through the schema once complete, as today.
- Parameter markers are matched by token identity, so an ordinary-token spelling of `</｜DSML｜parameter>` inside a value stays part of the value.
- Behavior changes beyond chunking: valid `string="false"` values keep their spelling instead of being coerced through the schema (`42` for a string parameter stays a number, `null` stays null), and a repeated parameter keeps its first value.

## Validation

- New behavioral tests fail on the base and pass here: `deepseek_v32_parse_complete_passes_json_values_through`, `deepseek_v32_streams_arguments_before_the_invoke_closes` (per-chunk deltas), `spaced_dsml_streaming_passes_json_values_through` (V4.1, including 1-character chunks), and `deepseek_v4_ordinary_block_closers_inside_parameter_value_stay_value`, extended with an ordinary-token parameter closer. They replace the two tests that pinned schema coercion of `string="false"` values.
- Malformed `string="false"` values stay valid JSON: `deepseek_v32_parse_complete_writes_malformed_json_values_as_strings` (a string labelled `string="false"`, an empty value, Python-style `True` and `{'a': 1}`, a non-`"true"` attribute value) and a malformed value in the V4.1 split-point test. Both fail on the first revision of this PR, which streamed `string="false"` text raw (`{"location": Hangzhou, "unit": , ...}`).
- Writer unit tests: string fragments escape exactly like the whole string at every split point; the writer's output equals serializing the whole object in each `JsonStyle`; `write_json` keeps valid text as spelled (`1.50`, `1e-05`, surrounding whitespace trimmed) and writes malformed text (`Hangzhou`, `NaN`, `1 2`, empty) as strings; keep-first duplicate keys; `{}` for no arguments.
- `verbatim_string_params_convert_any_text_unchanged` pins which schema types may stream (`"null"`, empty, and `" 42 "` stay verbatim).
- All 25 roundtrip cases pass unchanged: DSML output for template-rendered calls is byte-identical to the base PR's expectations.
- `cargo test -p vllm-parser -p vllm-chat -p vllm-server`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, and `cargo fmt --check` pass, apart from the `vllm-server` test noted in the base PR, which fails the same way on main.
- Not covered: a run against a real model or engine.

## Details

- Principle: a value streams only where its conversion is the identity for every text, which leaves JSON string escaping. JSON text the model writes passes through unchanged only when it is valid, which is known at its end, so it is buffered and written once; every other argument is converted once by the existing schema conversion. No partial version of any conversion exists, and non-streaming output is the same state machine fed once.
- DeepSeek's reference decoders (HF `encoding_dsv4.py`, [deepseek-recipe](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-recipe/blob/935817c66f5d6e64838f419692545f06787e485f/deepseek-recipe/src/stream/output_parser.rs#L553-L566)) pass `string="false"` text through unvalidated, but deepseek-recipe selects a tool-call grammar constraint for every request with tools, which vLLM does not apply by default, so this PR keeps the fallback that main and the Python parser have. Valid values come out byte-identical to the reference decoders.
- `tool/arguments.rs`:
  - `ArgumentsWriter` owns only JSON syntax: separators in the parser's `JsonStyle`, keys, quotes, escaping, keep-first duplicate keys, and the validity check of model-written JSON. A streamed argument is `open_string` + `push` + `close`; a whole argument is `write_value` (a converted `Value`) or `write_json` (JSON text, checked with `serde_json::from_str::<IgnoredAny>`, so no value tree is built). String escaping uses serde_json with a formatter that omits the quotes; serde_json escapes byte by byte, so fragments concatenate to the whole-string output.
  - `open_raw_json` streams JSON text unchecked and is unused, kept with `#[allow(dead_code)]` for formats whose JSON is valid by construction (such as a grammar-constrained call).
  - The writer keeps what it wrote since the last delta in a `Vec<u8>` that serde_json serializes into directly; taking it costs one UTF-8 check per delta and no copy.
  - `OpenToolCall` pairs the writer with the call's name and index and turns what one event wrote into one `ToolCallDelta`, the first carrying the name.
- The DSML parser keeps main's `match event` shape with a single `Invoke { call, body }` mode whose position (between parameters, streamed, buffered) changes in place, and emits one delta per event.
- Complexity: about 513 non-test lines added and 120 removed: 258 for the shared writer and call state (including docs), 231 added and 112 removed in DSML, 20 for `ToolSchemas::is_verbatim_string`.
- Known limitations, left to follow-ups: if a parser fails after a call has started streaming, the chat layer's existing parse-failure fallback still applies to the remaining text; a truncated stream (`finish_reason=length`) leaves the partial arguments unrepaired, as OpenAI's streaming does.
- No docs change: no page describes when Rust tool-call deltas are emitted.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Write tool-call arguments in the template's JSON style
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Rust tool parsers for converted formats (XML-like or special-token syntaxes) serialize the `arguments` object with serde_json's compact separators, while most of their chat templates render JSON values with Python's `json.dumps` separators (`, ` and `: `). The roundtrip harness pinned that incidental compact output per case instead of the template's style. This PR makes each parser that serializes `arguments` write the style its template renders JSON in, and makes the harness assert the template's style.

It is the base of a stack that streams tool-call arguments for DeepSeek DSML, Kimi K3, and MiniMax M3. Those parsers pass the model's JSON values through unchanged, so the object around them has to use the same separators.

## Claims

- New `JsonStyle { Compact, Spaced }` in `vllm-parser`. Every parser that serializes `arguments` uses the style its template renders JSON in, and `Spaced` (the HF `tojson` and Python `json.dumps` default) when its template renders no JSON:
  - `Spaced`: DeepSeek DSML (V3.2/V4/V4.1), GLM-4.5/4.7, HY, MiniMax M2, Qwen3-Coder (also Seed-OSS, MiMo, Step-5), Muse, `hf`, Gemma4, MiniMax M3.
  - `Compact`: Kimi K3, whose renderer writes compact values.
- `arguments` stay value-equal; only whitespace changes. For these formats that also matches the Python frontend, whose parsers end in `json.dumps(..., ensure_ascii=False)`.
- The roundtrip harness states each case's template style (`json_style`) instead of the parser's output; 16 cases move from compact to spaced.

## Validation

How the roundtrip templates render the fixture `{"y": 1.0, "x": 2, "items": ["left", "right"]}` (rendered prompts printed from the harness locally):

| Template JSON | Cases | Parser output before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| Spaced values (`tojson`, DeepSeek's encoder) | DeepSeek V3.2/V4/V4.1, GLM-4.5/4.7/5.2, MiniMax M2.5, Qwen3.5, Step-5, Seed-OSS, MiMo V2.6, Hy3, Muse Spark | compact | spaced |
| Spaced whole object, passed through | Qwen3, Kimi K2.5 | spaced | spaced |
| Compact | Kimi K3 values; gpt-oss, Inkling whole object | compact | compact |
| No JSON | Gemma4 (native and through `hf`), MiniMax M3 | compact | spaced |

- Templates outside the harness also use `tojson`: Qwen3-Coder, MiniMax M2, GLM-4.6, and HY V4 (`tencent/Hy4-preview`).
- The spaced formatter's output was byte-identical to `serde_json_fmt` with `, `/`: ` and to Python `json.dumps(ensure_ascii=False)` on 20,006 random values (nested and empty containers, keys and strings containing separators, quotes, control and non-ASCII characters).
- `cargo test -p vllm-parser -p vllm-chat -p vllm-server`: `vllm-parser` 627 and `vllm-chat` 460 unit tests and all 25 roundtrip cases (local HF tokenizer files) pass. In `vllm-server`, `chat_completions_n_returns_one_choice_per_seeded_sample` fails in the full parallel run and passes alone; it fails the same way on main and does not involve tool calls.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean.

## Details

- The style is a per-parser constant: each parser family's templates agree. A custom `--chat-template` with another style still gets value-equal JSON.
- Only separators are modeled. A parser that re-serializes values can still differ from its template in number spelling (Python's `1e-05` against serde's `1e-5`); later PRs in the stack pass DSML and K3 values through unchanged.
- Prompt tokens do not change: these templates parse `arguments` before rendering, and the harness's re-render check already passed.
- `Spaced` is a small serde `Formatter` rather than the `serde_json_fmt` crate: adding that crate to `vllm-parser` pulls `compact_str`, whose `Add` impls break `String + &String` inference in existing parser tests. The harness keeps formatting its expectations with `serde_json_fmt`, so it does not run the code under test.
- Snapshot-heavy diff: 10 unit tests that compared literal compact `arguments` strings now expect spaced output, and one Muse test drops `compact_` from its name.
- No docs change: no page describes the whitespace of Rust tool-call arguments.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Model] Avoid host synchronization in dots.ocr vision encoder
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Running `dots.ocr` image inference with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` currently crashes before returning an OCR result. The vision encoder builds position indices on the CPU and computes sequence metadata on the GPU, triggering host-device transfers and host reads that trip the synchronization check (Fixes [#66243](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/66243)).

## Claims

This PR resolves the synchronization overhead in the shared `dots.ocr` / `dots.mocr` vision encoder by:

1. Allocating position indices directly on the model device (`self.device`) so rotary embedding lookups don't trigger cross-device copies.
2. Computing cumulative sequence boundaries (`cu_seqlens`) and `max_seqlen` directly on the CPU from the existing Python `grid_thw` list via `itertools.accumulate`, avoiding blocking H2D copies, `repeat_interleave` host-read sizing, and `.item()` calls.
3. Transferring cumulative lengths asynchronously via `async_tensor_h2d` (keeping `int32` for normal inference and preserving the `int64` branch for TorchScript tracing).
4. Dropping the unused `grid_thw` tensor argument from the patch-embedding call.

## Validation

### Test Plan

#### 1. Unit & Distributed Tests (`tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_dots_ocr.py`)

Tested on 2x RTX 4090 GPUs (Python 3.12.11, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130, Transformers 5.22.2) against baseline `cf5cea2da37d3dfed27d2e0aa3041c3e553c2d57` using `rednote-hilab/dots.ocr` (`c0111ce6bc07803dbc267932ffef0ae3a51dc951`, bf16, eager mode).

- `vision_without_host_sync`: Warms up a small vision model and runs the forward pass under `torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode("error")`.
- `tensor_parallel_without_host_sync`: Runs `vllm_runner` with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` (prefix and multimodal processor caches disabled), verifying OCR outputs at TP=1 and TP=2 and comparing logprobs via `check_logprobs_close`.

### Test Result

#### 1. Synchronization Check (Before vs. After)

```bash
# Baseline (cf5cea2da): fails with synchronization errors
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_dots_ocr.py \
  -k vision_without_host_sync -v -s
# FAILED: 1 failed, 1 deselected
# rotary_pos_emb = rotary_pos_emb_full[pos_ids].flatten(1)
# RuntimeError: called a synchronizing CUDA operation

HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1,0 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_dots_ocr.py \
  -k tensor_parallel_without_host_sync -v -s
# FAILED during image inference:
# RuntimeError: GPU<->CPU sync detected - avoid it or wrap with gpu_sync_allowed()

# This PR: passes both checks
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=3,1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_dots_ocr.py -v -s
# 2 passed, 2 warnings in 212.28s

```

#### 2. Numerical Equivalence Across Backends

Compared output embeddings (`rtol=0, atol=0`) using a seeded 2-layer vision model across two grid shapes (`[[1, 4, 6]]` and `[[2, 4, 6], [1, 6, 8]]`):

| Vision Backend | Baseline vs. Patch (Both Grids) | `set_sync_debug_mode("error")` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FlashAttention 2 | Bit-identical | Passed |
| Triton | Bit-identical | Passed |
| Torch SDPA | Bit-identical | Fails in `torch_sdpa_wrapper` (`.tolist()`) |

*Note: `torch_sdpa_wrapper` still reads device sequence lengths via `.tolist()`, which is outside the scope of this model-level fix.*

#### 3. End-to-End OCR Regression Check

Evaluated 3 synthetic PIL-rendered images via `LLM.generate` (TP=1, greedy decoding, seed 0, `max_tokens=32`, top-5 logprobs, `max_model_len=1024`, `max_num_seqs=2`, 256 MiB KV cache, caches disabled). Baseline ran with sync checks disabled; this patch ran with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`:

| Image Text | Resolution | Baseline Output | Patch Output | Token IDs & Top-5 Logprobs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `HELLO 1234` | 448 × 224 | `HELLO 1234` | `HELLO 1234` | Exact match |
| `TOTAL 56` | 224 × 336 | `TOTAL 56` | `TOTAL 56` | Exact match |
| `DATE 2026` | 448 × 336 | `DATE 2026` | `DATE 2026` | Exact match |

#### 4. Linting

```bash
uv run --no-sync pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/model_executor/models/dots_ocr.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_dots_ocr.py \
  docs/models/supported_models.md \
  docs/usage/troubleshooting.md

```

All hooks (Ruff, markdownlint, mypy, test tethering) passed. The added `core_model` and `distributed(num_gpus=2)` tests map directly to the existing multimodal and distributed CI lanes.

## Details

**Related work:**

- [#64543](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64543) (merged) fixed QKV splitting at TP > 1, which is a separate issue.
- [#63074](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63074) (open) adds encoder CUDA graph support and overlaps with the CPU sequence-metadata change, but leaves CPU-allocated position indices in place. This PR focuses strictly on fixing the remaining synchronization bugs and adding regression coverage without introducing graph changes.

commits.pr_title: [Frontend] Honour --host for the run-batch Prometheus metrics server
commits.pr_body:
## Problem

`BatchFrontendArgs` declares `--host` for the Prometheus metrics server and marks `--url` deprecated in favour of it:

```python
host: str | None = None
"""Host name for the Prometheus metrics server (only needed if enable-metrics is set)."""
url: str = "0.0.0.0"
"""[DEPRECATED] Host name for the Prometheus metrics server ... Use --host instead."""
...
frontend_kwargs["url"]["deprecated"] = True
```

The CLI path binds with the deprecated one:

```python
# vllm/entrypoints/cli/run_batch.py:42
start_http_server(port=args.port, addr=args.url)
```

So `vllm run-batch --enable-metrics --host 127.0.0.1 -i in.jsonl -o out.jsonl` starts the metrics server on `0.0.0.0`, every interface, when the caller explicitly asked for loopback. Nothing warns.

The two entry points disagree on the same flags. `python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.run_batch` uses `addr=args.host` at `run_batch.py:873`; only the `vllm run-batch` subcommand uses `args.url`.

```
invocation                            binds now    binds after
--host 127.0.0.1                      0.0.0.0      127.0.0.1
--url 127.0.0.2 (deprecated)          127.0.0.2    127.0.0.2
--host 127.0.0.1 --url 127.0.0.2      127.0.0.2    127.0.0.1
neither (defaults)                    0.0.0.0      0.0.0.0
```

`addr` is what `prometheus_client.start_http_server` passes to the socket bind, so this is the difference between a metrics endpoint reachable only from the box and one reachable from anywhere that can route to it.

## Fix

Prefer `--host`, falling back to the deprecated `--url` only when `--host` was not given. The default and the deprecated flag keep working exactly as before, so nothing that relies on either changes.

## Not a duplicate

Checked per AGENTS.md:

```
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "run-batch metrics host"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "run_batch start_http_server"
gh api -X GET search/issues -f q="repo:vllm-project/vllm run-batch host metrics"
gh api "repos/vllm-project/vllm/commits?path=vllm/entrypoints/cli/run_batch.py&per_page=10"
```

The second returns nothing; the first and third return unrelated perf and ROCm work that the fuzzy search matched on the word "metrics". No open PR touches `vllm/entrypoints/cli/run_batch.py`, and the ten most recent commits to that file are CLI help, formatting and import-style changes, none of them on this line.

## Tests run and results

A parametrised unit test added to `tests/entrypoints/openai/test_run_batch.py`, covering all four invocations above. It parses real args through `make_arg_parser`, patches `prometheus_client.start_http_server` and `run_batch.main`, and asserts the `addr` that was passed, so it needs no model and no GPU.

Being straight about what I could and could not run: I do not have a machine that can import vLLM, so I could not execute the new test here, and CI is the check. What I did verify locally, and what the table above comes from, is the argument resolution itself, evaluated over the four invocations against both the old and the new expression, plus that `prometheus_client.start_http_server`'s `addr` really is the bind address (`127.0.0.1` binds loopback, `0.0.0.0` binds every interface, and `None` binds `::`). The two source lines and the deprecation marking were read from `main` at 1ab2801.

Related, and deliberately left alone: the module entry point passes `addr=args.host`, which is `None` unless `--host` is given, and `start_http_server(addr=None)` binds `::` rather than the `0.0.0.0` its signature defaults to. Both are all-interfaces, so it is not the same bug, but if you would like the two paths to agree exactly I am happy to align that in this PR.

## Model evaluation

Not applicable: this changes which address a Prometheus metrics HTTP server binds to. It does not touch generation, sampling, scheduling or any serving path, and produces no change to model output or accuracy.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][KV Connector][ROCm] MoRIIO WRITE: skip blocks the decoder prefix cache already holds
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

In MoRIIO WRITE mode the prefiller (P) rewrites every prompt block into the decoder (D), including the blocks D's prefix cache already holds. P now skips them.

Not a duplicate: #62190 and #48471 change READ mode only.

## Claims

- P skips D's hashed leading blocks (its local prefix hit), as NIXL push and Mooncake do. Single-group WRITE only.
- MiniMax-M3.1-Flash 1P1D on MI355X: KV written per request and P rank 1,650 MB to 130 MB; P write-thread busy time 79% to 32%.
- 3600 s agentic replay at concurrency 48: 35,639 to 38,741 tok/s/GPU (+8.7%), p90 interactivity 157.8 to 149.6. With one D the saved time becomes a larger decode batch, so no 1P1D Pareto claim.

## Validation

- branch @ 2029713aac: `test_moriio_*.py` 887 passed; with main's connector the new tests fail (5 of 163). ruff 0.14.0 clean.
- No accuracy eval: skipped blocks are D's cached copies of this KV.

<details><summary>Commands, revert-red and GPU setup</summary>

```bash
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONPATH=$PWD python -m pytest -q --noconftest \
  -p no:cacheprovider tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_*.py
uvx ruff@0.14.0 check <changed files>
uvx ruff@0.14.0 format --check <changed files>
```

Revert-red, new tests with main's `moriio_common.py`, `moriio_connector.py` and `moriio_engine.py`: 3 x `test_plain_write_notify_skips_blocks_of_the_local_prefix_hit`, `test_write_skips_blocks_the_consumer_prefix_cache_already_holds`, and `test_hybrid_write_notifies_grouped_slots_or_releases_a_complete_local_hit[9]` (now expects `num_skip_blocks=0`). Counting the skip as `(N - E) // B` instead fails `[1-8]`, a load trimmed by whole blocks.

The GPU runs below used that `(N - E) // B` count. On current main it equals the hashed-block count: before this hook the scheduler trims `E` by less than a block (SWA replay, partial tail) or to 0 (`cap_external_hit`, which takes the release path).

GPU build: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-40941f2c` with the Python tree of main @ 2173d7121 plus #63483 and this change. This branch is the same diff on a2bcb5657a; no MoRIIO file changed in between. One MI355X node: P TP4 on GPUs 0-3, D TP4 on GPUs 4-7, MoRIIO WRITE over xgmi, prefix caching on both, P-side MultiConnector (MoRIIO + SimpleCPUOffloadConnector), DSpark speculative decoding with synthetic acceptance length 4.04, nvfp4 KV cache, block size 128.

Workload: `agentx profile --public-dataset semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126 --benchmark-duration 3600 --concurrency 48`, average input about 155K tokens. Interactivity is 1000 / p90 ITL in ms; tok/s/GPU counts input and output tokens over the 8 GPUs.

| concurrency 48, 3600 s | main + #63483 | + this change |
|---|---|---|
| tok/s/GPU | 35,639 | 38,741 |
| p90 interactivity (tok/s/user) | 157.8 | 149.6 |
| succeeded / errors | 6,630 / 2 | 7,177 / 2 |
| D requests waiting for KV (avg) | 12.8 | 4.0 |

Write volume comes from a 900 s concurrency-64 pair with a per-request writer observer on P. These are instrumented builds, not throughput points. On average 955 of 1,027 blocks per request were skipped. Per request and P rank, contiguous segments went from 61.5K to 4.6K and bytes from 1,650 MB to 130 MB. Writer-thread busy time went from 79% to 32%.
</details>

## Details

1. D: the scheduler finds a local prefix hit of `L` tokens.
2. D: `update_state_after_alloc` sends P its whole block table in `remote_blocks`, including the blocks of the hit.
3. P: `MoRIIOWriter._prepare_transfer_plan` pairs both tables from block 0, so it rewrites `[0, L)`: shared cached blocks that other requests on D may be reading.
4. Fix: D also sends `num_skip_blocks`, its count of hashed leading blocks, and P slices both tables from it.

NIXL push and Mooncake send only the unhashed suffix and tail-align P. Here D keeps the whole table: `compute_block_transfer_offsets` zips the tables unchecked, so an older P would pair its leading blocks with a suffix, and D's table can end in lookahead blocks. An older P ignores the key; an older D omits it.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Mono: batch TP8 K2's X8 copies, load its push's peer bases late
commits.pr_body:
### Purpose

#63892 changes the gfx950 TP4 K2 build (target and DSpark draft) in two ways:

- `moe.load_x8_rows_all`: the one-tile X8 / X8R row copies issue every load before the first LDS store.
- `run_ffn(peer_load=...)`: the MoE all-reduce push loads its peer bases right before the down stage's barrier. Before, it held them from the start of the kernel.

#63892 gates both on `tp == 4 and not GFX942`. With TP8 mono decode (#64101), the TP8 K2 build goes through the same code, so this PR widens the gate to TP4 and TP8:

```python
late_peers = tp in (4, 8) and not GFX942
```

It also updates the comment and runs the no-scratch test at TP8. Nothing else changes. gfx942 and TP2 builds are not affected.

**Stacking.** This PR depends on two open PRs, and both must land first:

| commit in this branch | from |
|---|---|
| `92852abd06` Mono: batch TP4 K2's X8 copies, load its push's peer bases late | #63892 (its head; based on main `41f5146b5b`, **not** stacked on #63027) |
| `6b7a45b73b` Mono decode at TP8 on MI355X | #64101's code commit `b34932b6a7` (cherry-picked cleanly) |
| `013ac2a8a7` Mono: batch TP8 K2's X8 copies, load its push's peer bases late | **this PR** |

Only the last commit is new. After #63892 and #64101 merge, this PR is a 2-file, +7/-6 line diff (`mono/layer.py` and `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_numerics.py`).

- #64101's head is now `e58609ea50`. Its second commit adds only the optional MI355 x8 CI step in `.buildkite/test-amd.yaml`, and it is not in this branch. That step runs `test_mono_decode_layer_matches_vllm[8]`, the GPU check that covers this PR's TP8 K2.
- The branch sits on #63892's base, main `41f5146b5b`. #64101 is based on the newer main `83909ad84b`. In `mono/`, the only change between the two is #63689, the MXFP8 scale code in `attention/device.py` and `stages/moe.py`, and it does not touch the code this PR changes.
- The stack does not contain #63027 or #63893. Upstream has no tuned K2 at TP8, because tuned builds are TP2 compress-ratio 2 only. A trial merge of #63027 into this branch conflicts in four files, and none of the conflicts come from this PR. `attention/back.py` conflicts because of #64101: #63027's tuned store branch needs #64101's padded-head handling. `layer.py` (imports), `stages/moe.py` (`load_x8_rows`) and the numerics test conflict because of #63892. This PR's gate lines merge cleanly.

Branch: `okorzh-amd/vllm` `okorzh/dsv41-mono-tp8-x8r` @ `013ac2a8a7`.

### Test Plan

1. CPU compile for gfx950 (FlyDSL `COMPILE_ONLY`, image `rocm/mlperf-inference:custom_vllm_custom_2026-10-23-17-30-29`, no devices). I built the `mono/` tree at `6b7a45b73b` (base = #63892 + #64101) and at this PR. That is 72 configurations, each built at both, for 144 builds:
   - K2 at TP2, TP4 and TP8, with 7, 14, 16 and 28 rows, for 5 cases: compress ratio 0, 1 or 2 (no key index), ratio 2 with the key index, and the DSpark draft (128 experts, top-3, SWA 192)
   - K1 at 7 and 28 rows (ratio 2), and draft K1 at 14 rows, at each TP
   - FFN at 7 rows, at each TP

   For each build I recorded VGPRs, spills, LDS and private segment. I hashed the `gpu.binary` blob to compare base and PR, and checked the disassembly for `scratch_` instructions and for load -> `s_waitcnt vmcnt(0)` -> `ds_write` sequences.
2. `test_mono_decode_k2_no_scratch[tp=4,8][tokens=14,16]` (renamed from `test_mono_decode_k2_tp4_no_scratch`). I ran the test body in the same image on CPU with `ray` stubbed, because the `_on_cdna4()` skip needs a GPU.
3. On GPU, run `test_mono_decode_layer_matches_vllm[tp=8]` on MI355X. #64101 adds the TP8 cases and #63892 adds the 14-row ratio-2 step. In CI this runs in #64101's optional mi355_8 step. `test_mono_decode_k2_no_scratch` only compiles, so the existing 4-GPU "Mono Decode Numerics" step also runs its TP8 cases.
4. End to end: the DSv4.1 CI conc-1 recipe at TP8, measuring ms/step, GSM8K and acceptance length.

### Test Result

**1. CPU compile, gfx950.** All 144 builds succeed. No build has spills or scratch, and LDS is unchanged in every build.

- **TP2 and TP4: byte-identical to the base** (48 of 48 configurations: K1, K2, FFN, target and draft).
- **TP8 K1 and FFN: byte-identical** (4 of 4).
- **TP8 K2** (only these 20 configurations change):

| TP8 K2 | rows | VGPRs base -> PR | load->vmcnt(0)->LDS-store sequences base -> PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| target, ratio 0/1/2, with or without index | 7 | 250 -> 237 | 13 -> 2 |
|  | 14 | 242 -> 240 | 13 -> 2 |
|  | 16 | 248-249 -> 240 | 10-12 -> 1 |
|  | 28 | 232 -> 231-232 | 13 -> 11-13 (past 16 rows only the peer-base loads move, as at TP4) |
| draft | 7 / 14 / 16 / 28 | 199 / 167 / 165 / 174 -> 160 / 169 / 175 / 173 | 13 -> 2 / 13 -> 2 / 12 -> 1 / 13 -> 13 |

Unlike TP4 before #63892, the base TP8 K2 does not spill, even though it holds 8 peer bases. So at TP8, any gain from this PR has to come from the batched X8 copies and the late base loads, because there is no spill reload to remove. This PR's gain at TP8 has not been measured on its own. The draft's VGPR count rises by up to 10 at 14 and 16 rows, but stays at 175 or below with no spill. Occupancy does not change: K2 runs 8 waves per CTA (2 per SIMD) and one CTA per CU, because its LDS limits it to one.

As an independent check, I rebuilt three pairs from fresh `git archive` trees: TP4 K2 at 16 rows ratio 2, the TP4 draft at 14 rows, and TP8 K2 at 16 rows ratio 2. The binary hashes match the sweep: the two TP4 pairs are identical, and the TP8 pair differs. TP8 K2 at 16 rows ratio 2 goes from 249 to 240 VGPRs, and its load->vmcnt(0)->store sequences drop from 12 to 1.

**2. No-scratch test:** passes for TP4 and TP8 at 14 and 16 rows. At TP8 it is a guard: the base passes too.

**3. GPU tests:** not run. The GPUs were busy.

**4. Performance.** Measured on 8x MI355X with the local stack (not this branch). Setup: conc-1 microbench, 32k context, synthetic AL 3.87, CI recipe. Nightly `83c078d955` + #63182 #63027 #63367 #63181 #63355 + the local stack.

| TP8 mono | ms/step |
|---|---|
| generic | 4.970 |
| + #63885 #63888 #63890 #63891 + main #63576 | 4.795 |
| + tuned K1 at TP8 + X8R at TP8 (this PR) + seam poll batch | **4.534** |

- conc 2: 5.234 ms/step.
- conc 4, one TP8 server: 7.156 ms/step, TPOT 2.35 ms.
- GSM8K 0.919, AL 3.570. The base gives 0.917-0.923 and 3.565-3.585.
- For reference, TP4 with tuned K1 runs at 4.77 ms/step.

**Not measured:** the TP8 effect of this PR alone. In the measured run, X8R was turned on at TP8 together with tuned K1 at TP8 (#63893 widened) and the seam poll batch. At TP4, X8R alone measured -1.1% at conc 1 and -3.9% at conc 2.

The measured run used the local stack's version of X8R: an env-switched `MonoBuild.x8r` on non-tuned K2 builds, with the same `load_x8_rows_all` and late peer-base loads. It did not use this branch's gate. At TP8 no K2 build is tuned, so both turn on the same builds.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Mono: tuned K1 at TP4
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

**This draft is stacked on #63027. Only the last commit (`3d923a6848`) is new; the first three (`96fa04ad7a`, `043dd8da90`, `37372f010c`) are #63027's, rebased onto main `4b47db922b`.**

#63027 tunes K1 and K2 for the target's compress-ratio-2 layers at TP2 only. This PR turns its tuned K1 (the attention seam and front) on for every TP4 layer on gfx950 (MI355X), the DSpark draft's included. K2 stays generic at TP4, and TP8 keeps the generic K1. We run DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at low concurrency on MI355X as TP4 with `--monokernel`.

## Claims

- **Decode step (ABBA against #63027 rebased, 4 rounds):** c1 -284 us (-5.2%), c2 -326 us (-4.8%), c4 -194 us (-2.2%); every round faster, beyond t x SE and the base A/A spread.
- **Outputs unchanged, by design:** the paths are #63027's, which it shows bit-exact against the generic code at TP2. The numerics test now also compares them bit for bit at TP4: it passes on MI355X, and a mutant one bf16 ulp off in TP4 K1 fails it. GSM8K and AL match base within noise. The draft K1 has no GPU bit check (see test coverage).
- **Scope:** fixed per build, no env var: `MonoBuild.tuned_front = tuned or (not GFX942 and not generic and tp == 4)`. Mono builds only for gfx942 and gfx950, so this means gfx950. TP2, TP8, `generic=True` and gfx942 builds compile as on #63027. TP8 keeps the generic K1; #64152 extends this PR to TP8. TP4 K2 code is unchanged; only its scratch offsets move.
- **Compile level (measured):** TP4 K1 uses 148-174 VGPRs at 1-48 rows (#63027 rebased: 142-240), with no spills and unchanged LDS. TP8 builds are binary-identical to main's.

## Validation

**CPU (done, on the rebased code; the pushed head only trims comments and docstrings, and its AST is identical)**

- [x] Rebased onto main `4b47db922b`, which has #63576, #63689, #63816, #64008 and #64101 (TP8 mono). One conflict, in #63027's first commit (`stages/moe.py`, `stage_route`): the resolution keeps #63816's NaN guard and cursor mask, plus #63027's preloaded tuned bias.
- [x] `pre-commit` passes on the stack's 12 changed files (ruff, mypy, typos, markdownlint).
- [x] Compile-only (FlyDSL 0.4.0, `COMPILE_ONLY=1`): 252 gfx950 configs per tree (TP2 / TP4 / TP8, including TP4 K1 and K2 at ratio 2 at every width 1-48) and 50 gfx942 configs. The table is in the details below.
- [x] Gate and layout check over 1,728 `MonoBuild` keys per arch (TP2 / TP4 / TP8): only the 288 TP4 non-generic gfx950 layouts change, by 4,608-8,960 B per width. TP2, TP8, `generic=True` and gfx942 are identical.
- [x] Launcher check after #64008's launcher reuse: 1,248 launchers on gfx950, each build gets its own, and no two different builds share a JIT key.
- Test change: at TP4 every `_check_layers` case now also runs a `generic=True` runner (the code this PR replaces) and compares the outputs bit for bit. New case: ratio 0 at 7 rows, the c1 DSpark width. #63027 has no TP4 tuned build, so this comparison is new.
- CI: `:amd: (MI355) DeepSeek-V4.1 Mono Decode Numerics` (mi355_4, TP2 / TP4) and `:amd: (MI355) DeepSeek-V4.1 Mono Decode Numerics TP8` (mi355_8) run both test files on this PR's paths.
  - CI cost: the mi355_4 job's four test ids took 126 s / 133 s (numerics [2] / [4]) and 250 s / 243 s (layers [2-8] / [4-8]) on MI355X, each in a fresh container with no JIT cache mounted; the job's timeout is 40 min.

**GPU (done, 8x MI355X; base = #63027 rebased, `37372f010c`; PR = base + `3d923a6848`)**

- [x] Unit tests at TP2 / TP4 / TP8: `pytest -v -s tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_numerics.py tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_layers.py`. This covers the new TP4 bit compare, the ratio-0 7-row case and the 300-replay stress. Controls:
  - the same tests on #63027 rebased (adapted to its runner API; the TP4 compare runs generic against generic);
  - a mutant that flips one bf16 ulp in TP4 K1's residual store. It must fail the TP4 bit compare.
  - PR: numerics TP2 / TP4 / TP8 PASS; layers [2-8] [4-8] [8-8] [8-28] PASS ([4-42] gfx942-only, skipped). Control #63027 rebased: PASS. Mutant: fails the TP4 compare at `ratio 1, 1 x 6`, as expected.
- [x] ABBA at c1 / c2 / c4 (7 / 14 / 28 target rows): 4 rounds, both arms at once on GPUs 0-3 and 4-7, halves swapped (2 rounds each way), 3 runs of 32 prompts per point and server. The PR stays a draft until then, and is dropped if the gain at c1 or c2 is within drift. A gain counts only when every round has the same sign, |mean| > t x SE (t = 3.18 at 4 rounds), and it is larger than the base A/A spread. c4 is reported, not gating.
  - Resolved at c1, c2 and c4: PR faster in 4/4 rounds, |mean| > t x SE and larger than the base A/A spread (table and noise below). The rule above is met.
- [x] GSM8K-1319 with AL (block rejection): 3 passes per server (one cold, two with a per-request `cache_salt`) at `--parallel 6`, so every decode-only step fits mono's 48 rows. 2 servers per arm, halves swapped.
  - base 0.9185 (AL 3.580), PR 0.9158 (AL 3.583), 6 passes each; PR - base -0.0027 (binomial SE of a difference of two independent passes 0.0107); per-question flips between two passes (mean [min-max]): base vs PR 70.4 [57-81] over 36 pairs, within-arm 68.2 [59-79] (base) / 72.0 [63-82] (PR) over 15 pairs each
- [x] Greedy identity probe against #63027 rebased: the first 256 GSM8K questions at `--parallel 1`, compared by token ids, 2 passes per server. A/A pairs (same server, other server) give the noise floor. Each pass also records the accepted and drafted counts, meant as the only exact check of the draft K1 (GSM8K AL sees it only within noise).
  - Two passes of one arm are token-identical on only 65-79 of 256 answers (means 26.1-29.5%, same or another server; why is not investigated), so the probe cannot show identical outputs. Base vs PR: 64-79 of 256 over 16 pairs (mean 28.2%), at the A/A level; 0 PR-consistent differences (answers that differ in every base-vs-PR pair and in no A/A pair).
  - Acceptance counts: confounded. No base-vs-PR pair is token-identical on every answer, so the counts (max |d| 947, A/A floor 716) cannot isolate the draft K1.
- [x] Profiler K1 / K2 attribution: torch-profiler GPU time per decode step of the target's and the draft's K1 and K2 at 7 and 14 rows, on the GSM8K servers (PR once on each half).
  - 7 rows: K1 -277.2 us per step (target -259.9, draft -17.3), K2 +7.5 us; K1 is 98% of the ABBA step delta. 14 rows: K1 -301.2 us (target -281.7, draft -19.5), K2 +28.7 us; K1 is 93% of it.

**Perf (ABBA, 4 rounds)**

| 4x MI355X TP4 `--monokernel`, DSpark k=6, AV off | base (#63027 rebased) | this PR | delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| c1 decode step (ITL p50, ms) | 5.449 | 5.164 | -284 us (-5.2%) |
| c2 decode step (ITL p50, ms) | 6.720 | 6.395 | -326 us (-4.8%) |
| c4 decode step (ITL p50, ms) | 8.676 | 8.482 | -194 us (-2.2%) |

- **Image and workload:** nightly `3966924d56` with main `4b47db922b`'s mono files; base = #63027 rebased onto main (`37372f010c`, with #63576), PR = base + `3d923a6848` (the pushed PR head); random 32k in / 1024 out, `--ignore-eos`, synthetic AL 3.87; 3 x 32 prompts per point and server (seed 100 + 10 x (rep - 1) + c, every rep cold) after a 4-prompt warm-up; 4 rounds, both arms at once on GPUs 0-3 and 4-7, halves swapped between rounds. The images predate #63885 (SWA decode metadata in one launch, now on main), which does not touch the mono files: the absolute us should carry over, the percentages may not.
- **Noise:** c1: SE of the mean delta 1 us (x t 3.18, df 3 = 3 us), A/A (server-mean) spread 0.23% base / 0.29% PR; c2: SE of the mean delta 10 us (x t 3.18, df 3 = 33 us), A/A (server-mean) spread 0.31% base / 0.58% PR; c4: SE of the mean delta 12 us (x t 3.18, df 3 = 38 us), A/A (server-mean) spread 0.73% base / 0.50% PR. Delta = mean over rounds of (PR - base) in the same round.

<details>
<summary>GSM8K per pass, compile-level table, test coverage, reproduction commands</summary>

GSM8K-1319 per pass (8-shot, greedy, `--parallel 6`, real acceptance; one cold pass, then cache-salted ones; at `--parallel 6` every decode-only step fits mono's 48 rows):
- PR: 0.920 / 0.917 / 0.914 / 0.911 / 0.917 / 0.916, AL 3.579 / 3.587 / 3.582 / 3.587 / 3.585 / 3.580
- base: 0.913 / 0.928 / 0.917 / 0.919 / 0.917 / 0.917, AL 3.588 / 3.569 / 3.570 / 3.572 / 3.590 / 3.589 (standard error about 0.0076 per pass)

Compile-only, FlyDSL 0.4.0, gfx950 unless noted:

| | #63027 rebased | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| TP4 K1, ratio 2, 1-48 rows | 142-240 VGPR | 148-174 VGPR, no spill, LDS equal at 48/48 widths; fewer instructions at every width but 2 rows (+6) |
| TP4 K1, 7 / 14 / 48 rows | 152 / 152 / 240 VGPR | 170 / 172 / 174 VGPR |
| TP4 K1, other builds at 7-48 rows (ratio 0/1, index source, fold off, draft) | 152-240 VGPR | 170-174 VGPR, no spill, LDS unchanged |
| TP4 K2, 66 builds (1-48 rows, every ratio, index source, fold off, draft) | | same instruction stream once constants are masked; only 26-27 scratch-offset constants move, by 4,608-8,960 B; VGPR and LDS equal |
| TP8, 47 builds | | binary-identical (and 161/161 TP8 builds binary-identical to main) |
| `generic=True` (50), gfx942 (47), TP4 FFN launch (4) | | binary-identical |
| TP2, 19 builds | | 18 binary-identical. K1 at 48 rows differs by 3 instructions with identical IR; the same flip appears between two builds of one tree (compiler nondeterminism) |

gfx942 K2 at 48 rows fails to build on both trees: gfx942 takes at most 42 rows.

**Test coverage**
- Bit-compared at TP4 on gfx950 (the test is CDNA4-only): the target K1, fold on, at ratio 1 (6 rows), ratio 0 (7) and ratio 2 (12, 36, 48).
- Index-source and fold-off K1 are checked only against the model with a tolerance, in `test_dsv41_mono_layers.py` (TP4 at 8 rows on gfx950; its 42-row case runs on gfx942 only).
- The draft K1 has no unit test, and the acceptance-count check was confounded, so no GPU test checks it exactly; GSM8K AL sees it only within noise (3.580 vs 3.583). Its bit-exactness rests on sharing the target K1's tuned code paths.
- The decode step is timed at 7, 14 and 28 rows (c1 / c2 / c4) only. Steps of 29-48 rows (c5 / c6 at k=6: 35 / 42 rows) are not timed; they have the compile stats above and, at ratio 2, the 36- and 48-row bit compares.
- gfx942 builds are compile-checked only. `timeline=True` (profiling) builds were not compile-checked.

```bash
# Server on 4x MI355X, one per GPU half. For accuracy, use "rejection_sample_method":"block" and drop synthetic_acceptance_length.
# Attribution servers also take --profiler-config '{"profiler":"torch","torch_profiler_dir":"<dir>","torch_profiler_with_stack":false}'.
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA=True \
VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 AITER_TRITON_LOG_LEVEL=ERROR OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 \
VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 \
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 --monokernel --moe-backend aiter \
  --block-size 128 --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --max-cudagraph-capture-size 1024 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --language-model-only \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":false}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":6,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":3.87,"enable_adaptive_verification":false}'

# Perf: fresh server, warm-up (c2, 4 prompts, 32k in / 256 out, seed 7), then 3 runs per point.
# Run r at concurrency c uses --seed 100 + 10 x (r - 1) + c, so every run's prompts are new. Step = ITL p50.
vllm bench serve --backend openai --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 32768 --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos \
  --max-concurrency 1 --num-prompts 32 --seed 101 \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el --metric-percentiles 50,90,99
# c2 / c4: --max-concurrency 2 / 4.

# GSM8K: sglang few_shot_gsm8k prompt and scoring, 1319 questions, 8-shot, temperature 0, max 512 new tokens,
# over /v1/completions, 6 in parallel. One cold pass, then two with a unique "cache_salt" per request.
# Identity probe: the first 256 questions, 1 in parallel, one fixed salt per pass, "return_token_ids".
# AL = 1 + delta(vllm:spec_decode_num_accepted_tokens_total) / delta(vllm:spec_decode_num_drafts_total), read from /metrics.

# Unit tests on 8x MI355X (the TP8 cases need all 8)
pytest -v -s tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_numerics.py tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_layers.py
```
</details>

## Details

**Design**
- #63027's tuned K1 paths (flag copies, norms and gates off the wqkv CTAs, fused fold and slice, wide normed stores, batched norm polls) read no routing dims. At TP4 they apply to every ratio, to fold off, to index sources and to the draft.
- K2 keeps `tuned` (TP2 ratio 2 only). A TP4 tuned K2 hung during FULL capture in an earlier experiment, and that code is gone from #63027's head.

**Scratch**
- K1 and K2 of a width share `_layout(key)`; its K1 regions now follow `tuned_front`.
- The runner keys a scratch by (width, tuned, front), so a front-tuned layout never aliases the FFN launch's generic one.
- The cost is at most 8,960 B per width (48 rows: 11,153,024 -> 11,161,984 B; 14 rows: +5,632 B).
- `build_key()` replaces `tuned()` and the duplicate `MonoBuild` construction in `kernels()`.

**Earlier estimate:** -273 us at c1 and -298 us at c2 (an earlier #63027 K1 revision, one unswapped run per arm); the ABBA above measured -284 us and -326 us.

**Related PRs**
- **#63027** (open, head `d104a70f8d`, conflicts with main): the first three commits here are its commits rebased onto main. When it is rebased, this PR follows. This PR makes two statements in its description stale: "TP4 is not tuned" (TP4 K1 now is), and "every other build ... compiles to the same MLIR as on main" (TP4 K1 is new code; TP4 K2 keeps its instruction stream, but its scratch offsets move). I am happy for this commit to be folded into #63027.
- **#64152** (draft) is stacked on this PR. It changes the gate to `tp in (4, 8)`, so TP8 takes the tuned K1 too.
- **#63892** (sibling, K2 side: batch TP4 K2's X8 copies, load its push's peer bases late) applies cleanly to main, but still conflicts with this stack: 6 hunks in 3 files (the numerics test 1, `layer.py` 1, `stages/moe.py` 4). It gives the same 6 hunks on #63027 rebased alone, so the conflict comes from #63027's commits, not this one. Whichever lands second resolves them.
- **#63486** (draft): it moves this test and reads scratch through `runner.scratch(M)`, which #63027's TP2 ratio-2 steps already break. After this PR the same reads need `build_key(M, ratio)`'s `(tuned, tuned_front)` at TP4 too. Whichever lands second adapts.
- **#61934:** it hoisted K2's FFN-seam loads and was closed with "No e2e gain observed". That is why the ABBA gates this PR.
- No other open PR turns on the tuned K1 at TP4: #63027 is TP2-only, #64152 builds on this PR, and #63892 and #64153 change K2 (TP4 and TP8).

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][DSv4.1] Wire AITER MegaMoE into the V4.1 model
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Enable `--moe-backend aiter_mega_moe` for DeepSeek-V4.1 on ROCm (gfx950, DP+EP with MoRI). The V4 MoE base class already builds the AITER MegaMoE experts, and `config_utils.py` already accepts `DeepseekV41FP8Config` for this backend, but the V4.1 model hard-coded `use_mega_moe = False`, so the backend could not be used.

## Claims

- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash starts and serves with `--moe-backend aiter_mega_moe` at DP8/EP8 on MI355X, including the DSpark draft layers.
- GSM8K accuracy is on par with the existing `aiter` backend (table below).
- No change for any other backend: the new code is gated on `moe_backend == "aiter_mega_moe"`, which V4.1 previously could not reach.

## Validation

MI355X x8, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP1/DP8/EP8, `--moe-backend aiter_mega_moe --all2all-backend mori`, DSpark with 5 draft tokens and block rejection, `--engram-config '{"cpu_offload":false,"embedding_across_dp":true}'`, `MORI_SHMEM_HEAP_SIZE=48G`, `--max-num-batched-tokens 16384`.

| MoE backend | GSM8K strict-match (5-shot, chat, 1319 problems) | flexible-extract | acceptance length |
|---|---|---|---|
| `aiter` | 0.9704 ± 0.0047 | 0.9697 ± 0.0047 | 3.93 |
| `aiter_mega_moe` (this PR) | 0.9735 ± 0.0044 | 0.9727 ± 0.0045 | 3.95 |

The `aiter` row used `--max-num-batched-tokens 8192` (larger budgets hit FlyDSL's 32-bit buffer limit with `aiter` at DP8), the default cadence prefill scheduler and the PR #66500 fix; the `aiter_mega_moe` row used 16384 and the delayer from #65655. The GSM8K task is InferenceX's `gsm8k.yaml` with `--apply_chat_template`, `max_tokens=16384`, `temperature=0`. The numbers above come from the `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly` image at `cf5cea2da`; three further agentic trace-replay runs (AgentX, concurrency 256, 420 s each, ~3,100 successfully completed requests per run) with this change on a later nightly build (`0.33.0rc1.dev1065+g083fbac02`) finished with no engine failures.

Caveats on the evidence:
- I ran this change as a local overlay of the Python tree on top of those nightly builds, together with #65655 (prefill delayer, not relevant to correctness) and #66500 (Engram peer-gather fix, needed for `embedding_across_dp` at DP8). This exact commit has not been re-run on a build of current `main`. Between the tested build and `main`, `model.py` and `dspark.py` differ only in docstring/comment style; `kernel.py` gained unrelated NVIDIA FlashInfer options plus docstring edits, none of which touch this change.
- No performance claim is made here. A like-for-like comparison against the `aiter` backend is in progress and will be posted as a comment.
- No unit test: exercising this needs 8 gfx950 GPUs, MoRI and the 476 GB checkpoint, which the ROCm CI does not provide.

## Details

What changes (all ROCm V4.1):
- `DeepseekV4Model.use_mega_moe` is derived from `kernel_config.moe_backend` instead of being fixed to `False`; the MoE subclass no longer overwrites the flag set by the V4 base class (that overwrite made V4.1 call the generic expert forward on MegaMoE weights).
- Expert weights are mapped with an empty `routed_experts_prefix` under MegaMoE (the V4 model does the same), in both the target and the DSpark draft loaders.
- `finalize_mega_moe_weights` runs after loading for the target and the draft, as it does for V4.
- The router-only `bias_vl` hookup is skipped under MegaMoE, which has no router.
- The `input_ids.to(torch.int64)` cast under MegaMoE is removed: `fused_topk_bias` converts the dtype itself, and the cast makes the decoder-replay graphs fail with `expected scalar type Int but found Long`. GSM8K (which exercises the hash-routed layers) is unchanged without it.
- The `--moe-backend` help text said "DeepSeek-V4 only" and now says V4 and V4.1.

Limitations and notes:
- Requires TP1, PP1, EP on, `--all2all-backend mori` (EPv1), no EPLB; these are the existing V4 checks.
- The shared expert is not fused on V4.1 (V4.1 raises for fused shared experts); it runs unfused on the auxiliary stream.
- `MORI_SHMEM_HEAP_SIZE` needed 48G at `--max-num-batched-tokens 16384` (16G failed with an out-of-heap error); the manager's default of 8G is not enough at that budget. This PR does not change the default.

Not a duplicate: no open PR wires `aiter_mega_moe` into the V4.1 model (searched "DeepSeek V4.1 MegaMoE ROCm", "DSv4.1 aiter_mega_moe", "ROCm DSv4.1 DP expert parallel").

commits.pr_title: [Security] Require native chat encoding in Kimi K3 mode
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Require native XTML chat encoding in `kimi_k3` mode. A generic Hugging Face tokenizer can currently render Jinja through this mode, outside the HF renderer's async timeout.

## Claims

- Reject the generic Jinja fallback before evaluating a template, including during synchronous warmup and async request rendering.
- Preserve the native tokenizer path and document the requirement in the generated tokenizer-mode help.

## Validation

- `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu uv run --no-project .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/renderers/test_kimi_k3.py` — 30 passed, including synchronous rendering and a real `vllm launch render` HTTP test with local tokenizer files.
- On the base commit, the two new regression tests failed. Synchronous rendering did not raise and the HTTP endpoint returned 200 with the rendered token. With the patch, the endpoint returns 400.
- `pre-commit run --files vllm/renderers/kimi_k3.py vllm/config/model.py tests/renderers/test_kimi_k3.py` — passed. Commit hooks also passed.
- The HTTP test exercises the frontend without loading model weights. Full Kimi model inference and accuracy evaluation were not run.

## Details

Both Kimi render paths call `_apply_chat_template()`. The guard there rejects Transformers' inherited Jinja implementation before the tokenizer is called. Tokenizers that supply native chat encoding continue through the existing code path.

Duplicate check: #63463 changes timeout handling in `HfRenderer`. The Kimi rendering changes in #50543 and #51547 address parity and token accounting. Their diffs leave this fallback reachable.

This PR was developed with AI assistance.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][DSv4.1] Avoid runtime JIT of two prefill sparse-attention kernels
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fix runtime JIT of `_block_scores_kernel` and `CombineTopkSwaIndicesKernel.kernel` in DeepSeek-V4.1 serving. Triton specialized both on values that change from step to step, so serving compiled new variants after warmup.

## Claims

- `_block_scores_kernel`: `stride_scores` joins `do_not_specialize`.
- `CombineTopkSwaIndicesKernel`: `query_start_loc_ptr`, `seq_lens_ptr` and `gather_lens_ptr` move to `do_not_specialize_on_alignment`, and the warmup compiles two pointer variants per layer type (`topk_indices` aligned or not) instead of three.
- No change to outputs or to the work the kernels do.

## Validation

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on GB200 with `--jit-monitor-mode warn`: on main, both kernels compile during inference in DEP4 serving (5 of 5 runs); TP4 serving shows neither. With `--jit-monitor-verbose`, every other pointer and specialized stride in the runtime `_block_scores_kernel` key is 16-divisible or constant, which leaves `stride_scores` as the only specialized argument that follows the step's shape.

Runtime JIT before/after on GB200: compile the kernels' registered warmup keys plus one launch of each (startup), call `jit_monitor.activate(mode="warn")`, then launch with new logits widths (33-1537 blocks) and prefill chunk offsets (serving):

```text
# main
Triton kernel JIT compilation during inference: _block_scores_kernel. This causes a latency spike; consider extending warmup to cover this shape/config.
Triton kernel JIT compilation during inference: CombineTopkSwaIndicesKernel.kernel. This causes a latency spike; consider extending warmup to cover this shape/config.

# this PR
(no runtime JIT)
```

Kernel-level check on GB200 (two runs each): `select_candidate_blocks` over full-width rows of 32-1537 blocks with 256-aligned logits, and `combine_topk_swa_indices` with `query_start_loc`/`seq_lens` and `gather_lens` sliced at independent offsets, as prefill chunks pass them.

| | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `_block_scores_kernel` variants compiled | 2 | 1 |
| `CombineTopkSwaIndicesKernel.kernel` variants compiled | 4 | 1 |
| candidate blocks (rows sorted), combined indices and lens | identical | identical |

Candidate rows are compared sorted because `torch.topk` orders tied block scores differently from run to run, on main as well.

## Details

- `_block_scores_kernel` writes `scores[row * stride_scores + block]`. The scores row stride is `nblocks` on the full-width path and `nblocks` rounded up to DeepSelect's alignment otherwise, so it follows each step's logits width; a width in a divisibility class startup did not see compiles a new variant. The hint only aligned the small scores store; the kernel is bound by its logits reads, and the non-divisible variant is what these shapes already run.
- A prefill chunk passes `query_start_loc` and `seq_lens` at `num_decodes + chunk_start` and `gather_lens` at `chunk_start`, so each int32 pointer is 16 B aligned or not independently. The warmup registered 3 of the combinations; mixed DEP steps reach the others. Each program reads one value per request from these pointers, so alignment buys nothing.
- #64001 makes the same `CombineTopkSwaIndicesKernel` change for ROCm; this PR also covers `_block_scores_kernel`.
