commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode][XPU] greedy_argmax: treat NaN as -inf on the torch fallback
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

XPU on main is broken. This PR fixes `greedy_argmax`'s torch fallback to treat NaNs as `-inf`, matching its documented contract and Triton path. This issue was introduced by #57770.

**Notes for Reviewers**

- The fix only touches the torch fallback, which runs on XPU, for fp16, and for small vocabularies. The Triton path that bf16/fp32 models use on CUDA and ROCm is unchanged, so typical deployments see no difference.
- The trade-off is one extra copy of the logits on the fallback path. That's a small cost next to the weights the draft step already reads, and it's the price of getting the same token for the same logits everywhere.
- Turning on the Triton kernel for XPU would avoid that copy, but it needs XPU performance numbers and sign-off from the XPU owners. CPU and non-contiguous inputs would still need this fallback anyway. I kept this PR to the minimal fix so XPU CI is unblocked, and we can address the Triton change in a follow up PR.
- Why not just fix the test? The docstring already promises NaN is treated as -inf, and the Triton path does exactly that. Changing the test instead would let the drafted token depend on the platform and dtype.

## Reproducer

Add `1000` to the existing test's vocab parameters, then run the same command before and after the fallback fix:

```bash
  python -m pytest -v \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_gumbel_sample.py -k test_greedy_argmax_matches_torch
```

## Output on main / on branch

H100 80GB, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130, Triton 3.8.0. Main's two new fallback cases fail at the NaN row; all six Triton cases pass.

```text
Main + test parameter:
============ 2 failed, 6 passed, 22 deselected, 1 warning in 3.69s =============
Branch:
================= 8 passed, 22 deselected, 1 warning in 2.92s ==================
Full file on branch:
======================== 30 passed, 1 warning in 18.08s ========================
```

## Test Plan

The `:intel: (BMG) V1 test` in CI verifies these failures are cleared and the suite reaches later tests. 

<details>
<summary>Implementation and environment</summary>

The fallback uses `masked_fill(isnan, -inf).argmax(-1)`, preserving infinities and first-index ties without modifying inputs. It adds a mask and logits copy only on the fallback. The Triton kernels and gating are unchanged, so eligible BF16/FP32 CUDA/ROCm inputs keep the existing execution path.
</details>

## AI assistance disclosure

Codex (GPT-6) helped draft  this change.

commits.pr_title: [CI][ROCm] Add an AMD mirror for the DeepGEMM kernels step with AITER block-FP8 tests
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The `:nvidia: (H100) DeepGEMM Kernels` step had no AMD counterpart. This adds an MI355 mirror that runs the AITER/ROCm kernels vLLM uses on gfx950 for the same jobs DeepGEMM does on Hopper: block-FP8 GEMM, block-FP8 fused MoE, FP8 group quant, MQA logits and W4A16.

## Claims

- `kernels.yaml`: new `mirror.amd` on `kernels-deepgemm-test-h100` (mi355_1) running `test_rocm_aiter_moe.py`, `test_block_fp8.py` (same command as the H100 step), `test_rocm_aiter_grouped_quant.py`, the `mqa_logits` cases of `test_rocm_triton_attn_dsv4.py`, and the ROCm W4A16 tests.
- `test_block_fp8.py`: new `test_w8a8_block_fp8_aiter_matmul` checks the three AITER blockscale GEMMs vLLM picks on gfx950 (CK, CK bpreshuffle, Triton) against `native_w8a8_block_matmul`, on the same grid as the DeepGEMM case.
- `test_rocm_aiter_moe.py`: new `test_aiter_fused_moe_block_fp8_accuracy` covers the 128x128 block-FP8 MoE path (`AiterFp8BlockExperts`) on three shapes that hit the CK 2-stage and both ASM 1-stage kernels, against the DeepGEMM MoE reference `torch_w8a8_block_fp8_moe` (which gains a `quant_fn` argument, default unchanged).
- Each moved test runs exactly once on MI355: the legacy MI355 MoE, Quantization and Attention groups in `test-amd.yaml` stop collecting them, and the FP4/INT4 MoE steps drop their `test_rocm_aiter_moe.py` subset, which the mirror now runs in full.

## Validation

MI350X (gfx950), 1 GPU, from `tests/`:

```bash
pytest -v -s kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_moe.py
pytest -v -s kernels/quantization/test_block_fp8.py
pytest -v -s kernels/quantization/test_rocm_aiter_grouped_quant.py
pytest -v -s kernels/attention/test_rocm_triton_attn_dsv4.py -k mqa_logits
pytest -v -s kernels/quantization/test_w4a16_kernel_selection.py kernels/quantization/test_triton_w4a16.py kernels/quantization/test_rocm_compressed_tensors_w4a16.py
```

| Command | 10 runs in a row | After rebasing on current main |
|---|---|---|
| `test_rocm_aiter_moe.py` | 10/10, 91 passed | 10/10, 92 passed |
| `test_block_fp8.py` | 10/10, 521 passed, 260 skipped | 521 passed, 260 skipped |
| `test_rocm_aiter_grouped_quant.py` | 10/10, 3 passed | 3 passed |
| `test_rocm_triton_attn_dsv4.py -k mqa_logits` | 10/10, 4 passed | 4 passed |
| W4A16 (3 files) | 10/10, 24 passed | 24 passed |

The 10-run loop was on main 266e163d1e. After rebasing on 5629b26146 every command passed again, and `test_rocm_aiter_moe.py`, where the new test had to follow the AITER `QuantType` rename from #65517, passed 10 more times in a row (main added one test to that file, hence 92). All 300 new AITER GEMM cases and the 3 new block-FP8 MoE cases pass. The 260 skips in `test_block_fp8.py` are the existing DeepGEMM, FlashInfer, CUTLASS, b12x and SM90 `torch._scaled_mm` cases, which need CUDA-only libraries. A collection-only check on gfx950 confirms the legacy MI355 groups drop exactly the items the mirror runs (4 attention, 92 MoE, 813 quantization), so nothing is lost or run twice. The mirror takes about 10 minutes, under its 35 minute timeout. pre-commit is clean on the changed files.

## Details

The tolerances come from the kernels. AITER's tuned CK blockscale configs with split-K reduce partial sums into the bf16 output with atomics: on the same kernel instance at 1x512x4096 the mean relative error goes from 6e-6 (no split) to 1.8e-3, 2.5e-3 and 3.5e-3 for split-K 1, 2 and 3, and the worst over 20 repeats of 100 shapes is 3.9e-3 for CK and 3.6e-3 for CK bpreshuffle. So the CK paths use 0.005 while Triton keeps DeepGEMM's 0.001 (worst seen 2.7e-5). For MoE, AITER keeps the stage-1 output and SiLU in fp32 and requantizes with torch rounding, so the reference does the same: fp32 input and `native_per_token_group_quant_fp8`. With the bf16 path and vLLM's group-quant kernel in the reference, the 1335x4608x7168 shape fails DeepGEMM's 0.035 tolerance, because a 1-ULP tie difference on about 0.05% of elements gets amplified by the fp8 requant chain. With the matched reference the worst error-to-tolerance ratio is 0.55 on the three shapes and 0.97 across 8 shapes x 4 seeds x 3 repeats.

The new tests are gated on gfx950/OCP e4m3fn. MI300 (gfx942) keeps running these files through its own MoE, Quantization and Attention mirrors. Some DeepGEMM coverage has no AITER counterpart and stays uncovered on AMD: masked batched MoE experts (`test_batched_deepgemm.py`) and the FP4 branch of paged MQA logits.

No open PR adds an AMD mirror for this step or tests the AITER blockscale GEMMs or block-FP8 MoE for accuracy. I searched open PRs for "deepgemm mirror amd", "AITER block fp8 gemm test", "AITER MoE block fp8 accuracy" and the new test names. #64142 changes how AITER picks between plain and preshuffled blockscale GEMMs and adds selection tests, but it does not test kernel accuracy, so the two fit together. Draft #62233 regenerates `test-amd.yaml`. If it lands first, the `test-amd.yaml` hunks here can be dropped.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Mamba] Support Mamba cache stochastic rounding on gfx950
commits.pr_body:
- `mamba_ssm.py`: on ROCm, `convert_rs_fp16x2` lowers to gfx950's `v_cvt_sr_f16_f32` instead of the PTX `cvt.rs.f16x2.f32`.
- `mamba.py` (config): `--enable-mamba-cache-stochastic-rounding` is accepted on gfx950 and rejected on other ROCm archs with a clear error. CUDA checks are unchanged.
- `utils.py` (tests): shared `requires_triton_stochastic_rounding` mark (CC 10.0 or gfx950), used by the existing SSU stochastic rounding test.
- `test_mamba_ssm.py`: new `test_stochastic_rounding_is_unbiased`. Each draw has to land on an fp16 neighbor of x, and the mean over 4096 draws has to converge to x. Both platforms run it.
- `test_replayssm_standard_decode_mamba2.py`: stochastic rounding cases for the Triton ReplaySSM decode path.
- `kernels.yaml`: new `:amd: (MI355) Mamba SSM Kernels` step. The existing Mamba kernel mirror runs on MI250, where every stochastic rounding test is skipped.

Stochastic rounding of the fp16 Mamba SSM cache only worked on Blackwell, because the Triton kernels used the `cvt.rs` PTX instruction. gfx950 has a hardware equivalent, so MI350/MI355 can run the same FP16-state configs (for example the Nemotron-3-Super ReplaySSM + prefix caching setup) that NVIDIA runs with `--enable-mamba-cache-stochastic-rounding`. The two instructions read different bits of the random word. `cvt.rs.f16x2` uses bits [12:0] and [28:16], one 13-bit field per half, while `v_cvt_sr_f16_f32` rounds one value at a time using bits [31:19]. So the ROCm path passes the full Philox word and does not reuse the CUDA bit slicing. A probe matched every hardware output bit for bit against an exact model of that rule. Over 8192 draws per value, mean bias was +4.5e-5 ulp on gfx950 and -2.2e-4 ulp for an emulation of CUDA `cvt.rs` fed the same Philox bits. The new unbiasedness test fails for plain round-to-nearest (max mean bias 0.50 ulp) and for the wrong bit slice `rand >> 19` (1.00 ulp), so it catches both mistakes on either platform. This is not a duplicate: open PR searches for "stochastic rounding", "v_cvt_sr", "convert_rs_fp16x2" and "mamba gfx950" returned no ROCm stochastic rounding work. #40012 touches `convert_rs_fp16x2` for CUDA cache dtypes only.

### Validation (MI355X, gfx950)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `pytest -v -s kernels/mamba/test_mamba_ssm.py kernels/mamba/test_replayssm_standard_decode_mamba2.py` (the new CI step), 10 runs in a row | 10/10: 422 passed, 2 skipped each time. The 2 skips are the existing `test_selective_scan_varlen` padding cases, which skip on every platform. All 19 stochastic rounding tests (16 SSU, 1 unbiasedness, 2 ReplaySSM) ran and passed |
| Same command once more after rebasing onto current `main` | 422 passed, 2 skipped |
| `pytest tests/test_config.py -k "mamba or replayssm"` | 10 passed |
| GSM8K, Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-FP8, TP2+EP, Triton ReplaySSM + prefix caching, fp16 state, `--enable-mamba-cache-stochastic-rounding --mamba-cache-philox-rounds 5` (`evals/gsm8k/test_gsm8k_correctness.py`, threshold 0.93), 3 runs | 0.9363 / 0.9333 / 0.9340 (all passed). Same config with round-to-nearest fp16 state, 10 runs: mean 0.9327, sd 0.0038 |

Kernel cost (MI355X, Nemotron-3-Super geometry, headdim 64, dstate 128, fp16 state):

| Kernel | batch 1 | batch 16 | batch 64 | batch 256 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `selective_state_update`, SR off / on (us) | 39.8 / 52.0 | 43.0 / 53.7 | 73.4 / 91.1 | 327.0 / 402.4 |
| ReplaySSM flush step, SR off / on (us) | 79.9 / 91.7 | 80.6 / 97.0 | 79.2 / 89.0 | 155.9 / 200.6 |

Stochastic rounding is opt-in, so default paths are unchanged. The slowdown comes from Philox generation and the extra registers, not from the conversion: on 134M elements, `v_cvt_sr_f16_f32` takes 165.0 us and round-to-nearest takes 165.9 us.

Related: the #66315 CLI test needs `is_rocm` patched too once both land, and the #66316 ReplaySSM MI355 mirror can then add `--enable-mamba-cache-stochastic-rounding`.

commits.pr_title: [Quantization] Support compressed-tensors MXFP6 (mxfp6-pack-quantized)
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Load compressed-tensors `mxfp6-pack-quantized` checkpoints: MXFP6 (E2M3) weights with dynamic MXFP8 or 16-bit activations, routed to the existing MXFP6 linear kernels (Humming on CUDA). This follows @gau-nernst's [Qwen3.8-27B-MXFP6](https://huggingface.co/gaunernst/Qwen3.8-27B-MXFP6) Quark checkpoint, which showed MXFP6 MLPs + MXFP8 elsewhere fit a 27B model on a 32 GB GPU.

Bumps `compressed-tensors` from 0.17.0 to 0.20.1, the release line that ships MXFP6 (vllm-project/compressed-tensors#941: `num_bits=6` float = E2M3, `mxfp6-pack-quantized` format, `MXFP6A8`/`MXFP6A16` presets). LLM Compressor examples are in vllm-project/llm-compressor#3286.

## Claims

- New `CompressedTensorsW6A8Mxfp6` scheme for MXFP6 weights (4 values packed in 3 bytes, uint8 E8M0 scales, group 32). It takes its activation precision from the checkpoint: dynamic MXFP8 or none; anything else raises.
- Mixed MXFP6/MXFP8/FP8 compressed-tensors checkpoints (e.g. Qwen3.8-27B) load and run with torch.compile and CUDA graphs at TP=1 and TP=2.
- The packed layout is byte-identical to the Quark MXFP6 export that the Humming path already serves.
- Existing compressed-tensors checkpoints keep working on 0.20.1. Group/dynamic `actorder` checkpoints are still rejected, now by compressed-tensors itself while parsing.

## Validation

[nm-testing/Qwen3.8-27B-MXFP6A8](https://huggingface.co/nm-testing/Qwen3.8-27B-MXFP6A8): MXFP6A8 MLP + MXFP8 attention/GDN/MTP + FP8 per-channel `lm_head`, made with LLM Compressor's `model_free_ptq` (RTN, no calibration). GSM8K on one B300, `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`, 5-shot, temperature 0, 1319 questions, `vllm serve <model> --max-model-len 8192 --language-model-only`, on this branch:

| Model | Runs | GSM8K mean (range) | Invalid |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B (BF16) | 2 | 0.780 (0.777-0.783) | 0.000 |
| nm-testing/Qwen3.8-27B-MXFP6A8 | 5 | 0.752 (0.742-0.760) | 0.005-0.011 |

Scores vary between runs at temperature 0, so compare means. MXFP6A8 costs about 0.03 versus BF16. The same checkpoint on this PR's previous base (Humming 0.1.16, compressed-tensors 0.20.1) scored 0.759 (0.756-0.763, 3 runs), within run-to-run spread of this branch. An earlier revision of this PR reported 0.770 from a single run, which those repeats did not reproduce.

- Kernel selection: MXFP6 linears use `HummingMxFp6LinearKernel`, MXFP8 linears use `FlashInferCutedslMxfp8LinearKernel`, at TP=1 and TP=2. TP=2 smoke: 300 GSM8K questions, 0.740, no errors.
- Layout check (previous base, packing unchanged): given the same scales, the compressed-tensors packed weights are byte-identical to `gaunernst/Qwen3.8-27B-MXFP6`, and `humming.ops.weight.unpack_weight(..., 6)` decodes the same codes.
- `pytest tests/quantization/test_compressed_tensors.py` on B300 (SM103), compressed-tensors 0.20.1: 55 of 60 pass, including `test_compressed_tensors_mxfp6` ([nm-testing/Qwen3-0.6B-MXFP6A8](https://huggingface.co/nm-testing/Qwen3-0.6B-MXFP6A8)) and `test_compressed_tensors_mxfp4`. The 5 failures also fail with compressed-tensors 0.17.0 on the same tree, so they are not from the bump: `test_compressed_tensors_w8a8_logprobs[False-10-4-...]`, `no_enforce_eager`, `w4a8_fp8`, `transforms_perplexity`, `fp8_block_enabled[auto]`. The errors seen include `Int8 not supported on SM103` and no W4A8 scheme on this architecture; these need CI to confirm on the expected hardware. `test_compressed_tensors_moe_ignore_with_model` failed once and passed on rerun.

## Details

- Mirrors `CompressedTensorsW4A4Mxfp4` (packed `weight_packed` renamed to `weight` after loading) and reuses `init_mxfp6_linear_kernel`. The packed dim shards cleanly under TP because K per partition stays a multiple of 32.
- **Limitation:** MXFP6A8 needs Humming. `EmulationMxfp6LinearKernel` does not accept MXFP8 activations, so without Humming (e.g. ROCm) MXFP6A8 fails at load with "Failed to find a kernel"; weight-only `MXFP6A16` can use emulation.
- The scheme is named `W6A8` like the other MX schemes, and also serves weight-only (`MXFP6A16`) checkpoints.
- compressed-tensors 0.20 breaking changes checked against vLLM: `QuantizationArgs` rejects `actorder` group/dynamic/True while parsing, which made vLLM's guard unreachable, so it is removed and the test matches the new error. Python >=3.11 matches vLLM's floor, `psutil` is already a dependency, and vLLM does not serialize `QuantizationArgs` or subclass `OffloadCache`.
- Not a duplicate: no open vLLM PRs cover compressed-tensors MXFP6 or bump this pin. Existing MXFP6 support is Quark-only.
- AI assistance (Claude Code) was used. I reviewed the diff and ran the validation above.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][MoE] Skip DP padding rows in TRT-LLM monolithic MoE with vLLM's top-k
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## 1. Why this change

Under data parallelism (DP), every DP rank pads its batch to the largest batch on any rank. The FlashInfer TRT-LLM **monolithic** MoE kernels are the default on Blackwell for block-FP8 and MXFP8 checkpoints. They route from the router logits themselves, so padded rows pick experts like real tokens, and the kernel loads and computes those experts.

`VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING` (on by default) cannot help here. It works by having vLLM's routers write expert id -1 for padded rows, and the monolithic kernels never call vLLM's routers.

Padding under DP is large:
- In decode steps with up to 32 rows per rank, 34-65% of rows are padding.
- In mixed (prefill + decode) steps, 37-84% of rows are padding, because every rank pads to the rank running prefill.

## 2. What this PR changes

Under DP, the runner routes with vLLM's top-k, where padded rows get -1, and then calls the kernel's precomputed-routing op (`trtllm_fp8_block_scale_routed_moe`), which skips those rows. There is no new option: the existing `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING=0` turns it off (its doc comment now says so).

- `FusedMoEExpertsMonolithic.apply_precomputed_routing` and `supports_precomputed_routing`, implemented for TRT-LLM block FP8 and MXFP8 (`TrtLlmFp8ExpertsMonolithic`). The kwargs shared with the logits call move to one helper.
- `prepare_routed` for the NaiveDPEP monolithic prepare/finalize: it all-gathers top-k ids and weights instead of logits.
- `MoERunner` takes the routed path under DP.
  - Routers that do not mask padding themselves (`masks_padding` False, e.g. grouped top-k outside DeepEP v2) get the mask applied after top-k in the runner.
  - Routed-expert capture receives the gathered top-k ids, in the same layout as the monolithic kernel's `routing_replay_out`.
  - `routed_scaling_factor` is applied exactly once, as on the modular path: either by the router on the weights or by the runner on the output. The routed kernel call gets `None`.
- FlashInfer autotune tunes the op that runs. Under DP, the autotune cache key now records that the routed op is used, so a cache saved before this PR (which has only the logits op) does not hit and skip tuning. Only models with a MoE layer that can take the routed path get the new key; every other deployment keeps its key and its saved cache.

## 3. When the new path runs

Every MoE forward of the target model where all of these hold:
- Blackwell (SM100) with block-FP8 or MXFP8 MoE weights;
- DP > 1, either with EP and the default `allgather_reducescatter` all2all backend (DeepEP and other all2all backends use modular kernels and are unaffected), or without EP (the MoE layer is then TP-sharded across the DP ranks and always uses the naive DP all-gather, whatever the all2all backend);
- no EPLB and no sequence parallel;
- a routing method the TRT-LLM monolithic FP8 kernel supports;
- `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING` on (the default);
- the routing simulator (`VLLM_MOE_ROUTING_SIMULATION_STRATEGY`) off. The simulator works by feeding the kernel synthetic logits, so it keeps the logits op.

The decision depends only on DP size, so every DP rank takes the same path. This matters because the two paths dispatch different tensors in the all-gather.

| router | models | validation |
|---|---|---|
| softmax top-k (`FusedTopKRouter`) | Qwen3 MoE, Qwen3-Next / 3.5 / 3.8 FP8 | unit tests + serving (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8) |
| sigmoid + bias (`FusedTopKBiasRouter`, MiniMax2) | MiniMax-M2 / M3 | unit tests + serving (MiniMax-M3-MXFP8) |
| grouped top-k (`GroupedTopKRouter`, DeepSeekV3 routing) | DeepSeek-V3/R1, Kimi-K2, GLM-4.5+ FP8 | unit test vs the kernel's own grouped routing + serving (GLM-5.3-FP8, DP8 + EP) |

**No size threshold.** The top-k launch is a fixed cost per MoE layer. A threshold on batch size would leave out mixed steps, which are the most padded, and would need tuning per model. The cost of having none is on small-expert models at high concurrency (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, section 4.2): some large decode steps are slower, while throughput stays within noise. A FlashInfer-side padding mask would remove the top-k launch: flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#9000. The runner could then pass the mask instead.

### 3.1 Why only under DP + EP, not TP

**In short:** TP pads almost nothing, so the top-k launch has nothing to save. Forcing the path on under TP4 gives no throughput gain (table below), so it runs only with DP. All DP measurements in this PR are DP + EP; DP without EP also takes the path but is not measured here.

How much of the MoE input is padding. For each step: padded rows / all rows the MoE layers process, summed over DP ranks (TP has one), i.e. 1 - real tokens / (DP ranks x padded batch per rank). Averaged over the steps of Baseline serving runs. Steps are grouped by kind and by the padded batch per rank:

| step kind | DP4 / DP8 (Qwen, M3, GLM) | TP4 (Qwen, M3) |
|---|---|---|
| decode, <=32 rows | 34-65% | 0-0.4% |
| decode, 33-512 rows | 11-22% | 2-5% |
| mixed (prefill + decode) | 37-84% | 4-16% |

In the kernel table (section 4.3), the top-k path loses at 0% padding and only breaks even around 20%.

To check, I forced the same path on under TP4 (a local patch, not in this PR) with MiniMax-M3-MXFP8, which has the largest experts of the three models and so is the best case for this path. Each side was launched twice. Measured on an earlier base (871147447b); the TP path is unchanged since.

| concurrency | throughput, tok/s: Baseline | top-k path forced on | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 791 / 875 | 836 / 862 | +1.9% (within noise) |
| 16 | 1730 / 1681 | 1634 / 1766 | -0.3% (within noise) |
| 64 | 4177 / 4404 | 4308 / 4481 | +2.4% (within noise) |

## 4. Measured results

Summary:
- **Higher serving throughput for large-expert models under DP + EP:** GLM-5.3-FP8 (DP8) +9% / +26% / +27% at concurrency 8 / 16 / 64; MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 (DP4) +13% / +4% / +5% at concurrency 4 / 16 / 64. Both runs better at every concurrency for both models.
- **Small-expert models break even on throughput, with slower large decode steps:** Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 (4.9M-parameter experts, DP4) throughput is within noise at concurrency 4 to 256 (+2.1% / +1.2% / +5.5% / -0.7%). Small decode steps get faster (-4% to -17%), but large decode steps get slower in both runs: +6.4% for 33-128 rows per rank at concurrency 64, and +13.2% (33-128 rows) and +6.6% (129-512 rows) at concurrency 256. Those buckets are 18% and 16% of step time.
- **Accuracy unchanged** on all three router types (softmax top-k, sigmoid + bias, grouped top-k).
- **No gain without DP:** forcing the path on under TP4 does not change throughput beyond noise (section 3.1), so it runs only under DP.
- **Opt-out:** `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING=0` restores main's behavior on this path. It also turns off padding skip on the modular MoE paths, as it already does on main.

Terms:
- **Baseline** = upstream main at this PR's base commit; **After PR** = this change.
- **Concurrency** = requests in flight in `vllm bench serve` (`--max-concurrency`), summed over all DP ranks.
- **Step time** = wall time of one engine step, from a per-step timestamp log on DP rank 0 (a local patch, not in this PR). **decode** steps replay a full CUDA graph; **mixed** steps also run prefill and use piecewise graphs.
- **Rows per rank** = the padded batch size per DP rank.
- Each side was launched twice. **(both runs better)** / **(both runs worse)**: both After PR launches beat (or lost to) both Baseline launches. **(within noise)**: the two sides' values interleave.

Setup:
- GB200, FlashInfer 0.7.3 (main's pin), `vllm bench serve` on ShareGPT, temperature 0.
- Baseline = main 80e0cd68f8, After PR = f13ec7ed53 (this PR on that main; the last commit only changes the routing-simulator case of the autotune key and tests). All runs in one session, launch order Baseline, After PR, After PR, Baseline on one node (two nodes for GLM).
- All three models run with speculative decoding (MTP 3 for Qwen and GLM, EAGLE3 3 for M3), so verification batches also take the new path.
- Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8: DP4 + EP, FlashInfer autotune on. MiniMax-M3-MXFP8: DP4 + EP, autotune off. GLM-5.3-FP8: DP8 + EP on two nodes, autotune off on both sides (section 5).

<details>
<summary>Serve commands</summary>

```bash
# Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8, DP4 + EP
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 --data-parallel-size 4 --tensor-parallel-size 1 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-num-seqs 256 --max-model-len 32768 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --attention-config.indexer_kv_dtype fp8 --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
# MiniMax-M3-MXFP8, DP4 + EP
vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 --data-parallel-size 4 --tensor-parallel-size 1 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-num-seqs 256 --max-model-len 32768 --block-size 128 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHINFER","use_trtllm_attention":true,"indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8","minimax_m3_msa_decode_backend":"cutlass"}' \
  --kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune":false}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"eagle3","model":"<m3-eagle3>","num_speculative_tokens":3,"attention_backend":"FLASHINFER","use_local_argmax_reduction":true}'
# GLM-5.3-FP8, DP8 + EP over two nodes (4 local ranks each)
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3 --data-parallel-size 8 --data-parallel-size-local 4 --tensor-parallel-size 1 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-num-seqs 256 --max-model-len 32768 --tokenizer-mode glm5_next --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune":false}' --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
# Benchmark (ShareGPT, 4-6 prompts per unit of concurrency, at least 32)
vllm bench serve --dataset-name sharegpt --temperature 0 --max-concurrency <C> --num-prompts <N> --seed 0
```
</details>

### 4.1 Correctness

Unit tests:

```
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_routing.py tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_naive_dp_ep_dbo.py tests/kernels/moe/test_grouped_topk.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_routing_simulator.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_routed_experts_capture_monolithic.py \
  tests/model_executor/test_flashinfer_autotune_warmup.py
```

On this PR head (a7442ffcf4), one GB200: 1345 passed, 2 skipped (a column-major-scale case that only applies to [128, 128] blocks), 0 failed.

New tests:
- `test_trtllm_fp8_monolithic_routed_skips_padding[block / mxfp8 / block-grouped]`: on one GPU, on the same quantized input, the experts' routed op equals the monolithic op (the kernel's own routing) on real rows and gives zero on padded rows. Routers covered:
  - softmax top-k (block FP8);
  - sigmoid + bias with routed scaling 2.0 (MXFP8);
  - DeepSeek-V3 grouped top-k (8 groups, top-4 groups, sigmoid + bias, routed scaling 2.5; block FP8).

  Breaking the scaling on the vLLM side makes the grouped case fail.
- `test_runner_routes_dp_padding_rows_to_no_expert[router masks / runner masks]`: under DP the runner passes int32 top-k to the routed op with padding rows at -1, both when the router masks them (real fused top-k router) and when the runner has to. Removing the runner's mask fails the second case.
- `test_runner_prepares_monolithic_logits[dp 1 / 4]`: the routing simulator still feeds the kernel its synthetic logits under DP.
- NaiveDPEP `prepare_routed` all-gathers top-k ids and weights, not logits.
- Grouped top-k outside DeepEP v2 reports `masks_padding` False.
- The autotune cache key changes under DP only for models with a routed-capable MoE layer, and not under the routing simulator.

`test_flashinfer.py` (the routed-vs-logits kernel test, SM100 only) runs in the B200 Kernels CI step, which this PR's files do not trigger, so it runs there only on full or nightly builds; I ran it on GB200 (result above). The other files run in existing MoE and model-executor steps.

GSM8K, 1319 questions, 5-shot. At low concurrency (4 for DP4, 8 for DP8) each DP rank has about one request, so nearly every decode step is mostly padding and takes the new path; at concurrency 256, prefill and mixed steps do too. The models are not deterministic under DP, so I also compare per-question answers across runs:

- at small batches, the experts that only padded rows select;
- at large batches, the padded rows' GEMM rows.

Mixed steps under DP are mostly padding (37-84% of rows across the three models), because every rank pads to the rank running prefill.
- GLM-5.3 (38M-parameter experts) and MiniMax-M3 (57M) save far more than the top-k costs.
- Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (4.9M parameters, 512 experts) saves little per row. Its large decode steps are only 11-22% padding, so there the top-k launch costs more than it saves.

Frontier models deployed with DP + EP have experts of 25-66M parameters (DeepSeek-V3/V4, Kimi-K2/K3, GLM-5, MiniMax-M3, Qwen3.8-2.4T), i.e. the GLM / M3 side.

### 4.3 Kernel view

<details>
<summary>One MoE call, top-k + routed op vs logits op</summary>

Single GB200, EP layout as served (Qwen: 128 of 512 experts, M3: 32 of 128, GLM: 32 of 256), random logits, CUDA graph, median of 5 x 50 replays, FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1. M is rows across all DP ranks. Change in us per call (negative = faster):

| padded share | Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (M 8-4096) | MiniMax-M3 (M 8-4096) | GLM-5.3 (M 16-8192) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0% | +2 to +14 (+4% to +11%) | +3 to +21 (+1% to +6%) | +1 to +15 (+1% to +3%) |
| 20% | -2 to +9 | -1 to -25 | +2 to -140 |
| 50% | +7 to -66 | -18 to -53 | -8 to -359 |
| 75% | +2 to -72 | -27 to -119 | -19 to -553 |
</details>

### 4.4 Autotune cache key

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 DP4 with autotune on: main and this PR write different cache directories (`153f2d40…` vs `a4700ae6…`). This PR's cache holds entries for the routed op (top-k id/weight inputs) as well as the logits op, which the draft model's MoE layer still uses (below); main's holds only the logits op. After upgrading, a DP deployment of a block-FP8 / MXFP8 TRT-LLM MoE model retunes once at its first start; other deployments keep their key.

## 5. Limitations

- Only block-FP8 / MXFP8 TRT-LLM monolithic experts. NVFP4 monolithic is not selected under DP + EP; the NVFP4 modular kernel is, and the modular path already uses vLLM's routing and masks padding. FP8 per-tensor, BF16 and MXFP4 keep the kernel's routing.
- DP without EP takes the same path (same padding, same all-gather, TP-sharded experts) but is not measured in this PR.
- Small-expert models: large decode steps are slower (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next +6% to +13% at concurrency 64 / 256), with throughput within noise. `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING=0` turns the path off, together with padding skip on the modular paths.
- Draft-model forward passes do not mark padding (the forward context has `is_padding` only under PCP), so MoE layers in MTP drafters keep the kernel's own routing, as on main.
- GLM-5.3-FP8 runs with FlashInfer autotune off on both sides: with autotune on, main crashed at startup on this config in earlier tests (illegal memory access in the TRT-LLM routing kernel during the autotune dummy runs); this is pre-existing and tracked separately.

## 6. Not a duplicate

I searched open PRs for padding / monolithic / routed MoE / precomputed routing.
- #50759 (draft) masks padding in vLLM's routers, i.e. the modular path; it does not reach the monolithic kernels. The only overlap is masking padding after top-k for routers that cannot fuse it; this PR does that inline in the runner's routed path.
- #54109 (DeepEP v2 padded format) and #57946 (b12x padding sentinel) are other paths.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to write this change and run the experiments. I reviewed every changed line and the measurements.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Fix non-deferred structured-output draft retrieval
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fix a bug affecting spec decode + structured outputs under async scheduling, where the EngineCore does not retrieve the real draft token ids from the worker before computing the grammar bitmask, leading to a failed request and `500: Internal Server error`.

## Claims

Suppose PP=1 + async scheduling + spec decode, suppose request `p` requiring structured outputs is scheduled in batch A, skipped for batch B but remains RUNNING, and scheduled again in batch C. In step C, it will take the non-deferred sampling path and will not retrieve draft tokens from batch A. Grammar bitmask are then computed from `-1` placeholders instead of the real draft tokens, leading to grammar-invalid generation and `"Unexpected: grammar rejected tokens %s for request %s"`.

The non-deferred path can be most easily reached when model generation nears `max_model_len` (see repro below). I think it can also occur under KV pressure in P/D and KV offloading deployments. `Scheduler.defer_block_free` and `KVConnectorBase_V1.has_pending_block_frees()` can shortcut preemption, leaving requests RUNNING but unscheduled.

See "Details" for more background and code trace.

## Validation

Ran on H100.

Repro:
```
.venv/bin/vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-4B  \
--speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"RedHatAI/Qwen3-4B-speculator.dspark","num_speculative_tokens":7}'   \
--max-model-len 20

curl -sS http://localhost:8000/v1/completions   -H 'Content-Type: application/json'   -d '{
    "prompt": "Return only the JSON object required by the output constraint.",
    "temperature": 0,
    "structured_outputs": {"regex": "\\{\"v\":\"x\"\\}"}
  }'
```

On main, the request fails with:
```
(EngineCore pid=3266911) ERROR 11-06 04:16:14 [scheduler.py:2475] Unexpected: grammar rejected tokens [788, 330, 16] for request cmpl-802fafd32fa38c7c-0-8cca2192. Terminating request.
(APIServer pid=3265988) ERROR 11-06 04:16:14 [serving.py:203] Request cmpl-802fafd32fa38c7c failed with an internal error during generation
INFO:     127.0.0.1:40586 - "POST /v1/completions HTTP/1.1" 500 Internal Server Error
```

With the fix, the request succeeds, returning the correctly constrained output:
```
{"id":"cmpl-b0eb899cdb680c05","object":"text_completion","created":1793956679,"model":"Qwen/Qwen3-4B","choices":[{"index":0,"text":"{\"v\":\"x\"}","logprobs":null,"finish_reason":"stop","stop_reason":null,"token_ids":null,"prompt_logprobs":null,"prompt_token_ids":null,"routed_experts":null,"weight_versions":null}],"service_tier":null,"system_fingerprint":"vllm-0.33.0rc1.dev752+g1b16698eb0e5719412ecc3b2c7a05afad4d02354-2af0d37d","usage":{"prompt_tokens":11,"total_tokens":18,"completion_tokens":7,"completion_tokens_details":null},"kv_transfer_params":null,"ec_transfer_params":null,"metrics":null}
```

`tests/v1/e2e/general/test_async_scheduling.py::test_async_spec_decode_structured_output` is essentially the same test to be run in CI. On main, it fails with `AssertionError: assert 'error' == 'stop'`.

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -vs -m 'cpu_test' tests/v1/core

908 passed, 343 deselected

.venv/bin/python -m pytest -vs -m 'not cpu_test' tests/v1/core tests/v1/worker tests/v1/e2e/general/test_async_scheduling.py

1469 passed, 145 skipped, 941 deselected

.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s -m 'not cpu_test' \
  tests/v1/engine \
  --ignore=tests/v1/engine/test_preprocess_error_handling.py \
  --deselect=tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core.py::test_engine_core_tp

315 passed, 1 skipped, 62 deselected
```

https://gist.github.com/yzong-rh/e15dc602fbfd11e2b64c2d41527a1a72
Qwen/Qwen3-4B + RedHatAI/Qwen3-4B-speculator.dspark + 8 draft tokens + async scheduling + structured outputs.
Ran on 1 x B200.
- broad vs tight constraints: less vocab masked vs more vocab masked
- c1 vs c64: low vs high concurrency

```
.venv/bin/python run.py --output ... --pipeline-parallel-size ... --num-repeats 10
```

Workload | Baseline | Fix | Change
-- | -- | -- | --
broad, c=1 | 1082.0 | 1076.6 | −0.50%
broad, c=64 | 16601.2 | 16632.3 | +0.19%
tight, c=1 | 1627.7 | 1620.3 | −0.45%
tight, c=64 | 32677.9 | 32642.1 | −0.11%

Results not stat-sig

## Details

Suppose PP=1, async scheduling, and spec decode are used, batch queue size will be 2 (two batches can be inflight concurrently). Suppose some request `p` uses structured outputs.

### Deferred sampling path (not buggy)
The following normally occurs inside `EngineCore.step_with_batch_queue`:
- Step A: `p` is RUNNING and scheduled in a batch
- Step B: `p` is RUNNING and scheduled again, but since `p` needs the draft tokens from step A for `grammar_bitmask` constraints, it will defer sampling.
  - It will instead wait for Step A to finish and retire the request. It will retreive the draft tokens via `model_executor.take_draft_token_ids` to generate the bitmasks before dispatching step B sampling.
  - This is the deferred sampling path taken when there are `pending_structured_output_tokens`.

### Non-deferred sampling path (buggy)
However, there's no guarantee that Step B will schedule request `p`:
- Step A: `p` is RUNNING and scheduled in a batch
- Step B: `p` remains RUNNING but not scheduled
- Step C: Batch A is awaited on and retired due to batch queue size limit. Only after is `p` scheduled again.
  - Because Batch A has been retired, there batch C no longer has `pending_structured_output_tokens`. The deferred path is not taken.
  - The non-deferred path however never calls `model_executor.take_draft_token_ids` to retrieve `p`'s real draft tokens. Gramamr bitmask is generated from `-1` placeholders and could be incorrect.
  - When batch C eventually retires, grammar-invalid generation will cause "Unexpected: grammar rejected tokens %s for request %s", failing the request.

Cases where step A schedules `p` but step B skips it are rare, but can occur when:
- `p`'s generation is near the `max_model_len`. So step B does not have the budget to reschedule `p` until step A rejected some draft tokens and been retired, freeing up budget for `p` in step C.
- Preemption is shortcutted (no more RUNNING requests can be scheduled or pre-empted for that step) leaving RUNNING requests unscheduled. This notably occur with KVConnectors:
  - For P/D deployments, `Scheduler.defer_block_free` fences blocks belonging to inflight steps and preventing preemption.
  - For KV offlaoding deployments, `KVConnectorBase_V1.has_pending_block_frees()` can also stop preemption from choosing a victim when connector frees are still pending.

### Fix

The fix is to introduce a `SchedulerOutput.has_structured_output_spec_decode` flag orthogonal to the existing `SchedulerOutput.pending_structured_output_tokens`.
- `pending_structured_output_tokens` indicates whether sampling should be deferred for a structured outputs request `p`, which is needed whenever an earlier batch with `p` is stil inflight. It doesn't care about whether spec decode is used, `p` should be deferred regardless.
- `has_structured_output_spec_decode` indicates whether there's a structured output request `p` expecting draft tokens. It doesn't care whether `p` is deferred or not. Draft tokens should be retrieve regardless.

Note this introduces a sychronization between scheduler-side and worker-side on the non-deferred sampling path but this is required for correctness. Pipeline bubbles due to `take_draft_token_ids` is a known issue and being worked on in #64531. I hope to land this correctness fix first before finalizing #64531.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Fit the GLM-5.2 TP1-PCP4 eval's KV cache on B200
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes the `(B200) [Nightly] LM Eval PCP` failure on `GLM-5.2-NVFP4-TP1-PCP4-EP` by lowering its `--max-num-batched-tokens` from 32768 to 16384. This is a config-only change. The eval has failed every nightly since #56492 made the extensible KV cache the default ([latest failure](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/101018#01a1bf1e-2a62-451e-b3df-6d67e5f33ad0)).

## Claims

- `GLM-5.2-NVFP4-TP1-PCP4-EP` starts and passes again. Before this change it got 0 KV cache blocks and failed startup with `No available memory for the cache blocks`.
- The pass criteria are unchanged: threshold, tolerance and question count stay the same.

## Validation

I ran this on 4×B300, with each GPU's free memory capped to a B200's by a process that pins the difference (vLLM's initial free memory was 175.62 GiB here, vs 175.85 GiB on CI). The profiling numbers matched CI exactly: 130.62 GiB weights, 27.91 GiB torch peak.

| `--max-num-batched-tokens` | Held for activations | KV cache after warmup | GSM8K (threshold 0.90) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 32768 (main) | 26.79 GiB | 0 blocks → startup `ValueError` (same as CI) | — |
| 16384 (this PR) | 13.4 GiB | 6,314 blocks (17.95 GiB) | 0.9378 |

```bash
cd tests
pytest -s -v evals/gsm8k/test_gsm8k_correctness.py \
  --config-list-file=configs/models-pcp.txt -k "TP1-PCP4-EP and not DCP4"
```

I have not run this on B200 hardware; the B200 numbers above come from the memory cap.

## Details

**Root cause.** After warmup, the extensible KV cache keeps free the profiled transient peak plus a margin of `0.75 × peak` (`KV_CACHE_MARGIN_FRACTION`), so 1.75× the peak in total. At 32,768 batched tokens the peak is 26.79 GiB, which means about 47 GiB must stay free. Only 38.95 GiB is free after the 130.6 GiB model on a B200, so no KV cache fits:

```
Memory after warmup: 38.95 GiB free, 0.19 GiB committed to the KV cache, 26.79 GiB kept for transient
activations; 0 KV cache blocks (0.0 GiB) fit within the requested 178.35 GiB.
```

Before #56492, classic sizing at `gpu_memory_utilization=0.92` gave this config 4.82 GiB of KV cache, and it passed.

**Timeline.** It looks like the eval broke on Nov 6, but it actually broke when #56492 landed:
- Builds 99098–100339 failed on this config with an illegal memory access at startup, from unaligned extensible KV cache segments.
- #65554 fixed that crash, and this sizing failure showed up next.
- Automatic sharding hides this from the dashboard, because before Nov 6 the config ran in the other shard.

**Tradeoff.** This config now prefills in batches of at most 16,384 tokens. `GLM-5.2-NVFP4-TP2-PCP2-EP` still covers 32,768-token PCP batches in the same job: it holds back 14.4 GiB and passes. The DCP4 config already caps batched tokens at 4,096 for the same kind of headroom reason.

**Open question for extensible KV cache owners.** The 1.75× rule is a lot more conservative than classic sizing for large-activation configs like this one. If that's not intended, the right fix is in the sizing, and this PR is only a stopgap. #66197 (autotune peak) and #55828 (per-process memory) don't change this case: here the held-back amount is the profiled peak itself.

**Duplicate check.** No open PR touches this config or the PCP eval on NVIDIA. #66321/#66322 add ROCm mirrors with separate configs.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Preserve batch invariance in Triton unified attention on SM100
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Preserve batch invariance in Triton unified attention by excluding batch-invariant execution from the SM100-family large-head tuning path. The regression compares each causal query alone with the same query inside a multi-query block.

Related tracking issue: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/27433 (this does not close the broader tracker).

## Claims

- Restores exact attention-output agreement for the tested BF16 head-size-256 SM100 configurations when batch invariance is enabled.
- Leaves batch-invariant-off tuning unchanged; head-size-512 cases are regression controls.
- Public Gemma3 checks show exact selected-token log-probability agreement after the fix. Generated-token divergence was not observed in those model checks; full speculative-serving correctness is not claimed.

## Validation

Tested on NVIDIA B200; the new test requires SM100 and is skipped in upstream CI.

| Check | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| New kernel regression | 10 failures / 10 passes | 20 passes |
| Gemma3 decode vs teacher-prefill selected log-probabilities, eager | Different for all 3 contexts | Exact for all 3 |
| Same model check, FULL CUDA graphs | Different for all 3 contexts | Exact for all 3 |
| Gemma3 solo vs batch selected log-probabilities, FULL | Different for all 3 contexts | Exact for all 3 |

The ten failing baseline cases all have head size 256; the ten head-size-512 controls pass before and after. Test parameters: context lengths 32/65/1024/1025/2048 and query lengths 2/8; every query row is compared, with `rtol=atol=0`.

Model check: `google/gemma-3-1b-it`, BF16, TP1, Model Runner V2, `TRITON_ATTN`, prompt lengths 65/512/1025, 16 greedy output tokens per prompt. Patched eager and FULL CUDA graph outputs also match exactly.

Three warmed offline batches per arm, each containing all three prompts (mean [min, max] milliseconds):

| Execution | Before | After | Mean change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Eager | 657.0 [654.4, 660.2] | 637.6 [634.9, 641.8] | -3.0% |
| FULL | 188.4 [188.2, 188.7] | 196.8 [196.0, 197.7] | +4.5% |

These short, sequential-arm measurements characterize only this workload; they do not establish a general speedup or online serving performance.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands</summary>

Reproduce in a configured B200 checkout with its vLLM/test dependencies installed:

```bash
# Run this against both source revisions, keeping the new test in both.
PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest -v \
  tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_unified_attention.py \
  -k batch_invariant_multi_query_matches_single_query
```

</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, `unified_attention` always launches the 2D kernel, so decode and speculative verification share one kernel. On SM100 with head size 256, however, the large-head tuning path is gated on `max_seqlen_q > 1`. It switches multi-query calls to `BLOCK_M=32`, `TILE_SIZE=128`, 8 warps and 2 stages, while single-query decode keeps the defaults (`BLOCK_M=16`, `TILE_SIZE=32`). The different tile and warp configuration changes the floating-point reduction order, so a token's attention output depends on how many other query tokens are in the same call. That breaks the batch-invariance guarantee: a token verified alongside speculative proposals does not match the same token decoded alone.

**Fix.** Skip the tuned path when batch invariance is enabled, so every call uses the same launch configuration regardless of query length. Behavior with batch invariance disabled is unchanged, and other GPUs and head sizes never take this path.

**Tradeoff.** With batch invariance enabled, SM100 head-size-256 prefill and verification no longer use the large-head tuning (+4.5% latency with FULL CUDA graphs in the Gemma3 check above). This matches existing batch-invariant behavior, which already trades throughput for determinism, e.g. by disabling the 3D decode kernel.

**Test.** `test_batch_invariant_multi_query_matches_single_query` runs each query alone at its causal KV length and compares the result bit-exactly with a single call over all queries (`rtol=0, atol=0`). Exact equality is the property under test, not a tolerance choice. Head-size-512 cases serve as controls because they never take the tuned path.

**AI assistance.** AI tools (OpenAI Codex and Cursor) were used to develop the fix, the regression test and the validation scripts. All changed lines were reviewed by the submitter.

commits.pr_title: [Attention] Sync FA with upstream (54b044c8)
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Companion to [vllm-project/flash-attention#213](https://github.com/vllm-project/flash-attention/pull/213). That PR syncs the 72 Dao-AILab commits from `ce088ab9` through `54b044c8`, with FA3 (`hopper/`) frozen.

#213 has landed; `GIT_TAG` now pins its merge commit `af5422c5c24e2f464d394295c5b2f659f9332217` on `vllm-project/flash-attention`.

## Changes

- `cmake/external_projects/vllm_flash_attn.cmake`: repository and `GIT_TAG` point at the candidate (temporary).
- `vllm/vllm_flash_attn/flash_attn_interface.py`: upstream's `_flash_attn_fwd` now returns 5 values (it adds `o_lo`), so the FA4 call unpacks `out, softmax_lse, _, _, _`. `compile_flash_attn_varlen_func_from_specs` also builds its compile-only `out` spec 32-byte aligned when `head_dim_v == 512`, which upstream's `_flash_attn_fwd` now requires. Without that, Gemma 4's SM90 hd512 FA4 warmup fails on Hopper (found and fixed by @simon-veitner-redhat).

- Remove vLLM's FA4 hd256 special-casing. It existed for the fork's dedicated hd256 kernel; upstream's unified forward serves head_size=256 without those restrictions.
  - `fa_utils.py`: drop `FA4_HD256_PAGE_SIZE`, `uses_fa4_hd256_kernel`, `_fa4_hd256_fallback_reason`, and the `supports_fa4_hd256` / `requires_softcap` / `kv_cache_block_size` parameters. hd256 no longer falls back to FA2 for sinks, softcap, quantized KV, block sizes that are not a multiple of 128, mm_prefix, R-SWA, DCP, or windowed encoders.
  - `flash_attn.py`: drop the 128-token block-size advertisement, page-aligned `max_seqlen_k`, block-table trimming, and the forced `num_splits=1`. hd256 now uses the default block size (16), and FA4 warmup also compiles the split variant.
  - **Known slowdown:** hd256 with softcap (Gemma 2) under a forced `FLASH_ATTN` backend now runs on FA4 instead of FA2. Accuracy is unchanged, but it is about 1.5x slower end to end (B300, GSM8K pass: ~35 s vs ~21 s). B300 picks FlashInfer for Gemma 2 by default, so only forced `FLASH_ATTN` is affected.
  - Callers that never opted in (`mm_encoder_attention`, MLA prefill, TurboQuant/UltraQuant prefill) also resolve FA4 instead of FA2 for 256/256 on Blackwell.
  - `sparse_mla_attention.py`, `triton_flash_attn.py`, `flash_attn_diffkv.py`, `docs/design/attention_backends.md`: remove the hd256 leftovers.
- Tests: delete the four hd256 selector tests; `test_fa4_hd256_paged_call_shape` becomes `test_fa4_hd256_varlen_with_paged_kv` (block 16/128, softcap, sliding window, `num_splits` 1/4, unaligned `max_seqlen_k`, wide block table); `test_mm_prefix_kv_cache_path` adds head_size=256.
- `tests/kernels/attention/test_flash_attn_interface.py`: the mocked `_flash_attn_fwd` returns 5 values, matching upstream.
- `tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py`: **widens the bf16 tolerance for `masked_mha_chunked_context` from `rtol=0.01` to `rtol=0.02`** (see the note below).

## Note: sparse MLA chunked-context tolerance

`test_sparse_backend_prefill_correctness[*-masked_mha_chunked_context]` is flaky across seeds on `main` as well. The test fixes `torch.manual_seed(42)`, and the new hd256 kernel happens to fail at that seed.

- **Cause:** the chunked-context path rounds the running context partial to bf16 at every chunk merge, and again in the final suffix merge. With outputs around 128, `rtol=atol=0.01` allows only about 1.3 bf16 ULP. Keeping the running partial in fp32 makes the case pass, which isolates the error to these extra roundings rather than the kernel.
- **Seed sweep:** `torch.manual_seed` patched across seeds 0–299, on B300. "Old" is `main` with stock FA4 (the dedicated hd256 kernel); "new" is this PR with #213.

| shape | kernel | seeds failing at rtol 0.01 | at 0.015 | at 0.02 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| deepseek 192/128 | old / new | 21 / 21 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| glm5 256/256 | old / new | 5 / 10 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| glm53 256/256 (NoPE) | old / new | 1 / 6 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |

- **New vs old kernel:** the new hd256 kernel exceeds 1 ULP on more seeds than the old dedicated kernel, at about the same rate as FA4's standard kernel on deepseek. The maximum error is the same 1.5 for both, and without chunked context both stay within 1 ULP.
- **Chosen tolerance:** `rtol=0.02` keeps at least 1.06 of margin on every seed. A follow-up could keep the running partial in fp32 instead. That would roughly double the partial buffer's memory and changes shared MLA code, so it is not done here.

## Validation

vLLM `main` plus this branch, precompiled install. `vllm/vllm_flash_attn/cute` was replaced with #213's `flash_attn/cute`, with imports rewritten as the CMake install does. Environment: vLLM's pinned deps (nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.8.0, apache-tvm-ffi 0.1.11). This PR does not change those pins.

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_flash_attn.py tests/kernels/attention/test_mixed_causal_attn.py \
  tests/kernels/attention/test_attention_selector.py tests/v1/attention/test_mm_prefix.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_mla_prefill_quant_output.py tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py \
  tests/models/inkling/test_fa4_rel_attention.py tests/models/inkling/test_fa4_warmup.py \
  tests/kernels/attention/test_cascade_flash_attn.py
```

- **H100 80GB HBM3:** 1002 passed, 68 failed, 794 skipped. All 68 failures are `fa_version=3` cases of `test_varlen_with_paged_kv`, mostly with FP8 Q. They run the unchanged FA3 binary from the precompiled wheel, which this sync does not touch.
- **B300 SXM6 AC:** 908 passed, 1 failed, 955 skipped. The failure is `test_sparse_backend_prefill_correctness[glm53_flash_nope_hd256_v256-auto-masked_mha_chunked_context]`. It passes with the stock FA4. One element out of 8,388,608 differs by 1.5 at magnitude ~128 (1.17% relative, against `rtol=atol=0.01`), about 1.5 bf16 ULP.
  - This is the hd256 forward, which moved from the fork's dedicated kernel to upstream's unified one.
  - Measured directly against an fp32 reference, the unified kernel's LSE error is 3–24× lower than the dedicated kernel's. Output error is at bf16 rounding level for both: max relative 1.6e-3 vs 1.2e-3, where bf16 half-ULP is 3.9e-3.
  - So the tolerance in this test is right at the edge.
- **hd256 perf on B300 (`benchmarks/attention_benchmarks`, FLASH_ATTN, block size 128):** compared with fork `main`'s dedicated hd256 kernel, the unified kernel is faster in all 39 cases. Prefill is 1.03–1.42× and decode/mixed is 1.5–9.3×, even with `num_splits=1`. With SplitKV enabled (this PR), small decode batches gain further (`8q1s4k`: 4.8× vs 2.5× at 16/2 heads; 6.0× vs 4.7× at 32/4). One case is slightly worse: `16q4s4k` at 32/4, 5.2× vs 6.2×. Full table in [vllm-project/flash-attention#213](https://github.com/vllm-project/flash-attention/pull/213).

**hd256 removal validation (B300, vLLM branch head, precompiled install + #213 FA4 overlay).**

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_flash_attn.py -k fa4_hd256
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_attention_selector.py tests/v1/attention/test_mm_prefix.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py tests/models/inkling/test_fa4_warmup.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_jit_warmup_migration.py tests/model_executor/test_jit_warmup.py \
  tests/kernels/attention/test_mixed_causal_attn.py tests/v1/attention/test_mla_prefill_quant_output.py
```

- 64 passed; 695 passed, 1 failed (the same `glm53…hd256…chunked_context` single-element miss described above; with the widened tolerance, all 12 `test_sparse_backend_prefill_correctness` cases pass). `test_mm_prefix_kv_cache_path[sliding_256]` passes.
- Direct FA4 probes, max abs error vs fp32 reference, hd256 vs hd128 in the same 2–4e-3 range: pages 16–256, unaligned lengths, wide block tables, sinks, softcap, sliding window, splits, unpaged windowed encoder; FP8 Q/K/V with descales 1.45–1.55e-2 (hd128: 1.33–1.72e-2).
- Perf tradeoff: hd256 now defaults to block 16 instead of 128. On B300, block 128 is 1.19–1.47× faster for hd256 prefill/extend and 1.0–1.3× for decode (hd128 sees 1.02–1.25×), since FA4 uses TMA paged KV only when the page equals the 128-token tile. A follow-up PR will prefer 128-token blocks for FA4 in general rather than special-casing hd256.

The full FA2 C++ build is left to CI on this PR.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Drop sparse MLA metadata host sync; use persistent AITER for gfx950 long BF16 prefills
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

This PR removes the host `synchronize()` that `ROCMAiterMLASparseMetadataBuilder.build()` runs after each `get_mla_metadata_v1` rebuild. That sync fails `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` inside `execute_model`. The PR also stops gfx950 from sending long pure BF16 prefills to AITER's nonpersistent ASM decode kernels, which give wrong results that change from run to run at 32, 64 and 128 heads. That kernel is what made `large_q_pure_prefill-auto-ROCMAiterMLA` flaky, on main and once the sync was gone.

The persistent-metadata block keeps its pre-existing `gpu_sync_allowed()` `seq_lens[:num_reqs].cpu()` read. Because of the routing change, gfx950 long pure BF16 prefill steps now enter that block and so now hit that allowed read; before this PR they skipped it. Removing that read is follow-up work, not part of this PR.

This is part of the work to re-enable `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` on AMD CI, which #61939 dropped from `docker/Dockerfile.rocm`. It replaces the `gpu_sync_allowed()` wrap that #64176 used for this site, following `njhill`'s review there (fix the syncs instead of allowing them). Related PRs: #66397, #66398, #66399; #64176 turns the check back on and depends on all of them.

## Claims

- **Post-metadata `synchronize()` removed, with no allow-wrap in its place.** The pre-existing allowed `seq_lens` read in the same block remains (see Overview). Before this PR, the removed sync (`rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py:726` on main) failed these AMD jobs with the check on: in [build 97758](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/97758), `mi300 v1-attention shard 1/3`, `mi355 dpx v1-attention shard 2/4`, `mi355 lm-eval deepseek-v3-2-tp` and `-dp`; in [amd-ci 15532](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15532), `mi300 v1-attention shard 1` and `shard 2`, `mi355 dpx v1-attention shard 1` and `shard 2`, `mi355 lm-eval deepseek-v3-2-tp` and `-dp`.
- **Flaky test fixed.** `test_sparse_backend_decode_correctness[deepseek-1.0-1.0-64-1-auto-large_q_pure_prefill-ROCMAiterMLA]` now gives the same result on every run on gfx950. Pristine main: 3/60 in-process failures. This PR: 0/60.
- **Correct at every head count on gfx950.** For long pure BF16 prefills, AITER's persistent kernel was deterministic and within 0.006 of an fp32 reference at 16-128 heads. The nonpersistent kernels main uses are nondeterministic with errors up to 0.036 (32 heads), 0.092 (64) and 0.173 (128), and at 48/80/96/112 heads AITER has no nonpersistent kernel at all (table in Details).
- **Faster only at 128 heads.** At 128 heads the persistent kernel is about 1.2-1.5x faster per layer (kernel table below). At fewer heads it is slower: at TP4 DeepSeek-V3.2 (32 heads per rank) TTFT on an 8192-token prompt rises by 17.0 ms (+2.6%) (see Model eval). Each such step also pays one `get_mla_metadata_v1` launch (1.3 ms at 8192 tokens) and the allowed `seq_lens` read.
- **No metadata that AITER would ignore.** The builder skips persistent metadata and its `seq_lens` read when AITER would not use the persistent kernel for the batch (gfx950, BF16, 16 heads, at least 32 tokens). With AITER 0.1.28.post1 on MI350X (gfx950), 16 heads and BF16, output with and without metadata was bit-identical at 32, 64, 512 and 4096 tokens over 3 reruns each. At 31 tokens, below the threshold, the two outputs differ (max 2.4e-4) because a different kernel runs; that is the positive control. At TP8 DeepSeek-V3.2 the kernel trace now matches main exactly. This covers batches of 32 or more tokens; a 16-head long-context prefill with fewer than 32 new tokens (prefix hit or short chunked tail) still builds metadata and runs the persistent kernel, which was deterministic in the study.
- **gfx942 unchanged.** Long BF16 prefills there still skip persistent metadata and take the Triton fallback.

## Validation

All local runs: MI350X (gfx950), ROCm torch 2.13, amd-aiter 0.1.28.post1, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`. Commands 1 and 2 were re-run on 2deae9c3dd and gave the same results: 155 passed / 108 skipped, and 30/30. The other runs used 36442e9f. Both earlier commits differ from 14f9dc450e only in docstrings. The command 1, unit-test and 25-run fresh-process counts were rerun at the head with the metadata-skip change and the head-count test parametrization.

| Check | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Sparse MLA CI set with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` (command 1) | 2 failed (`test_rocm_fused_v32_dense_prefill_matches_mqa[auto]`, `[fp8]`: `GPU<->CPU sync detected` at the removed line), 141 passed, 108 skipped | 181 passed, 108 skipped, 0 failed (the extra passes come from the gfx942 and head-count parametrizations and the 2 metadata-skip tests) |
| `kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_sparse_metadata_sync.py` (this PR's test file; main column runs it against main's source) | 2 failed (`test_sparse_persistent_metadata_recomputes_without_host_sync`, `test_sparse_metadata_workload_length_dtype_matrix[prefill-long-auto-False]`), 40 passed | 68 passed |
| `large_q_pure_prefill-auto-ROCMAiterMLA`, repeated in one process | 3/60 failed (mismatched elements: 11464, 11640, 217); separately 5/30 | 0/60; also 0/30 with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` (command 2) |
| Same test, one fresh process per run | 3/12 failed | 0/40, and 0/20 with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`; 0/25 with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` after the metadata-skip change |
| Integration stack (`sync-fix/rocm-enable-gpu-sync-check`: this fix at 36442e9f plus #66397/#66398/#66399 and the Dockerfile change), `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, command 1 | - | 155 passed, 108 skipped, no syncs |

The unit matrix is the deterministic guard for the routing change. The e2e `large_q_pure_prefill` test only catches the bad kernel about 5-25% of the time on main (3/60, 5/30, 3/12), so it is a weak regression signal on its own.

<details>
<summary>Extra stress runs and commands</summary>

Independent reviewer stress of the target test: 0/50 fresh-process failures and 100/100 in-process passes (one reviewer), and another 100/100 in-process (a second reviewer). A full run of the `ROCMAiterMLA` cases of `test_sparse_backend_decode_correctness`, repeated 10 times, gave 108 passed / 108 skipped every time.

```bash
# 1. CI set (from tests/)
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error pytest -q \
  v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py \
  kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_sparse_metadata_sync.py \
  -k "rocm or sparse_persistent or sink"

# 2. Target test, repeated in one process (REPEAT_N from a small local repeat plugin)
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error REPEAT_N=30 pytest -q -p repeat_plugin \
  "v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py::test_sparse_backend_decode_correctness[deepseek-1.0-1.0-64-1-auto-large_q_pure_prefill-ROCMAiterMLA]"
```
</details>

**Kernel timings** (MI350X, BF16, CUDA events, mean over 20 iterations, us). The AITER-only repro and timing script uses random inputs, a fresh zeroed output and a device sync around every call. "Differing reruns" counts reruns whose output differed from the first run.

| shape (reqs x tokens, topk, heads) | nonpersistent (old gfx950 path) | persistent (this PR) | Triton | differing reruns: nonpersistent / persistent |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2x256, 128, 128 | 83.5 | 71.1 | 385 | 20-49/49 (two runs) / 0/49 |
| 1x4096, 2048, 128 | 2958 | 2005 | 36272 | 5/19 / 0/19 |
| 4x2048, 2048, 128 | 4236 | 3017 | 49728 | 7/19 / 0/19 |
| 1x4096, 2048, 64 | 1214 | 1163 | 18264 | 0/19 / 0/19 |

The extra `get_mla_metadata_v1` launch runs once per step and all layers share it: 113 us at 512 tokens, 1.3 ms at 8192, 2.6 ms at 16384.

**Model eval and end-to-end latency.** DeepSeek-V3.2 on 8x MI350X (gfx950), amd-aiter 0.1.28.post1, main (fd0c471b3a) vs this PR with the same arguments. The changed path is reached only by pure-prefill steps whose longest prefill exceeds topk=2048, with BF16 KV. So the runs use `num_concurrent=1`, 25-shot GSM8K (all 1319 prompts are 3151-5087 tokens) and `--max-num-batched-tokens 32768`, so each prompt prefills in one step. MTP is off and CUDA graphs are on (FULL_DECODE_ONLY). Dispatch was checked with rocprofv3 on an 8192-token request.

- TP4 (32 heads per rank): the PR runs the persistent `mla_a16w16_qh64_qseqlen1_gqaratio64_v3_ps` plus `kn_mla_reduce_v1_ps` instead of main's nonpersistent `mla_a16w16_qh16_m16x4_n32x1`. That is 155.0 vs 144.0 ms over 61 layers, plus 2.7 ms of reduce and a 1.44 ms metadata launch.
- TP8 (16 heads per rank): AITER falls back to nonpersistent split-KV (`mla_dec_stage1_bf16_a16w16_subQ16_mqa16`) on both sides. With the metadata skip, kernel names and counts match main on all 8 ranks. Without it, the only extra work was one ignored metadata launch (1.44 ms) and one `seq_lens` copy.

TP4 (32 heads per rank):

| TP4 | GSM8K flexible | GSM8K strict | TTFT med (ms) | TPOT med (ms) | E2E med (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 0.9545 | 0.9553 | 667.2 | 13.45 | 2372.8 |
| this PR | 0.9560 | 0.9568 | 684.2 | 13.46 | 2393.8 |

TP8 (16 heads per rank):

| TP8 | GSM8K flexible | GSM8K strict | TTFT (ms) | TPOT (ms) | E2E (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 0.9545 | 0.9545 | 493.4 ± 1.8 | 12.87 | 2127.7 ± 2.0 |
| this PR without the metadata skip | - | - | 493.8 ± 2.1 | 12.87 | 2127.6 ± 1.5 |
| this PR | 0.9522 | 0.9530 | 493.0 ± 2.8 | 12.86 | 2126.4 ± 0.9 |

- Latency is from `vllm bench serve` with random 8192 in / 128 out, concurrency 1, 50 prompts plus 5 warmups, `--ignore-eos`.
  - TP4: 3 repeats per side on each of two GPU sets, alternating, then swapped (300 requests per side). The result is +17.0 ms TTFT (+2.6%) and +21.1 ms E2E (+0.9%), and it holds with the GPU sets swapped.
  - TP8: 4 fresh-server rounds in rotated order, 3 repeats each. Values are the mean ± sd of the per-round medians. The 1.44 ms metadata launch is below restart-to-restart noise.
- Accuracy: GSM8K standard error is about ±0.006. Paired McNemar tests give p = 0.79 (TP4) and p = 0.61 / 0.79 (TP8, flexible/strict). At TP8 main and this PR run identical kernels and still share only 579/1319 identical generations, so differences of this size come from run-to-run nondeterminism.
- The CI-parity eval (`configs/models-mi355-deepseek-v32-tp.txt`, TP4 + MTP + eager, 5-shot) has not been rerun; its 0.6k-1.6k token prompts and high concurrency probably never reach the changed path.

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MLA=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 \
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2 --tensor-parallel-size {4,8} --enable-expert-parallel \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE --moe-backend aiter \
  --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16 --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching
lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 25 \
  --model_args model=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=1,tokenized_requests=False
vllm bench serve --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2 --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 128 --max-concurrency 1 \
  --num-prompts 50 --num-warmups 5 --ignore-eos
```

**Not validated locally:**
- gfx942/MI300. gfx942 routing is unchanged, but its FP8-KV persistent path also loses the sync. CI's mi300 v1-attention shards cover that path, but not MTP + CUDA graphs at 200k context (#47404's setup, see below).
- MTP with DeepSeek-V3.2 at model level. TP4/TP8 runs above use CUDA graphs (FULL_DECODE_ONLY) without MTP. Kernel-level graph replay after an unsynced metadata rebuild was checked (see "Why the sync can go").

## Details

**Why the sync can go.** With `fast_mode=True`, `get_mla_metadata_v1` dispatches to AITER's `get_mla_metadata_v1_2_device`. That function launches one device kernel on `aiter::getCurrentHIPStream()`, and AITER's `compile_ops` sets that stream to torch's current stream before each call. Nothing is staged through host memory, there is no `hipMemcpy`, and the function owns no buffers. The decode kernel, whether eager or captured in a graph and replayed, runs later on the same stream and reads the metadata on the device, so stream order already puts the write before the read. The block also already starts with a blocking `seq_lens.cpu()`, so the removed sync only waited for the single metadata kernel launched after it. The dense `rocm_aiter_mla` builder already rebuilds the same metadata every step without a sync. Two investigation experiments back this up:
- Outputs stayed bit-identical with no sync even with a 5M-cycle `torch.cuda._sleep` queued before the metadata kernel, which lets the host run far ahead of the GPU.
- Direct graph-replay race test (AITER persistent FP8 MLA decode, 128 heads, 256 tokens, same metadata arguments as vLLM): capture a CUDA graph, then per iteration rewrite `kv_indptr` to a different config, queue a 20M-cycle sleep, rebuild metadata with no host sync and replay. Same stream: 0/50 mismatches against per-config eager references. Positive control replaying on an unordered side stream: 49/50 mismatches.

**Concern about #47404.** The sync came from #47404, which reported that it removed a fault on 8x MI300X (gfx942), TP8, `ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE` + MTP + CUDA graphs, FP8 KV, `max_model_len=200000`. That PR gave no root cause beyond "graph replay could observe stale metadata". The kernel-level graph-replay test above shows that same-stream ordering covers that case, but it ran on gfx950 with one GPU and no model. #47404's exact configuration has not been rerun with this PR; all local hardware is gfx950. Plan before leaving draft: rerun that configuration (100+ requests) on MI300X with this PR, through AMD CI or a reviewer with MI300X access, or get confirmation from the #47404 author; if none is possible, the regression risk stays open and is called out to reviewers.

**Why the flaky test failed.** `large_q_pure_prefill` (2x256 tokens, topk 128, BF16 KV) never reached the sync. On main, `_is_long_bf16_prefill()` skipped persistent metadata for long pure BF16 prefills on every architecture, but only gfx942 sent those batches to Triton. On gfx950 they fell through to AITER's nonpersistent `mla_dec_stage1_bf16_a16w16_subQ128_mqa128`. With bit-identical inputs and device syncs around every call, that kernel returns different rows from run to run. Against an fp32 reference its max error is 0.12-0.21, compared with 0.0053 for the persistent kernel. So the kernel computes wrong values; this is not an ordering race. Syncs placed before or after stage 1, `AMD_SERIALIZE_KERNEL=3` and `HIP_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` all still reproduce the failure. It reproduces with AITER alone and the newest AITER nightly ships the same binary; reported as ROCm/aiter#7631. The 32- and 64-head nonpersistent kernels are also nondeterministic, mostly on multi-request shapes (the single-request 1x4096 64-head row above showed 0/19). The sink/LSE path still calls the nonpersistent kernel. This PR leaves it alone, and #66454 handles it separately (see Tradeoffs).

Determinism by head count (AITER only, sparse layout: one entry per query token, ragged top-k indices, page_size 1; same inputs every run, NaN-poisoned output, with and without an L2 flush; 50-400 runs per config at 2x256 to 1x8192 tokens; error is the max against an fp32 reference):

| padded heads | nonpersistent kernel | nondeterministic configs | max err | persistent nondeterministic configs | max err |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 16 | `subQ16_mqa16` | 0/18 | 0.0059 | 0/12 (AITER runs the nonpersistent kernel) | 0.0051 |
| 32 | `qh16_m16x4_n32x1` | 4/22 | 0.036 | 0/22 | 0.0052 |
| 64 | `qh64_qseqlen1_gqaratio64_v3` | 5/18 | 0.092 | 0/18 | 0.0057 |
| 128 | `subQ128_mqa128` | 12/18 | 0.173 | 0/18 | 0.0060 |
| 48/80/96/112 | none (`cannot get heuristic kernel`) | - | - | 0/4 each | ≤0.0059 |

**The fix.** `_is_long_bf16_prefill` is renamed to `_use_triton_long_bf16_prefill` and now checks `on_gfx942()` first. The builder and `_forward_mla` share this helper, so they cannot disagree about which path a batch takes. The import of `on_gfx942` stays lazy so that the tests' monkeypatch still applies. The gfx942-only Triton routing for these prefills was in place before this PR. The all-architecture skip of persistent metadata came from #49263 (cc `tjtanaa`), which gave no reason for it. Routing gfx950 to Triton instead would be deterministic, but 5-18x slower (table above).

**Tradeoffs and limitations.**
- On gfx950, long pure BF16 prefill steps now enter the persistent block. So they now also pay the existing `gpu_sync_allowed()` `seq_lens.cpu()` read and one metadata launch per step. At TP4 DeepSeek-V3.2 (32 heads per rank) the persistent kernel is also slower than the nonpersistent one, so 8192-token TTFT rises by 17 ms (+2.6%). That is the cost of not running the 32-head nonpersistent kernel, which gives wrong values (see the determinism table).
- The one exception is 16-head BF16 batches of at least `AITER_MLA_DECODE_PERSISTENT_MAX_BATCH` tokens (32 by default). There, AITER's `mla_decode_fwd` ignores `work_meta_data` and runs the nonpersistent split-KV kernel. The builder asks AITER's own `_use_persistent_mla_decode` and skips both the metadata and the read in that case, so these steps do what main did. The check also covers decode and mixed batches, where main built metadata that AITER then dropped. If the installed AITER lacks that function, the builder keeps the old behavior.
- Layers with sinks or `use_aiter_sparse_mla` set `_use_persistent_metadata=False`. This PR does not change sink layers. On gfx950, BF16 sink layers still run AITER's nonpersistent `mla_decode_fwd_lse`, which ROCm/aiter#7631 also covers (`return_lse=True`). #66454 routes those layers to Triton until #7631 is fixed. The two PRs are independent, and either can land first.
- `metadata_key` does not include `max_split_per_batch`. That was already true before this PR; it is only flagged for follow-up.

**Tests.**
- `test_sparse_persistent_metadata_syncs_only_after_recompute` is renamed to `test_sparse_persistent_metadata_recomputes_without_host_sync` and now asserts that no sync happens.
- `test_sparse_metadata_workload_length_dtype_matrix` is parametrized over `(on_gfx942, num_heads)` in `(True, 128), (False, 32), (False, 64), (False, 128)`: only gfx942 may skip persistent metadata for long BF16 prefills. Against main's source `[prefill-long-auto-False]` failed (before the head parametrization), and a 128-only rule fails the 32- and 64-head cases, so this is the deterministic guard for the routing change.
- `test_build_skips_metadata_aiter_ignores[-1|0]` uses AITER's real predicate with gfx950 and its default threshold patched in. At the threshold, it checks that the builder launches no `get_mla_metadata_v1`, enters no `gpu_sync_allowed()` read and returns `work_meta_data=None`. One token below the threshold, it checks that metadata is still built. Without the source change, `[0]` fails.
- The previously flaky `test_sparse_backend_decode_correctness[...large_q_pure_prefill-ROCMAiterMLA]` runs in the AMD v1-attention CI shards, but it is a low-rate catcher (see Validation).

**Duplicate check.** Searched open PRs for `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK`, `gpu_sync_allowed`, "sync rocm" and sparse MLA metadata keywords. #64176 is the submitter's own predecessor, and this PR replaces its approach for this site. #66003 removes a different allowed sync, in the `ROCM_AITER_FA` builder, so the two do not overlap. #62946 targets the INT4 RHT-signs site, which is handled in #66399. No open PR touches this site.

**AI assistance.** AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to investigate, implement and validate this change. The human submitter is responsible for the change.
